# Minimap

“Let's get started, shall we?”

This article is a stub. You can help the Deadlock Wiki by expanding it.

The **Minimap** is a simplified depiction of the map from above. It is used in a match to navigate the map, see the location of teammates, and to see any enemy players within the player's or players' teammates line of sight.

In spectator mode, the Minimap has The Archmother side as North and The Hidden King side as South by default.

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Reveal Duration
- 1.2 Things that reveal the player to enemies on the minimap
- 1.3 Things that will not reveal the player to enemies on the minimap
- 2 Invisibility
- 3 Hero Interactions
- 4 Item Interactions

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

### Reveal Duration

[edit | edit source]

When revealed on the minimap, the player remains visible for approximately **2 seconds** after the revealing action ends.

### Things that reveal the player to enemies on the minimap

[edit | edit source]

- Shooting enemy Troopers.
- Shooting at enemy defensive structures (Guardians, Walkers, Shrines, Patron).

- This includes shooting them from an angle where the structure cannot see or shoot back. The act of shooting at the structure is what causes the player to appear on the enemy minimap, regardless of location.
- Being targeted or shot at by enemy defensive structures.
- Being within an enemy hero's line of sight, within approximately **50–60 meters**. Note that this is based on the heroes' line of sight specifically, not the enemy player's. A straight line between the centers of both heroes must be free of vision blockers.

- Leaning around a corner only exposes the hero's torso and does not count as line of sight, meaning neither hero will reveal the other on the minimap while one is leaning.

A visual of the maximum range that the player will reveal enemy heroes (that are in line of sight) on the minimap

- Being very near an enemy hero (just under light melee range), even if they are facing away. The hero will be revealed even if they are not visible on screen, as long as there are no vision blockers.

Bebop cannot see McGinnis on his minimap, and McGinnis would not be able to see Bebop on the minimap (were she looking at him).

- Carrying the Urn.
- Activating  Mirage's  Djinn's Mark on an enemy.

### Things that will not reveal the player to enemies on the minimap

[edit | edit source]

- Standing near enemy Troopers while they are not shooting at or targeting the player.
- Using abilities or items on enemy Troopers or heroes.
- Being targeted or shot at by an enemy hero from beyond approximately **50–60 meters**, even if they have line of sight on the player.
- Enemy Troopers riding a zipline near or above the player.
- Shooting at summons such as  Graves'  Ghouls or  Deadheads or deployables such as  McGinnis'  Mini Turrets.
- Being hit by summons or deployable abilities (Though it will make the player's portrait appear in the HUD for the hero who summoned the unit).

## Invisibility

[edit | edit source]

Invisibility (from  Veil Walker,  Shadow Weave, or  Haze's  Smoke Bomb) prevents revealing under the following rules:

- Breaking invisibility requires: using abilities, shooting, or being within proximity of an enemy hero with line of sight (walls block this).
- **Exception:** Haze's Smoke Bomb allows using items and abilities without breaking invisibility or revealing her on the minimap.
- Buildings and objectives do not break invisibility or reveal the player.
- Graves'  Ghouls will chase invisible players but will not explode on them.

## Hero Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Calico cannot be revealed on the minimap while using  Ava, even if shot by troopers, guardians, or walkers.
- Mirage's  Djinn's Mark will reveal invisible enemies on the minimap when activated.

## Item Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Stalker provides wall-hack vision of the target but does not reveal them on the minimap for the team.

## Direct Relations

[edit | edit source]

Ms. Shelly Fisher

### Shelly Fisher

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Shelly Fisher

**Shelly Fisher** is Bebop's creator. She is a widowed junkyard attendant who built Bebop, thus relying on Bebop for support in paying for her treatment. Johann Geist Jr. is her doctor.[1]

### The Geists

[edit | edit source]

#### Johann Geist

[edit | edit source]

Born in 1805 and dying in 1880, **Johann Geist** was a German painter and the husband of Jeanne Geist.[1] 50 years before the Ritual, the Paradox Organisation stole one of Johann's paintings.[2][3][4]

#### Walter Geist

[edit | edit source]

The son of Johann and Lady Geist. Born in 1850 and died sometime in the 1900s.[1]

#### Johann Geist (Jr.)

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Johann Geist Jr.

The grandson of Lady Geist and the doctor of Shelly Fisher.[1]

### The Arroyos

[edit | edit source]

Main article: The Arroyo's

#### Carlos Arroyo

[edit | edit source]

A Community organiser in Spanish Harlem. Possibly looking to run for mayor.[5]

#### Sophia Arroyo

[edit | edit source]

A young woman who studies under Dynamo in Columbia University. She works with Wraith to fund her tuition.[5]

#### Manny Arroyo

[edit | edit source]

Sophia's younger brother. He's a fan of Kelvin and his books.[6][7]

### Marla

[edit | edit source]

Marla is Dynamo's wife. They have been married for 31 years.[8] She bakes Dynamo key lime pies despite him being incapable of eating them and made enough for Dynamo to share with his team if they win.[9][10]

### Agent Marlowe

[edit | edit source]

Main article: OSIC

Marlowe is an OSIC Agent.[11][12] He also is a friend of Venator.[13]

### The Troubadour

[edit | edit source]

Main article: The Troubadour

**"The Troubadour"** is the name given by media for a serial killer who commited a killing spree in a town in central Illinois. He was confronted by the town's sheriff, Holliday, but he managed to escape by turning into a murder of crows and flying away, although Holliday still has been looking for him. Both she and the New York Oracle speculate that The Troubadour is flying from Champaign–Urbana to New York.[11]

### Nashala Dion

[edit | edit source]

**Nashala Dion** is a Djinn ambassador, who has employed Mirage to work as her bodyguard and companion. Mirage enjoys Nashala's company, but he also finds her "impulsive, short-sighted" decisions "frustrating".[14] She (and Mirage) are currently in New York attempting to arrange a deal so the Djinn can buy a portion of Wyoming.

### Cadence and the Requiem Boys

[edit | edit source]

*Main article: Cadence*

**Cadence and the Requiem Boys** are a band, with **Cadence** as their lead vocalist, that produced the single "Paying the Price". The song has concerned some parents over its mention and "glorification" of human sacrifice.[15]

### John Hathorne

[edit | edit source]

*Wikipedia article: John Hathorne*

**John Hathorne** was a magistrate and merchant who had a key role as a judge in the Salem Witch Trials during the 1600s which persecuted people believed to be witches. One of the people sentenced to death by him was Vindicta, who now holds a grudge against his descendants after she was brought back into reality from the first maelstrom.

### John Hathorne (Jr.)

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Friends of Humanity

A "controversial speaker" and descendant of the original John Hathorne currently in New York.[16]

He is a member of the neo inquisition political group "Friends of Humanity" which has rallied for the US to stop sending aid to the Outer Planes.

There was an assassination attempt on his life.[17]

### Ettrick

[edit | edit source]

Ettrick is an old friend of  Kelvin, who the latter has not seen since his return from the expedition. Ettrick held ambitions for an unknown goal, which drove Kelvin to push him away.[18] Ettrick was "rather rude" and "caused a scene" at Kelvin's fundraiser, according to  Lady Geist.[19]

### The Adversary

[edit | edit source]

Main article: The Deep

The Adversary is a creature from an Outer Plane that stalks the Deep. It is described as "dark and predatory" and "a genocidal force of nature". Viscous says that if the Adversary isn't stopped, "he will come for everything".[20]

### Captain Murphy

[edit | edit source]

Captain Murphy is  Holliday's contact in the New York Police Department. She uses his help to track down The Troubadour.[11] Yamato threatens to kill Murphy should Holliday not "play her part" during the ritual.[21]

### Allie Kinkaid

[edit | edit source]

A reporter from The New York Oracle. She's writing an interview with Seven.[11][22]

### Hank

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Jezebel's

Hank is the owner of Jezebel's Billard Hall. He's the boss and close friend of Infernus and is friends with  Lady Geist. [1]

### Bryce

[edit | edit source]

The brother of Paige, Bryce was a rebellious teen who wanted to use his family's bibliomancy for his own desires. A few years before the ritual, he was kicked out of his family's house for unknown reasons, and has been missing since. Paige is participating in the ritual to find out what happened to Bryce and to restore her family.[23]

Bryce used to hang out with Vyper[24] and is described by Paige as a "curmudgeon".[25]  Venator believes Bryce is beyond saving, expressing remorse that Paige has "thrown away her life to save someone who doesn't deserve it".[26][27] Haze believes Paige would be happier if she lets her brother go.[28]

### Molly Molenzo

[edit | edit source]

A convict at Rikers, Molly was shanked by  Vyper using a toothbrush-mattress spring combo.[29] The stabbing of Molly was heard about by  Wraith, who mentions that she "isn't friends" with Molly.[30]  Yamato wants to speak to Molly about something important.[31]

### Cinnamon

[edit | edit source]

Cinnamon is a performer at a place called *Pole Palace*.  Vyper calls her a "librarian" and mistakes  Paige for her.[32]

### Blockhead Lenny

[edit | edit source]

One of the sideshows at Coney Island, Lenny is friends and coworkers with Celeste. He's implied to be stubborn,[33] and is possibly the friend of Celeste who sold part of their soul to cover a gambling debt.[34][35] Lenny once got beaten by Lash in the Bear Pit.[36] Part of Lenny's act includes knife throwing.[37]

### Keruba the Mermaid, Chickenwing and Ted

[edit | edit source]

Friends of Celeste who work alongside her at Coney Island's sideshow.[34]

## Mentioned Characters

[edit | edit source]

Characters mentioned in passing by The New York Oracle.

### Harry Houdini

[edit | edit source]

*Wikipedia article: Harry Houdini*

Rumoured to still be alive and possibly evaded death itself.[38]

### Michael Assan

[edit | edit source]

Wrote "A Memoir by Incubus to the Stars" which spent 3 weeks on the top of The New York Oracle's best seller list.[39]

### Madame Lapri

[edit | edit source]

A relationships expert who wrote a column in The New York Oracle about love potions.[40]

### Nathan Vice

[edit | edit source]

Centre for the Knickerbockers, had their legs broken by The Curiosity Shop shopkeep for one of the items.[41]

### Rodgers and Hammerstein

[edit | edit source]

*Wikipedia article: Rodgers and Hammerstein*

A duo of theater writers who produced the musical South Pacific, which had its tickets scalped and resold for 1/8 of a soul.[42]

### Eric Clansky

[edit | edit source]

A man standing trial for a botched exorcism.[43]

### Miser Heart

[edit | edit source]

The person accusing Mr Clansky in court for causing the spirit inhuman pain and suffering.

### George Frederick Cooke

[edit | edit source]

*Wikipedia article: George Frederick Cooke*

Still performing on stage but as a headless ghost.[44]

### Mittens and Peppermint

[edit | edit source]

A cat familiar duo running a cat café in Soho.[45]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Allie Kinkaid's name may be a reference to Alex Kincaide, a journalist character in Valve's *Counter-Strike*: *Global Offensive*.
- Chickenwing and Ted were both teased 3 months before Celeste's backstory was revealed, in a joke post by developer Hopoo.[46]

[edit | edit source]

Trapper wants to impress Cinnamon.[47]

“

Sometimes, the small things make all the difference.

**Mirage** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. He is agile and uses powerful wind-based abilities for disruption. By throwing out Fire Scarabs and transforming into a Dust Devil, Mirage can damage, lift up, steal life and elude his targets while applying Djinn's Mark to enemies to enhance his attacks. When the time is right, he can Travel across the map in an instant to assist his allies, hunt down weak foes and take care of objectives.

An emissary of the Djinn ambassador Nashala Dion, Mirage is a diplomatic bodyguard who is charged with carrying and protecting the djinn's vessel.

Mirage was added to the roster on September 26, 2024.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Mirage/Lore** for more story content.*

“

The Djinn are one of the more curious groups of people in the modern world.  Possessing great power in controlled doses, Djinn are incapable of maintaining corporeal form for longer than 48 minutes without resting within a vessel.  As a result, most Djinn employ human bodyguards for transport, protection, and companionship.

Mirage is one such bodyguard.  Employed by Djinn ambassador Nashala Dion, Mirage is in New York on a diplomatic mission.  It's the hope of the Djinn that they can negotiate with the US government for a sale of part of Wyoming so that they can build a sovereign nation for their people.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Mirage is the third hero to be introduced through an update, following Shiv and Viscous.
- Nashala has an unused human-sized model in the game files.
- Mirage is one of two heroes to share a name with a Counter-Strike map, the other being Infernus' old name, Inferno.
- Mirage's model was updated in the 2024-12-06 Update.
- Mirage carries Nashala in the bottle in his hand. In his previous model, it used to be attached to his chest.
- Mirage's first official model wasn't shipped in the game files until he was officially released. However, the model was leaked a couple weeks earlier by an updated portrait art.
- Mirage's pre-release model was based on Paradox's model with a modified McGinnis head.
- Mirage has never had a hotdog before.[2]
- "Dreaming of Wyoming in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Mirage in the Hideout.

The Djinn are one of the more curious groups of people in the modern world.  Possessing great power in controlled doses, Djinn are incapable of maintaining corporeal form for longer than 48 minutes without resting within a vessel.  As a result, most Djinn employ human bodyguards for transport, protection, and companionship.

Mirage is one such bodyguard.  Employed by Djinn ambassador Nashala Dion, Mirage is in New York on a diplomatic mission.  It's the hope of the Djinn that they can negotiate with the US government for a sale of part of Wyoming so that they can build a sovereign nation for their people.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Mirage's wish (which is moreso Nashala's wish) is to help Nashala buy a piece of Wyoming to turn into a home for the Djinn.[1][2][3]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Mirage has worked for Nashala for a few years, after she approached him with a job offer.[4]

Mirage and Nashala haven't had the chance to do much sightseeing, but are looking forward to seeing various locales,[5][6] such as New Jersey and Columbia University.[7][8]

While in New York, Mirage and Nashala are guests at the Baroness Hotel.[9][10]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Mirage views the Djinn as "people". He thinks some are "fascinating", but some others are "assholes".[11]

Mirage likes to play bowling and calls it "the sport of kings". He learned it in England.[12]

Most characters respect Mirage due to his conviction for the Djinn.[13]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Mirage has visited New York's Public Library.[6]

Mirage wants to try eating a hot dog.[14]

Mirage dislikes the Paradox Organisation, since they keep trying to steal Nashala for the Paradox Museum.[15][16][17]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Nashala Dion

[edit | edit source]

Mirage is deeply loyal to Nashala and the Djinn's plight,[18][19] willing to die and kill for her.[20]

While Mirage enjoys Nashala's company, he can find her frustrating to work with when she makes "impulsive, short-sighted" decisions (such as asking him to trust  Seven).[21]

Mirage fights with Nashala by his side since he believes that's the safest place for her.[22]

Anyone who wants to talk to Nashala must have Mirage's approval,[23] and anyone trying to steal or harm Nashala will be killed by Mirage.[24][25]

Mirage believes that Nashala doesn't need a wish to pull off the deal,[26] since the Djinn can offer America money and power.[27]

### The Doorman

[edit | edit source]

Mirage and The Doorman are familiar with each other from the Baroness Hotel. Both are apologetic when killing each other.[28][29]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Mirage asks  Dynamo for a tour of Columbia University.[30]
- Mirage calls out Abrams and Calico for valuing money over duty.[31][32]
- Mirage shows no mercy towards monsters like  Drifter,[33]  Lady Geist,[34] and  Seven.[35]
- Mina, Silver and  Vyper want Mirage to "stop yelling about the Djinn".[36][37][38]

- Billy likens Mirage to 'people who think having a dog is like having a personality' and also wants him to stop talking about the Djinn.[39]
- Paige admires Mirage and says he "stepped out of every romance novel ever written".[40][41] She thinks Mirage is better than  Shiv.[42]
- Lady Geist,  Mina and  Seven respect Mirage for "knowing his place".[43][44][45]
- Paradox and  Vyper think Mirage needs to "lighten up".[46][47]
- Billy and  Drifter think Mirage is handsome.[48][49]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

### Neon Prime - Sandeep

[edit | edit source]

In *Neon Prime**,* Mirage was named **Sandeep**.

“

Everyone has a plan until they're grabbed by a mole man.

— Krill

**Mo & Krill** are Heroes in *Deadlock*. Fighting together, they are a disruptive and mobile pair that can burrow around the battlefield and leave their enemies in ruins. Beginning encounters with Burrow can let Mo & Krill pop out on unsuspecting enemies, attacking them with Scorn to damage and Sand Blast to disarm them. With the support of their team, they can Combo one targeted enemy to pin their target in place while the rest of their allies unleash their attacks.

Members of The Tunnel Rats, Mo & Krill are smugglers and illicit traders who make the underground of New York their home. Rival gangs that try to exploit these tunnel systems for their own gain will rapidly discover how protective and deadly this pair of smugglers can be.

## Backstory

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Krill is the only one of the duo who has voice lines. However, Mo's grunts can be heard during Combo.
- Krill's model was inherited from *Neon Prime*.
- In a now removed voice line,  McGinnis referred to Krill as a rat.[1]
- Both Mo and Krills' heads are capable of being headshot, but Mo's head has 20% headshot damage reduction.
- Mo & Krill have the highest base health in the game at 900hp with no boons and 3110hp at max boons.
- Mo & Krill have a unique conversation with Holliday in the files titled "Troubadour", hinting that they will appear in Holliday's visual novel.[2]
- "Relaxing in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Mo & Krill in the Hideout.

He does the digging, I do the talking. We tried it the other way but, it didn't work.

— Krill

Mo and Krill are members of The Tunnel Rats, a group that help facilitate illicit trade and commerce between the boroughs thanks to a network of underground tunnels.  But while most denizens of the New York underworld respect the work The Rats do, every once in a while a gang tries to exploit the tunnel system for personal vendettas...that's when Mo and Krill step in and remind the city what happens to those who disrespect their hospitality.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Mo & Krill's motivation in the ritual is to achieve the respect and glory they believe is owed to them.[1][2]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Mo is a mole man.[3][4] Krill's species is currently unknown, but he has monkey-like characteristics. He also seems to have fur.[5]

Mo and Krill have been forced to live in the margins of society.[6] It's unknown how the two met, but Krill mentions that their friendship was forged from "respect and certain death".[7]

Mo's full name is Maurice.[8] Krill and Pocket also calls him "Momo".[9][10] Mo is learning pottery and wants to audit pottery classes at Columbia University,[11][12] although it's implied that he doesn't know to use a pottery wheel.[13]

Krill is an author and is writing a memoir about his and Mo's adventures, which currently has 31 chapters.[14][11]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Mo & Krill value their independence.[15] They're friends with  Wraith and used to do business with the Mendoza Syndicate.[16][17][18]

Mo & Krill don't like the Friends of Humanity.[19] They also don't like it when their names get mixed up.[20]

Mo knows how to speak, but doesn't speak around people he's unfamiliar with.[21][22]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Mo stinks.[23][24] Krill has bathed in sewer sludge.[25]

Mo & Krill have smuggled a wide variety of objects in the New York tunnels, such as jewels, fine art and Ixian trinkets.[26] They also offer information for a "reasonable price",[27] and accept money to dig new underground tunnels.[28] Notable items of value they've sold include trinkets from  Kelvin's Ixia expedition and knock-offs of Mina's dresses.[29][30] Krill knows someone looking to sell a first edition copy of "*Don Quixote".*[31]

Mo & Krill don't pay taxes.[32]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Pocket

[edit | edit source]

Mo & Krill protected Pocket after Pocket's assassination attempt, and they regard each other as family.[33][34][35] They love each other.[36]

### Wraith

[edit | edit source]

Mo & Krill are in Wraith's weekly poker game and owe money to her.[37] If they're on the same team, Wraith may say she called a favor to have them fighting on her side.[17] They regard each other as friends.[16][38]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Mo & Krill watch and bet on  Bebop's fights in the Bear Pit.[39] They know Ms. Shelly and have tried to help her.[40]
- Mo & Krill are friends with Infernus and have offered to help him prevent Jezebel's from closing.[41]
- Mo & Krill are friends with Abrams.[42][43] Abrams owes Mo & Krill $50.[37]
- Krill compares Apollo to a teenage version of Lash.[44]
- Krill is impressed by  Lady Geist's ward and Holliday's revolver.[45][46]
- Krill has read  Kelvin's books and found them "riveting".[14]
- Krill liked Sinclair's stage show and pities them for their fate.[47]
- Mo wants to cry if he kills Celeste. [48]
- Lady Geist shows contempt and disgust towards Mo & Krill.[49][50]
- Yamato wants to turn Mo into a coat and Krill into a hat.[51]
- Seven hides in Mo & Krill's subway tunnels, without their permission.[52]
- Mendoza was a "good" client of Mo & Krill.[18]
- Vyper really likes Mo & Krill.[53] They don't like her.[54]
- Paige likes Mo & Krill and wants to be their friend.[55] Krill mentions that they once planned to start a book club together.[56]
- While trapped inside the Baroness, The Doorman attempts to split Mo & Krill up from each other. He tells Mo that Krill is dead weight and that he should kill him, and he tells Krill that Mo is keeping him down and would be better off if he never met Krill.[57]  Seven also tells Mo that Krill is holding him back.[58]

- When killing the Doorman, Krill reassures Mo that he'd never betray him.[59]
- Kelvin,[7] Paige,[60] Vindicta[61] respect Mo & Krill's friendship.
- Dynamo,[62] Holliday,[63] Ivy[64] and Lash[65] don't know which of the duo is Mo or Krill.
- The Shopkeeper and Rem want to hug Mo.[66][67]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

In a removed voice line,  McGinnis referred to Krill as a rat.[68]

**Monster Rounds** is a Tier 1  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **800**.

It is a component of  Cultist Sacrifice.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Monster Rounds applies additional damage to Non-Player Characters. This includes Troopers, lane structures like Guardians, Walkers, neutral entities such as Denizen, and the Patron.
- It does apply additional damage against  Graves'  Ghouls, but *not* against  McGinnis'  Mini Turrets.

# Move Speed

**Move Speed** is a stat that heroes start with and can obtain more through items. Move speed dictates how many meters per second the hero will move.

*See also: Movement Slow*

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Sprint Speed
- 1.2 Slide
- 2 Calculation

- 2.1 Calculating Move Speed
- 2.2 Sprint Speed Stacking
- 2.3 Combined Example
- 3 Base Move and Sprint Speed
- 4 Sources

- 4.1 Move Speed
- 4.2 Sprint Speed
- 4.3 Map Spawns

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Heroes will accelerate up to base movement speed velocity from a standstill. Move Speed bonuses from items and abilities stack diminishingly, meaning adding more speed provides progressively less value.

While firing, a hero's movement speed is reduced to 75% of its normal value (a 25% slow), which can be mitigated by  Fleetfoot. There is no penalty while zooming in. While crouched, all heroes have 4.8 m/s crouch speed not affected by the movement speed penalty, except for  Grey Talon and  Warden, whose movement speed penalty while firing applies while crouched, becoming 4.4 m/s.

Move Speed is an important stat in overall movement, as it affects how quickly one can reach their destination.

Some heroes have Spirit Scaling affecting their Move Speed and Sprint Speed. See "Base Move and Sprint Speed" table below.

### Sprint Speed

[edit | edit source]

**Sprint Speed** is a related stat that is conditionally added to a hero's move speed when a hero is out of combat for five seconds, and persists until entering combat or zooming in. Zooming in while sprinting resets the player's speed back to base move speed.

If the hero has more than **2.5m/s Sprint Speed,** the rest of the sprint speed will be added to the hero's movement at a rate of **0.6m/s** as the player moves. While capped at the hero's Sprint Speed stat, sprinting will continue building up past its current max value, meaning bonuses applied while sprinting (e.g. Healing Rite) will instantly increase current Move Speed. Sliding, taking damage, getting Stunned, Immobilized, Displaced or Slept, using a Zipline, or stopping movement input will reset this counter.

### Slide

[edit | edit source]

Heroes moving above 8.9 m/s can slide on a flat horizontal surface by crouching.

## Calculation

[edit | edit source]

### Calculating Move Speed

[edit | edit source]

While items often display movement speed bonuses as flat values (e.g., +2 m/s), multiple sources of move speed do not simply add together. Instead, they stack **multiplicatively** using a similar formula to resistance, meaning each additional source provides diminishing returns.

To find your effective move speed bonus, use the following formula:

Effective Move Bonus=11×(1−(1−B111)×(1−B211)…)

Where B₁, B₂, etc. are individual move speed bonuses.

Then calculate your total speed:

Total Speed=Base Move Speed+Effective Move Bonus+Base Sprint Speed+Sprint Bonus1+Sprint Bonus2…

**Example:**
If you have two sources of move speed, one providing **+2 m/s** and another providing **+3 m/s**:

1. Divide each bonus by 11: ≈0.182 and ≈0.273.
1. Subtract from 1: (1 - 0.182) = **0.818** and (1 - 0.273) = **0.727**.
1. Multiply the remainders: 0.818 × 0.727 = **0.595**.
1. Subtract from 1: 1 - 0.595 = **0.405**.
1. Multiply by 11: 0.405 × 11 = **4.46 m/s** (or **4.5 m/s** rounded).
1. Your Effective Move Bonus is **4.5 m/s** (not 5 m/s).

If your hero has 6.5 base move speed, 1.6 base sprint speed, and no sprint bonuses:
6.5+4.5+1.6=𝟏𝟐.𝟔 m/s

### Sprint Speed Stacking

[edit | edit source]

Unlike move speed, sprint speed stacks **additively** with no diminishing returns. If you have base 1.6 sprint speed and get items with +2 and +5 sprint speed, you simply have 8.6 sprint speed.

Total Sprint=Base Sprint+Bonus1+Bonus2…

### Combined Example

[edit | edit source]

A hero with:

- 6.4 base move speed
- 1.6 base sprint speed
- +2 and +3 move speed bonuses
- +2 and +1.5 sprint speed bonuses

**Step 1: Calculate Move Speed**
11×(1−(1−211)×(1−311))=4.5 m/s effective
6.4+4.5=𝟏𝟎.𝟗 m/s

**Step 2: Calculate Sprint Speed**
1.6+2+1.5=𝟓.𝟏 m/s

**Step 3: Add Together**
10.9+5.1=𝟏𝟔.𝟎 m/s

# Movement Slow

**Movement Slow** is a status effect applied by many items and abilities that slows move speed by a percentage.

Movement Slow cannot reduce a player's speed below 2.0 m/s in-game (or 80 hammer units per second).

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Calculation

- 2.1 Stacking Multiple Slows
- 2.2 Calculating Final Speed
- 2.3 Movement Slow Resist
- 3 Sources

- 3.1 Heroes
- 3.2 Items
- 3.3 Movement Slow Resist

- 3.3.1 Heroes
- 3.3.2 Items

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- The displayed speed in-game in m/s is rounded to the nearest decimal for all numbers under 10 m/s.

## Calculation

[edit | edit source]

### Stacking Multiple Slows

[edit | edit source]

While abilities and items display slow percentages (e.g., 30%), multiple sources of movement slow do not simply add together. Instead, they stack **multiplicatively**.

To find your total slow percentage, use the following formula:

Total Slow=1−(1−Slow1)×(1−Slow2)×...

**Example:**
If you are affected by two slows, one providing **30%** and another providing **25%**:

1. Convert percentages to decimals: 0.30 and 0.25.
1. Subtract from 1: (1 - 0.30) = **0.70** and (1 - 0.25) = **0.75**.
1. Multiply the remainders: 0.70 × 0.75 = **0.525**.
1. Subtract from 1: 1 - 0.525 = **0.475**.
1. Your Total Slow is **47.5%**.

### Calculating Final Speed

[edit | edit source]

Once you have the total slow percentage, apply it to your speed. However, movement slow is calculated using 2.0 m/s as a floor - you cannot be slowed below this speed.

Slowed Speed=((Current Speed−2)×(1−Total Slow))+2

**Example:**
If you are moving at **10 m/s** and have **50%** total slow:

1. Subtract the floor: 10 - 2 = **8**.
1. Apply the slow: 8 × (1 - 0.50) = 8 × 0.50 = **4**.
1. Add the floor back: 4 + 2 = **6 m/s**.

### Movement Slow Resist

[edit | edit source]

Movement Slow Resist reduces the final calculated slow percentage. Multiple sources of Movement Slow Resist stack **additively** (not multiplicatively).

Actual Slow=Total Slow×(1−Resist1−Resist2−...)

**Example:**
If you have **47.5%** total slow and **30%** Movement Slow Resist:
47.5%×(1−0.30)=47.5%×0.70=𝟑𝟑.𝟐𝟓%

# Movement

“Alright buddy, give 'em hell!”

This page is under construction. To avoid edit conflicts, please consult the edit history and the talk page.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Movement is a concept that encompasses traversing the map. In a broad sense, it is important for positioning, map rotations, ganking, and pushing, while from a mechanical point of view, it is the specific actions to escape, chase, initiate fights, or otherwise catch enemies out of position.

Several heroes and items have specific movement tech that cannot be executed otherwise.

Distances and speeds are displayed in-game by meters (m) and meters per second (m/s). As the game built on the Source 2 Engine, internal measurements are calculated by hammer units (hu), where 1 hammer unit can be approximated to 1 inch. Therefore, 1 hu is roughly equal to and represents .0254 m.

There is no fall damage in *Deadlock*.

## Basic Movement

[edit | edit source]

### Controls

[edit | edit source]

The character is controlled using movement keys (by default: W, A, S, and D). Pressing the jump key (by default: Space) makes the character jump, and holding it near a ledge allows the character to mantle (by default: Space). The crouch key (default: Ctrl) causes the character to crouch or slide if they have enough speed  (8.9 m/s or 350 hu/s) or are on an inclined surface, such as stairs. Additionally, the dash key (default: Shift) enables the character to perform a dash both on the ground and in the air. Heroes have differing move speeds and dash speeds.

Main articles: Move Speed, Movement Slow

Heroes have differing base moving and sprinting speeds. Sprinting will activate on its own, which occurs after a hero is out of combat for five seconds and persists until entering combat or zooming in. Zooming in while sprinting resets the player's speed back to base move speed. Most heroes can obtain sprint through items, but several start with it initially.

### Air Jump

[edit | edit source]

Jumping while midair functions like a double jump, allowing the player to reach rooftops or get over tall walls. This consumes one stamina.

- At the start of each game, you are only permitted one Air Jump per jump. This can be expanded to two with the  Vitality Item  Stamina Mastery.

### Wall Jump

[edit | edit source]

Pressing Space next to a wall will cause the character to perform a Wall Jump, which does not consume stamina. You can Wall Jump multiple times per jump, but each Wall Jump after the first one costs 0.5 stamina and incurs a fatigue that reduces the height of successive jumps. This fatigue recovers non-linearly[*Citation needed*] over the course of 1.25 seconds and recovers completely upon landing. Using a heavy melee while airborne will also incur fatigue.

### Air Dash

[edit | edit source]

Dashing midair can be done similarly to a grounded dash. A dash performed in the air is called an Air Dash, and consumes the same amount of stamina as a grounded dash. You can Air Dash only once per jump, but this limit can be expanded to two with the  Vitality Item  Stamina Mastery.

### Dash Jump

[edit | edit source]

A *Dash jump* is a fast long jump, which can be performed as an additive input during a dash during a set timing window and which costs 1 stamina, for a total of 2 stamina. The timing of a *dash jump* is visualized by the stamina bars under your crosshair turning blue while *dashing.* While the crosshair is blue, the player can press jump to *dash jump*.

### Down Dash

[edit | edit source]

Double tapping crouch midair performs a down dash, allowing the player to return to the ground quickly. This consumes 0.5[1] stamina. You can Down Dash only once per jump. This can be expanded to two with the  Vitality Item  Stamina Mastery.

### Mantle

[edit | edit source]

Mantling is the act of climbing a nearby ledge. If a player holds the crouch key (default: Ctrl) while mantling, they will slide after climbing up, which is called a Mantle Glide.

If the player is hit by a melee attack while mantling, they will get an 80% Movement Slow, which will taper down to 20% over 2s.

### Stamina

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Stamina

Stamina management is an important aspect of player movement.

## Map features

[edit | edit source]

There are multiple elements on the map that let players move uniquely.

### Jump Pads

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Jump pad

Jump Pads are small vents that push heroes through the air after standing on them.

### Ropes

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Ropes

Ropes dangle from the roofs of buildings or inside buildings, allowing heroes to access rooftops or additional floors, and facilitate vertical traversal.

### Teleporter

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Teleporter

There are multiple pairs of teleporters throughout the map that can be entered to quickly traverse left and right across the map.

### Ziplines

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Ziplines

Ziplines are the most prominent method of traversal, as the heroes spawn riding the lines. They connect the opposing bases together and facilitate fights.

## Advanced Movement

[edit | edit source]

As a physics based game, several principles in the real world are also modeled in-game. However, quirks with the game engine allow unique movement options that are not readily apparent.

### Melee Jump

[edit | edit source]

Melee jumping is the technique of using a heavy melee timed with a *Wall Jump* to go up without double jumping, thus saving a Stamina bar.

### Corner Boost

[edit | edit source]

*Corner boosting* is a technique that exploits the game's wall jump mechanics to achieve greater vertical velocity than a standard wall jump. The effect is believed to occur due to the following implementation behavior:

- **Velocity Reset on Wall Jump Initiation** – When a wall jump is performed, the game first sets the character's velocity to a fixed absolute value.
- **Collision Normal Calculation** – The game determines the direction of the jump by using the normal vector of the character's collision capsule at the nearest point of contact with the wall.
- **Upward-Angled Normals on Corners** – Because the collision capsule is rounded, the normal vector near a corner can point diagonally upward or downward rather than purely sideways. When the normal is angled upward, the resulting velocity is applied at a steeper angle, leading to increased upward momentum.

#### Visual Comparison

[edit | edit source]

- Normal Wall Jump – Final velocity is directed primarily sideways, following a standard wall jump.
- Corner Boost – Final velocity is angled higher due to the upward-tilting normal, resulting in a stronger ascent.

| Corner Boost Normal Wall Jump | ##### Key  [edit | edit source]         - ■ Light Blue: Collision capsule - ■ Red: Absolute velocity - ■ Green: Sideways velocity - ■ Orange: Wall push - ■ Purple: Final velocity |

### Dropdown Corner Boost

[edit | edit source]

Same as *Corner Boost*, *Dropdown Corner Boost* can be done on any edge in the game. To perform it, drop down from an edge and wall jump to gain extra height without using stamina.

### Dash Jump Cancel

[edit | edit source]

Dash Jump Canceling is a technique that allows for Jumping immediately after a Dash without performing a Dash Jump. After performing a Dash for a short duration it is possible to spend 1 Stamina to perform a Dash Jump. Casting an ability during the Dash Jump window will immediately cancel it. This can then be followed up with a normal Jump. When done correctly a Dash Jump Cancel can be used to travel further than a Dash.

Only some abilities provide a benefit when used to Dash Jump Cancel. Abilities with long cast time or abilities that slow movement during cast provide almost no benefit.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

Prior to the April 17, 2025 update, players could use Heavy Melee Cancel to maintain momentum from a Heavy Melee attack. However, the update significantly reduced the momentum preservation, making the technique nearly ineffective for movement purposes.

# Municipal Coven

“

The city owes you boys in the Municipal Coven a lot.

— Shopkeeper

The Municipal Coven makes sure the streets of New York stay safe and tidy.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

The New York Municipal Coven works as the primary caretakers of New York.

During the festive season, the Municipal Coven were looking for volunteers to spend time with stray familiars in their Soho shelter. [1]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

Trapper is a Municipal Coven employee. His duties include building Spirit Urns, luring giant rats, and capturing invasive species from other realms.[2] Staff were given the option to work on Maelstrom day, which Trapper volunteered to do.[3]

Trapper believes the Municipal Coven needs to be respected more.[4]

Holliday[5] and the Shopkeeper[6] respect what the Municipal Coven does for the city.

The Municipal Coven seems to accept donations.[7]

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

*Deadlock's* main musical identity since the Six New Heroes update displays elements of Trip hop, a genre popularized in the 1990s and defined as a psychedelic fusion of hip-hop and electronica, with influences from jazz and other styles.

## Composer

[edit | edit source]

The music for *Deadlock* was composed by a member of the development team who wishes to remain anonymous for the time being. In a private email, Valve composer Mike Morasky explained that the composer will likely take credit at a future date and confirmed it was not him or "anyone else you might normally guess."[1] Morasky had also previously denied his involvement publicly on X (formerly Twitter).[2]

**Mystic Burst** is a Tier 1  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **800**.

It is a component of  Tankbuster.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Update history
- 3 Gallery
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- **Mystic Burst** uses Charge-Up
- Heroes with Spirit Lifesteal will heal from Mystic Burst's passive effect triggering.
- A small lightning shock visual is applied to the enemy hero when it is hit by Mystic Burst's passive effect.
- When the target is hit with **spirit damage**, the damage value which is compared against the triggering threshold is the base damage value prior to any increases or decreases from damage amp, damage reduction, spirit resistance, and spirit resistance reduction.

- Damage amp and spirit resist reduction will not help you in achieving the damage threshold to trigger the passive.
- Damage reduction and the target's spirit resistance will not prevent the passive from triggering when it otherwise would.
- While the tooltip only specifies 'Abilities', only Spirit Damage will activate Mystic Burst. Abilities dealing weapon damage - such as  Venator's  Consecrating Grenade or  Viscous'  Puddle Punch - will not activate Mystic Burst.
- The additional damage, and the ability which triggered the additional damage, are applied to the target as separate instances of damage. The additional damage from Mystic Burst is dealt after the original spell damage.

**Mystic Reverb** is a Tier 4  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **6,400**.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Notable Interactions
- 3 Known Bugs
- 4 Update history
- 5 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- The debuff effect is applied to the first enemy hit. If the imbued ability is an area-of-effect and it hits multiple heroes, only one enemy will receive the debuff.

## Notable Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Pure Damage does not trigger the reverb or use the imbued lifesteal. If an ability has bonus Pure Damage like the blessed stakes of  Venator's  Ira Domini, it will not be used to calculate the damage of the reverb.

- Mystic Reverb can be imbued on  Lady Geist's  Soul Exchange, but it has no effect.
- Abilities that only deal Melee Damage such as  Viscous'  Puddle Punch or  Calico's  Leaping Slash can be imbued, though they cannot activate the reverb or use the imbued lifesteal.

- Spirit Snatch applies after the melee damage and does not allow melee abilities to use Mystic Reverb.
- However,  Quicksilver Reload and  Mercurial Magnum grant bonus spirit damage to the imbued ability's first hit of weapon or spirit damage and can activate the debuff.
- The debuff can store damage from items like  Quicksilver Reload or  Tankbuster on the imbued ability.
- The 50% extra damage is calculated based on pre-mitigation damage, but can then still be mitigated by spirit resistance when it triggers.

## Known Bugs

[edit | edit source]

- The initial reverb damage can kill the primary target, but is sometimes non-lethal to secondary targets, leaving them with at least 1 hp remaining. This seems to mainly happen against Target Dummies in Sandbox

**Mystic Shot** is a Tier 2  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **1,600**.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

The item provides a passive effect that creates an additional bullet when the hero shoots their weapon, and the additional bullet will mimic the bullets created by the current weapon. The Mystic Shot bullet appears as a glowing purple version of the hero's regular bullets.

For most weapons, the Mystic bullet can follow the trajectory of any bullet, which can make it fly off-center for weapons with significant spread over time, such as  McGinnis'. The exception are spreadshot weapons such as  Abrams' and  Shiv's, in which the Mystic pellet is always fired at the center of the crosshair.

For explosive alternate fire weapons such as  Viscous' and  Yamato's, the Mystic bullet will appear the same but cannot deal damage in an area. Instead, it only deals the Spirit damage to the closest enemy to impact.

The Mystic bullet hits before regular bullets. So for example,  Bullet Resist Shredder's effect is applied first and amplifies the weapon damage, but  Crippling Headshot's Spirit Resist reduction is applied after and does not amplify Mystic Shot's spirit damage.

The additional Mystic bullet cannot deal critical (headshot) damage and is not affect by  Ricochet.

A Mystic bullet is immune to evasion.

**Mystic Vulnerability** is a Tier 2  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **1,600**.

It is a component of  Escalating Exposure.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Update history
- 3 Gallery
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Unlike  Escalating Exposure, Mystic Vulnerability does not cause a stacking effect. Hitting the enemy with additional spirit damage after the debuff has been applied will only refresh the duration.
- Escalating Exposure's debuff takes priority over the Mystic Vulnerability debuff, so if two players have each of these items they will not stack together on the same target.

# Neon Prime lore

“Welcome to Fracture: City of a Thousand Cities!”

This page has content related to *Neon Prime*, an earlier version of *Deadlock*.

The following text describes the full lore of *Neon Prime.*

It was extracted from the section labeled *OLD LORE* in the file *citadel_dev_english.txt*, found in the *Deadlock* localization folders. The file has since been removed.

## Welcome to Fracture: City of a Thousand Cities™

Welcome, intergalactic tourists, to Fracture -- City of a Thousand Cities™! As you walk down our many historic streets and enjoy our countless parks and museums, you might think that Fracture is just like any other bustling planet-capital in the galaxy. And in most ways, it is. But in other tiny but important ways, Fracture is one of a kind. As a for-instance: When you got off the shuttle at Bowl o’ Blood Spaceport, you probably got robbed. But not for all your money -- around 34% -- and you were given a receipt. Then you started yelling for the police, and you got robbed again. That’s because Fracture is run by criminals. Now, that might sound like a bad idea, but if you read on, you’ll find out it’s actually one of the best darn ways a city could be run -- fine-tuned from centuries of illegality.

### Humble Beginnings

While it might not look like it now, Fracture used to be a prison planet. That’s right! Prisoners were sent here to slave in the deep fissures of the planet’s crust, toiling away in the marrow mines until they died. That’s when the Founding Families realized -- "Hold on a minute. We’re alone on a planet here! We can do anything we want." That’s when Fracture truly began -- its days as a prison mining planet behind it, and its bright future as an anything-goes prison utopia lying tantalizingly ahead. The galaxy still dumped off its law-defying folks, of course. And it was still pretty much impossible to escape the planet. But you could otherwise do mostly anything you wanted, unless you wanted to leave. Now, are the good folks of Fracture ashamed of their lawless past? Far from it! In fact, many folks here claim they can trace their lineage back to one of the twelve Founding Families!

### The Founding Families

So who are the Founding Families, and why are they so important? Well, in the beginning, Fracture didn’t have a fancy mayor, or even laws or a way to enforce them. It wasn’t pretty. But what it had in abundance, being a prison planet, was criminals and walls. So the biggest prison gangs cut up the city into the Twelve Boroughs, with each family responsible for maintaining law and order. And crazily enough, it worked! If you wanted to commit a crime, you needed a permit for it, or there’d be hell to pay. Left to govern themselves, the criminals ended up being more organized and motivated than a government ever could’ve been. Sure, there was still crime -- but no surprises. You might be due to get mugged today, but you’d know about it, sure as jury duty.

### The Great Borough Boom

As the first planet in the galaxy to have institutionalized crime, Fracture was an overnight success. In fact, it was such a success, the population exploded. The walls of the twelve boroughs couldn’t contain all the fresh blood, and it quickly spilled over to the town’s outskirts. New boroughs were born. New walls were built. And these upstart gangs didn’t see much sense in paying tribute to a syndicate on the other end of town, when they had perfectly good rings in need of kissing right there. This was known as The Great Borough Boom, an exciting and, as it turned out, deadly time in Fracture’s history that led directly to The Hundred-Borough War. Today it’s estimated there are over a thousand boroughs jostling for elbow room in Fracture -- but the truth is, the city’s such a shifting mosaic of alliances, backstabs, assassinations, and startups, the census bureau’s never gonna get a headcount. All you need to know is where you’re standing -- because wherever it is, you owe someone some respect.

### Fracture Today

As you can imagine, an ever-shifting map of alliances makes it hard to get around the city without making a lot of folks mad. That’s why the Bureau of Tourism recommends all newcomers to Fracture hire yourselves a guide to help you bribe, threaten, and stab your way to all the culture, art, and history Fracture has to offer.

## The Fracture Mayoral Election

The Fracture Mayoral Election -- the greatest show of democratic bloodsport in the galaxy! To visitors from more "traditional" planets, having an election settled by bullets instead of ballots may seem like a bit of a culture shock, so read on and learn how Fracture redefined Democracy for these modern times.

### The Golden Age of Impartiality

As the first and only planet in the galaxy to have institutionalized crime, Fracture had discovered a new problem. For the first time in our history, people were coming here willingly. The sudden population explosion led to The Great Borough Boom. And that led to the dark days of The Hundred Borough War. Thus, the role of the Mayor was invented to re-establish Fracture’s unique brand of lawless order. Back then, the Mayor was more like a judge. One time she was a Djinn (Hammurabi the Fire-Wise). Another time it was a robot (S.O.L.O.M.O.N.). But every time, the Mayor was the one person in Fracture you could take an inter-borough dispute to, knowing for certain that they were impartial, unbiased, and incorruptible. But that’s the thing about Fracture: We never give up. And while it may have taken us thousands of years, we eventually found a way to buy off a robot mayor and ruin our perfect legal system. But, as luck would have it, we accidentally invented an even better one! It turned out a corruptible mayor was an even bigger boon to the city than an incorruptible one.

### The Golden Age of Corruption

Let’s say you’re the leader of a gang. You’ve worked hard to put your borough on the map. The shake-down money is rolling in from local businesses, you’ve cornered the market on fake designer handbags, and your crew has more ammunition than they could hope to fire in a lifetime. Now, according to the stupid law, you shouldn’t be able to take over the borough next door, even though it’s run by a spoiled brat who inherited it from his dad and he’s running it into the ground. What’s fair is that the borough is technically his. What’s right is that it should be yours. Once word got out that a little hard work and backroom dealing could move the borough borders in a gang’s favor, competition once again thrived in Fracture.

### On the Verge of War

Over time, it became clear that having a mayor in your corner could make the difference between your borough thriving or dying. With every election season that passed, tactics got a little more brutal. What started as simple bribes to the mayor turned into assassination attempts. Paying for votes turned to threatening the voters. In time, Fracture was on the verge of its first-ever Thousand Borough War. With the city on the brink, a Conclave was held in the one neutral part of town, the City Center. Representatives from every borough showed up to negotiate a peaceful solution -- Here's what they came up with.

### A Single Battle

Going forward, mayoral elections would be settled by a single knock-down, drag-out fight in the City Center, winner take all. Each candidate meets with all the boroughs they’re in bed with and selects six champions to represent them in the fight. Now, these six representatives might not like each other -- in fact, they might have plenty of good reasons to kill each other -- but if they want all the favors, kickbacks, and special treatment their candidate promised them, that mayor needs to win. So for one day only, they’d better work together.

## Factions in Fracture

A criminal ecosystem as rich and diverse as Fracture is full of organizations that are constantly jockeying for power in the city. Here's a handy guide of some of the more prominent factions that have taken an interest in this year’s election cycle.

### The 7th Moon

The 7th Moon is not just one of the founding families of Fracture; it's the criminal institution with the longest lineage of leadership in the entire city. Driven by history, tradition, and a strict hierarchy - one family has run The 7th Moon for generations, and there is no sign of that stopping anytime soon.

### The 8th Sun

To most people; death is the end. To the leaders of The 7th Moon, it's a promotion. Comprised entirely of the undead elders of The 7th Moon; The 8th Sun once acted as a shadow council that would quietly advise their descendants. However, that all changed during the Hundred Borough war when The 8th Sun revealed themselves to the world. Now an "independent" organization, the elderly undead mostly keep to themselves.

### The Alliance

The Fracture Tourist Bureau would like to remind visiting members of the Intergalactic Alliance that Fracture is a sovereign city planet and that none of your laws, rules, titles, or customs are obligated to be observed. The Bureau would also like to remind Fracture locals that while profiting off of The Alliance is certainly in the spirit of our great city: declaring fealty to The Alliance is not, and may be grounds to lose citizenship. Collaborate with the Alliance against your fellow citizens at your own risk.

### The Constables

The robot peacekeepers that make up The Constables are the closest thing to an unbiased party in Fracture. Acting as a deterrent when inter-borough disputes can't be resolved between themselves, when The Constables show up, most gangs know it's time to back off.

### The Grey

REDACTED BY THE GREY. A REWARD WILL BE OFFERED TO ANYONE WHO TURNS IN OLDER EDITIONS OF THIS PUBLICATION THAT HAD WRITTEN INFORMATION ON THE GREY.

### The Haunts

The Haunts: an organization that specializes in assassinating the supernatural. Unfortunately for The Haunts, science is a thing. As such, almost everyone in the galaxy thinks they're a bunch of zealots who use mumbo jumbo to justify the murder of anyone that gets in their way.

### The Lost Battalion

Members of the Lost Battalion insist that they are veterans of the Delcano Time War. Sadly, there's no record of such a war ever occurring. Whether this is because the whole story is made up, or because time was forever altered, is up for debate. But here's a pro-tip to visitors who have a vested interest in not breathing through a tube: don't tell a member of The Lost Battalion that the time war never happened.

### The Meakashi

As word of the criminal utopia that is Fracture spread throughout the galaxy, criminals from every corner of the cosmos sought to visit, thinking it would be a great place for their murder-vacations. However, the illicit ecosystem in Fracture is a delicate one. Each gang has a role to play and rules to follow, and the city of Fracture has no interest in letting tourists mess that up. That's where the Meakashi come in: a crew of bounty hunters (more like a biker gang) that roam the boroughs, hunting down those off-world criminals that flaunt the rules of Fracture.

### The Protean Coalition

While undoubtedly you've heard about the pleasant small-town vibe of the 48th Borough, tourists are advised to stay away unless specifically granted permission by The Protean Coalition: a collection of were-folk that claim that land as their own.

### The Tunnel Rats

Looking for that special bottle of liquor to celebrate a heist? Or maybe your birthday's coming up and you really want some macarons. In Fracture, you can find anything, but the real question is, "How do I get it?" Between gang wars, cold wars, trade wars, and wars wars, there are dozens of reasons why access to your favorite items made in a specific borough may be inaccessible. And when you run into one of those situations, you're going to need The Tunnel Rats. Specializing in inter-borough trade routes, The Tunnel Rats are experts in moving products from one borough to another.

### The Wreckage Movement

Did you happen to see that burned-out husk of a nightclub in the 819th Borough? That's not the result of domestic terrorism; it's just a new form of street art pioneered by The Wreckage Movement! If you're interested in buying a professional colleague a custom demolition for their place of business, don't hesitate to contact Ballista.

### Paradox

Fracture is full of criminals, but only the best are invited to join Paradox, Fracture's premier thieves guild. Now, it may sound intimidating to visit a borough run by the galaxy's greatest collection of cat burglars, grifters, and second-story men, but don't worry! Led by the enigmatic Chrono, Paradox prides itself on constructing elaborate heists that target the most untouchable of individuals and institutions. So unless you happen to be traveling with a collection of ancient artifacts or are an intergalactic head of state, you have little to fear from Paradox.

### The Disciples of Creela

A relatively new institution in Fracture, The Disciples of Creela are one part assassin cartel, one part religious cult, and one part multi-level marketing company.

### Smuggler's Local 3150

Are you a smuggler looking for a new ship and need a storage solution for predatory off-world animals? Or perhaps you're exporting recreational munitions and fusion bombs and really don't want to deal with all the hassle non-Fracture governments impose on their citizens? Then you need to contact Smuggler's Local 3150, a union made up of the planet's most skilled craftsfolk.

### Strike Team Endeavor

Once, Strike Team Endeavor was the most decorated black ops group in The Alliance Special Forces. Today, they've been declared anathema and are now seen as enemies of the state in the eyes of The Intergalactic Alliance. Taking refuge in Fracture, Strike Team Endeavor now offers their particular set of skills to the highest bidder.

## Locations in Fracture

While City Center has been closed off to prepare for The Election Battle, there are plenty of places to explore in Fracture -- some of them might even be safe!

### The Bear Pit

Home to Fracture's number one combat sport "Robot Rumble," The Bear Pit is an arena with an atmosphere like none other. In its hallowed halls, Kali, Bebop, and Lash rose from obscurity to become icons in the sport.

### Jeong's Dumplings and More

Come for the dumplings, stay for the black market tech auction that happens after hours!

### The Boy and the Drizaloth

A NEW DINING CONCEPT COMING SOON TO FRACTURE (PENDING ACQUISITION OF LIQUOR LICENSE FROM THE MAYOR)

### The Midnight Robo Rally

Looking for danger and excitement? Then check out the Midnight Robo Rally! Marvel as 20 robots race through 20 miles of winding roads through the industrial wasteland that is Fracture's 113th Borough. Special note to attendees with small children: an average MRR will usually claim the lives of 4 racers and 19 live attendees, so be sure to wear a poncho!

### 854 Industrial Meat Management

Come see the place where Kelvin decided that he wanted more in life than just having a bathroom at his workplace! There's really not much to see. It's a meat-packing plant. But the owners paid for product placement, so check it out!

### The Deep

Did you know that in addition to all the open violence and grift you see on our streets, there is a whole other world of crime waiting to be explored? If you're feeling adventurous, put on some scuba gear and explore The Deep, where the criminal mysteries of ocean life await you.

### The Attic

The Attic is the main base of operations for The Haunts. Here in this grand murder cathedral, new recruits are "trained" (read: indoctrinated) in the skills needed to fight the "supernatural" (read: anyone The Haunts leadership deems necessary to remove).

### Temple of Kreela

Looking to dedicate your life in service to a questionable Goddess of Assassination? Speak to Haze at the Temple of Kreela.

### Fracture Cooperative Ixith Distillery

We may not like The Alliance here in Fracture, but many citizens of the city love the proprietary liquor they make there. That's why our patriotic citizens stole the materials needed to set up their own Ixith Distillery here on Fracture. It's the closest you can get to the real thing without stealing it yourself.

### Lash's Dojo

Hey. Lash here. There was no way The Lash was going to let the city write a bio for his place of business -- words can't describe poetry in motion. Just check out the Dojo. Be inspired. Be humbled. Be better than your sucky self. -L.

### Mole Town

Looking to step away from the hustle and bustle of the lower 100 Boroughs? Pay a visit to Mole Town, where galaxy-renowned Mole artisans craft traditional furniture, art, and jewelry.

### Strike Out Bowling and Bikes

If the Meakashi's first love is roughing up tourists, their second is bowling, so it's no wonder they added a 10-lane bowling alley to their bike shop. If you're feeling particularly adventurous, be sure to swing by on Wednesday nights for "The Deadliest Karaoke In The Galaxy."

### The Paradox Museum

Nestled in the 93rd Borough is the Paradox Museum: a remarkable collection of art, government secrets, antiquities, and celebrity paternity tests all stolen by the notorious thieves guild. Admission is free for children and anyone who provides blackmail material.

### The Deep Embassy (Formerly Fracture Aquarium)

While many of the conflicts of The Deep stay localized to its 30 Borough trench, sometimes its denizens need to interact with the surface. If you're looking to do business with seahorse loan sharks or psychic sea anemones, here's the place to do it.

### City Center

City Center (or as the locals call it: District Zero) is the heart of Fracture. Because violence of any kind is forbidden in City Center, it's a popular destination both for tourists looking to not get stabbed, and citizens brokering inter-borough deals alike. The only exception of course, is during The Election Battle, where District Zero turns into the most violent spectacle in the galaxy.

## Hero Backgrounds

### Akimbo

Though he was built by a lonely gunslinger, Akimbo was taught that he couldn't use a gun to solve all his problems. This frustrated the robot outlaw immensely, but as time passed Akimbo realized that his human father was right. A gun only solved about 75% of his problems. To solve ALL his problems, he would need at least 2 guns.

### Ballista

At a young age, Ballista learned a valuable lesson: if you blow up 13 buildings you're a public menace. If you CREATIVELY blow up 50 buildings you can pass it off as avant-garde street art. As such, Ballista declared themselves founder of The Wreckage Movement, a collective of bohemian artists whose medium is demolition.

# Neon Prime

“Welcome to Fracture: City of a Thousand Cities!”

This page has content related to *Neon Prime*, an earlier version of *Deadlock*.

 Neon Prime screenshot

***Neon Prime*** was an early development version of *Deadlock.* It was created after *Citadel.*

The game was cancelled late in development and reworked into *Shadowline* and later *Deadlock*, due to negative feedback from playtesters regarding its art style and setting. *Neon Prime* reportedly had issues of poor visibility due to the heavy use of neon lights in VFX and models.[1]

Many of *Deadlock's* current features and assets have been inherited from *Neon Prime*, and are expected to be updated or replaced over the course of development.

## Setting

[edit | edit source]

*Main article: Neon Prime lore*

*Neon Prime* had a Cyberpunk sci-fi aesthetic featuring supernatural elements.

The game took place in an alien world called Fracture, a former prison planet that was taken over by inmates and turned into a tourism hotspot where crime is legal. The game matches were elections in the form of organized bloodsports in the city center, in which each team represented a mayor candidate.

## Gameplay

[edit | edit source]

The gameplay of *Neon Prime* was similar to *Deadlock.* 6 players on each side would use ziplines (then called *hyperlines*) to traverse 4 lanes and fight guardians and walkers to destroy an enemy boss called the Titan. The players would unlock *tech* (abilities) and use coins to buy items, called *mods.* In *Neon Prime,* the players had 6 item slots for each category instead of 8 universal slots.

A notable difference is that *Neon Prime* had a 3-hit combo melee system, instead of *Deadlock's* light and heavy melee.

There were two major versions of the Neon Prime map. V1 was developed around 2021 and was set during daylight. V2 was developed around 2022 and was set during night time.

Killing the Mid-Boss gave you the ability to immediately respawn after the player's death, as can be heard in the unused tutorial voice line from the Deadlock files.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- *Neon Prime's* portraits were drawn by former Valve artist Claire Hummel.[9]
- Vasili Zorin was the character designer of *Neon Prime*.[9] Vasili has been working at Valve since 2018,[10] when development on *Citadel* began.
- Fracture's title of "City of a thousand cities" may have been a reference to the 2017 movie *Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets,* based on the 1967 French comic series *Valérian and Laureline*.

# Oathkeeper

Oathkeeper's true form in *The Binding of Oathkeeper*.

“

Oathkeeper wasn't named ironically; that thing is like the Patron Saint of Faustian Bargains.

— Johann Geist Jr.

**Oathkeeper** is a spirit residing in  Lady Geist's arm that provides her with power and a youthful appearance in return for feeding on the life force of others.

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

Circa 1899, the first Maelstrom happened, bringing various supernatural forces to Earth. Around this time, Lady Geist was an old lady stuck in a nursing home, dreaming of her glorious past. At this moment, Oathkeeper revealed himself to Geist with a proposition: he could restore her youth; all she had to do was drain the essence of the living to sustain herself.[1]

Understanding that Oathkeeper likely couldn't be trusted, Lady Geist had a ward built to bind Oathkeeper to her arm shortly after their deal was made. The purpose of the ward was to limit Oathkeeper's influence over Geist, keeping him under control. As the ward was "against the spirit of the bargain," Oathkeeper promised to make Geist suffer if he ever broke free.[2] Since that day, Oathkeeper has been bound to Geist for roughly 50 years.[3] However, the ward has started to weaken, and it won't be long until he successfully breaks the ward and is released from his prison.[1]

Lady Geist's visual novel, *The Binding of Oathkeeper*, tells of Lady Geist's story to prevent Oathkeeper from breaking free and killing her. This is also Lady Geist's motivation for participating in the ritual.[4][5]

Oathkeeper's power comes from him feeding on life. The more youthful and "quality" the life is, the longer Oathkeeper is satiated.[2] If he is starved, his power drains, which causes Lady Geist to return to her old age. Apparently, Oathkeeper's hunger has become harder to satiate, as a year ago Geist could kill one vagrant to stay youthful throughout Summer,[6] yet in the present day killing three vagrants would only satiate Oathkeeper for 2 months.[7] It's possible for Oathkeeper to be transferred from Lady Geist to a different host, as seen in The Binding of Oathkeeper where Lady Geist pawns off Oathkeeper to Maximilian Fairfax.[8]

The ward binding Oathkeeper was originally constructed by Lady Geist's son, Walter Geist, who did extensive research into Oathkeeper.[9][10] The resposibilities of maintaining and upgrading the ward after Walter's death fell to his son, Johann Geist Jr, who last upgraded the ward 5 years ago.[11] According to Lady Geist, the ward acts like a puzzle box that Oathkeeper would be compelled to open, which diverts his attention away from making demands of Geist.[12] The reason why the ward is failing is because Oathkeeper "got better at multitasking". It isn't possible for Johann Jr. to make a better ward.[13]

Aside from keeping Oathkeeper under control, the ward also prevents Oathkeeper from interacting with the world outside his prison. Lady Geist can choose when she wants Oathkeeper to see or listen to the outside world.[14] Only Lady Geist can hear Oathkeeper speak, with the main exception of Graves.[15]

Oathkeeper originated from a different realm, coming to Earth after being conjured by the tome  Detective Abrams carries.[16] While it's unknown when Oathkeeper was summoned, he is old friends with Drifter and apparently goes "way back" with him,[17] implying that Oathkeeper was on Earth before the First Maelstrom.

Oathkeeper is described as a "parasite" who needs a host to survive.[18]

# Occult Security and Investigation Commission

OSIC letter addressed to Dynamo

“

You know it's bad when they send a Sandman.

— Haze

A secretive "Black Box" United States government organization, the **Occult Security and Investigation Commission** (**OSIC**, for short) specializes in keeping the country safe from sinister and supernatural forces.[1]

## Contents

- 1 Summary
- 2 Members

- 2.1 Agent Marlowe
- 3 Divisions

- 3.1 Sandman Division
- 3.2 Curator Division
- 3.3 Medium Division
- 4 Trivia
- 5 References

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

The Occult Security and Investigation Commission works hard to ensure supernatural threats that are too big for local law enforcement to handle are taken care of.[1] The OSIC keeps files on many notable persons,[2] and once a threat to national security has been identified, a Sandman is sent to neutralize the threat.[3]

The OSIC has warned New York citizens to stay indoors for the duration of the Maelstrom.[4]  Haze has been sent to fight in the ritual by the OSIC, although the details of her mission are currently unknown.[5][6]

The OSIC wants Calico and Seven dead.[7][8] They seem to know that Seven is in New York, as Seven is hiding from them in New York's subway tunnels.[9] The OSIC is also keeping an eye on Wraith and Yamato,[10][11] although they haven't been considered worth allocating resources to take out yet. Haze mentions that if the Seventh Moon becomes a cartel, then her superiors would likely send her to kill Yamato.[12] The OSIC doesn't seem to be after Drifter.[13]

The OSIC is implied to be worried about creatures of The Deep.[14] They seem to know about the Adversary and are aware of how dangerous it is.[15] Once the ritual is over, Haze wants Viscous to tell her everything about the Adversary so the OSIC can prepare in case any more creatures like it come through The Deep's Astral Gate.[16]

The OSIC's main office is not local to New York. Instead, they've set up a temporary base of operations in the area, although Haze believes that the OSIC will open a permanent office after the ritual due to all the activity going on in the area.[17]

Haze acknowledges that the OSIC is flawed and that they don't have enough people "who care what doors are getting kicked down".[18][19] That said, she is still loyal to her job and believes that the ends justify the means.[20] Haze works for the OSIC because she "loves her country".[21]

Lady Geist is worried she will be sent to an OSIC oubliette if she caters to Oathkeeper's demands.[22] Haze warns her that the OSIC will have to intervene if "the Oathkeeper issue isn't resolved".[23]

The OSIC is interested in  Kelvin's condition as a revenant.[24] They also show some interest in Celeste being a unicorn.[25]

The OSIC has released a report about hexes.[26]

The OSIC limits expeditions to the North Pole.[27]

## Members

[edit | edit source]

- Haze - OSIC agent in the Sandman Division
- Marlowe - OSIC agent

### Agent Marlowe

[edit | edit source]

Marlowe is an agent for the OSIC. While his exact role in the organization is unknown, he's noted as someone who "spins stories" and seems to be one of Haze's superiors.[28][29]

Haze mentions that Marlowe made "a good offer" to Dynamo. While the details of the offer are unclear, Dynamo refuses it, although Marlowe told Haze that the offer still stands in case Dynamo changes his mind.[30] Dynamo carries a letter from the OSIC addressed to him in his bag.

Venator is a friend of Marlowe and calls him a "bastard".[28]

Haze believes Marlowe would want to know about The Doorman's involvement in the ritual.[31]

Marlowe makes an appearance in Holliday's visual novel, where he tells Holliday and Captain Murphy that the OSIC is taking over the investigation into the Troubadour. He asks Holliday to either help him or get out of his way.[32] While his role in the story past chapter 2 is unclear, Holliday's conversations with Seven imply that his goal was to hire the Troubadour.[33]

## Divisions

[edit | edit source]

The OSIC has multiple divisions. Known divisions include:

- The Sandman Division
- The Curator Division
- The Medium Division

### Sandman Division

[edit | edit source]

A division specialized in infiltrating dreams.  Haze is a notable member of this division; seeking out the dreams of "persons of interest" to investigate them. If necessary, members of the Sandman Division have clearance to "eliminate" significant detected threats.[1]

The OSIC's Sandmen rarely work together.[34] It's unknown how many Sandmen there are, but Haze says that there's enough of them to call themselves a division.[35]

The OSIC has not confirmed or denied the existence of the Sandman Division.[36]

The Sandman Division has released a holiday calendar to "soften their image", but it only made them seem "more terrifying".[37]

### Curator Division

[edit | edit source]

The Curator Division deals with magical objects like Pocket's case or Graves' lich hand.[38][39] According to  Haze, "Curators care about things and Sandmen care about people".[3]

Haze believes  Paige would be a good Curator.[40]  Paradox wants Haze to put in a good word with the Curator Division for her.[41]

### Medium Division

[edit | edit source]

Not much is known about the Medium Division.  Haze recommends a job as an OSIC medium to  Graves, asking her to consider the offer and call her if she's interested.[42]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

OSIC door in the work-in-progress Hideout map

- The initialism OSIC is pronounced "oh-ess-i-see".
- Haze's background compares the OSIC to the CIA, which was founded in 1947 in the real world. The CIA is also mentioned in Wrecker's background.
- In an older work-in-progress version of the Hideout map, a door labeled "O.S.I.C. Restricted Area" could be found.
- A removed  Dynamo voiceline suggested that Sandmen were considered a conspiracy theory.[43]

# Outer Planes

An advert for *Astral Plane Canned Mille-Pattes Dazzle*

**The Outer Planes** refer to planes of existence beyond the known universe.

Some Outer Planes are connected to Earth by Astral Gates.

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

The Outer Planes include Ixia[1] and the Patron's plane.[2] Some souls of humans move to an Outer Plane after death.[3]

The US is currently sending aid to the Outer Planes due to the military campaign in Ixia.[4][1]

The Doorman is an extraplanar being and an "old friend" of the Patrons.[5][6]

An exhibit at the Met is due to open up showing off artifacts from the Outer Planes.[7]

The New York Astral Gate has led to extraplanar invasive species appearing in the city.[8]

*Astral Plane Canned Mille-Pattes Dazzle* ("mille-pattes" is French for "centipede") are advertised as *The World's Most Popular Delicacy*.

“

Books can save people's lives!

**Paige** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. Citizens of Manhattan will learn to appreciate the power of the written word when Paige joins the fight. With the mere toss of a book she can conjure a Bookwyrm that sears enemies who get too close, or bind them to the ground with Captivating Read. Waning allies will find themselves emboldened by Plot Armor, granting them the courage to fight another day. Fantasy becomes reality with Rallying Charge, summoning an entire cavalry to gallop across the city.

Paige grew up with books, love, and kindness in her family home; but she was at odds with her rebellious younger brother, Bryce. He sought out dangerous occult magics, disappearing one day while Paige's normally-watchful eye was away. Now a talented bibliomancer, Paige seeks answers about her brother's disappearance and will stop at nothing to find the answers.

Paige was released on August 25, 2025 as the fourth hero of the Six New Heroes update (third winner of hero vote).

Rapid Fire

Chapter's End's projectiles can pierce through enemies. Items that proc on bullet hit such as  Mystic Shot only proc on the first enemy hit.

Chapter's End does not deal critical damage on headshots, but it does proc headshot items such as  Headshot Booster.

Paige can gain stacks from  Split Shot by hitting multiple players with the same projectile.
