## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Paige/Lore** for more story content.*

“

The daughter of a rare book dealer, Paige grew up in a loving home that prioritized kindness, magic, and storytelling.  But while Paige took naturally to her parents' values, her little brother Bryce did not.

A rebellious teen, Bryce resented not only his family’s saccharine attitude, but also their refusal to let him dabble in magics that they deemed too dangerous.  Paige tried everything she could think of to keep him out of trouble, but like most teenagers, the more his big sister tried to tell him what was best for him, the more he turned away.

Paige doesn't know what Bryce did to get kicked out of the house...just that she came home from the library to find her brother gone and her parents crying.

Days turned to weeks, to months, to years.  Paige grew to become a talented bibliomancer, making a living as a storyteller reading at libraries across the five boroughs; and while her parents have remained silent about what happened with Bryce, Paige's obsession with finding him has only grown.  She will discover what happened to her brother... and no man or god is going to stand in her way.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Paige's name has a double meaning: It can be a reference to the pages of books, as well as the servants of knights and noblemen in medieval times.
- Paige was one of the heroes in a private build who was accidently leaked on stream in May 2025.[2]
- Paige was originally named **Bookworm**, and later renamed to **Patience** during development, before being changed to her current name. Some voice lines still refer to her as Patience,[3][4] but that is unintentional.[5]
- Paige's ability VFX uses text from the book *Sir Gawain and the Green Knight* and the placeholder Lorem Ipsum text.
- "Reading in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Paige in the Hideout.
- **Bookwyrm** was originally named **Conjure Dragon**, and **Plot Armor** was originally named **Defend and Fight!**. These abilities were renamed based on feedback from a Reddit post by user *u/CDranzer*.[6] *Wyrm* is an Old English word for "serpent" or "dragon" in Germanic folklore.
- The book used in Bookwyrm uses textures from TF2's Bombinomicon.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Paige's motivation in the ritual is to find and save her brother, Bryce.[1][2]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Paige reads books to kindergarteners.[3][4] She loved showing off  Bookwyrm at the library, but was forced to stop after the dragon burnt some books.[5][6]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Paige loves reading all kinds of books, having set times of day for different types of books.[7] Aside from real-world novels, Paige has read books on  Kelvin's adventures and the Baxter Society.[8][9]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Paige had a diary in high school where she wrote about byronic heroes.[10]

### Literature References

[edit | edit source]

Paige makes several references to real life literature and authors. These include:

- Various references to Arthurian Legend.[11][12]
- *A Midsummer Night's Dream,* written by William Shakespeare and performed in 1595-1596.[11]
- *Henry V,* written by Shakespeare and performed in 1599-1600.[13]
- *Othello,* written by William Shakespeare and performed in 1601-1604.[14]
- *Pride and Prejudice,* written by Jane Austen and published in 1813.[15][16]
- *Wuthering Heights,* written by Emily Brontë and published in 1847.[11][16][15]
- *The Picture of Dorian Gray,* written by Oscar Wilde and published in 1891.[17]
- *Sherlock Holmes,* specifically *The Adventure of the Empty House,* written by Arthur Conan Doyle and published in 1903.[18]
- *The Wind in the Willows,* written by Kenneth Grahame and published in 1908.[19]
- *Hercule Poirot,* a fictional detective from a series written by Agatha Christie.[20]
- *Of Mice and Men,* written by John Steinbeck and published in 1937.[21]
- *The Lion, The Witch and The Wardrobe,* written by C. S. Lewis and published in 1950.[22]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Bryce

[edit | edit source]

Paige describes her brother Bryce as a curmudgeon.[23]

Venator believes Bryce is beyond saving, expressing remorse that Paige has "thrown away her life to save someone who doesn't deserve it".[24][25]  Haze believes Paige would be happier if she lets her brother go.[26]

### Kelvin

[edit | edit source]

Paige idolises Kelvin and loves his stories.[27][28]

### Ivy and Manny Arroyo

[edit | edit source]

Ivy has brought her brother Manny to Paige's story hour.[29] Ivy wants to start a book club with Paige.[30]

### Krill

[edit | edit source]

Krill and Paige once planned to start a book club together.[31]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Paige likes heroic men[32][33] and has a crush on  Mirage,[34]  Shiv[35] and  Victor.[36][37]
- Paige admires  Mirage and says he "stepped out of every romance novel ever written".[38][39] She thinks Mirage is better than  Shiv.[40]
- Paige wants to give Billy and Viscous a hug.[41][42] Celeste wants to give Paige a hug.[43]
- Paige compares Billy to Nick Bottom from *A Midsummer Night's Dream*[44] and Mr. Tumnus from *The Chronicles of Narnia*.[45]
- Paige calls Lash a "dimestore Mr. Collins".[46]
- Paige loves animals like Mo and Ava.[47][48] She believes that Calico "can't be evil" because she has a cat.[49]
- Paige thinks Holliday shouldn't have a gun due to her mental state.[50][51]
- Vyper has met Paige's brother and says he was "more fun".[52] Bryce told her that Paige is "wound up tight".[53]
- The Doorman likes Paige's taste in books and invites her to host a storytelling event at the Baroness Hotel.[54][55]
- Yamato likes Paige, likening her to a "puppy that pisses on the rug: stupid, yet strangely endearing".[56][57]
- Infernus and the Shopkeeper are familiar with Paige's family.[58][59]
- Lash respects Paige for going to college.[60]
- Paradox is interested in stealing Paige's rare books.[61]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

During development, Paige was originally called **Patience**.[62][63]

# Paradox Museum

“

Think I'll take a walk through the museum.

— Paradox

The Paradox Museum is a pop-up gallery showcasing everything the Paradox Organisation steals.

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

The Paradox Organisation steals priceless artifacts to be showcased at the Paradox Museum, with the intention of showing that anything can be stolen by Paradox.[1] Once a sufficient number of artifacts are gathered, the museum is open to the public for a short amount of time.[2]

The Paradox Museum isn't exclusively for art: it's also used to showcase stolen state secrets, celebrity paternity tests,[1] and forms of blackmail on renowned individuals.[3]

As a pop-up gallery, the Paradox Museum has no set location.[1] Where Paradox stores their artifacts while the Museum is closed is unknown.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Characters that have visited the Paradox Museum include but aren't limited toCalico,[4] Dynamo[5] and Lady Geist.[6] Vyper has also visited the museum, but was kicked out.[7]
- The items that are known to be showcased at the Paradox Museum include The Ghent Altarpiece,[3] a hellenistic Bust of Homer,[8] one of Johann Geist's paintings,[9][10] the Tome of Anubis (whichRaven allegedly also has),[3][11] and some kind of "blackmail on Fairfax".[3]
- Calico and  Dynamo both show adoration for the Paradox Museum.[5][4]  Lady Geist, on the other hand, describes it as "a multi-million exhibition with the emotional depth of a 10th grader writing "I will rage against conformity" in a poetry unit of Remedial English."[12]

# Paradox Organisation

“

The only thing I expect from Paradox is style over substance.

— Grey Talon

The Paradox Organisation is a guild of thieves who want to show the world that there's nothing they can't steal.

## Contents

- 1 Summary
- 2 Thefts
- 3 Trivia
- 4 References

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

The Paradox Organisation, also known as Paradox for short, is a group of bored rich thieves who steal various objects of interest.[1] Whatever Paradox steals is presented at the Paradox Museum, a pop-up gallery open to the public with the intention of showing the world that Paradox can steal from anyone.[2]

The Paradox Organisation does not exclusively steal artifacts: they also steal state secrets and blackmail on celebrities.[2]

Paradox (the playable character) is one member of the Paradox Organisation. Each member of Paradox wears a mask and a coat,[3][4] and gives up their name to join the organisation.[5]

The members of Paradox work mostly independently, gathering together a few times a year to discuss their thefts.[6][1] The thefts of each Paradox member is "based on individual interest and challenge".[7]

The origins of the Paradox Organisation are unknown. Their oldest known theft seems to be one of Johann Geist's paintings, which happened 50 years before the events of the game.[8][9]

## Thefts

[edit | edit source]

The Paradox Organisation has had several artifacts on its radar. Some thefts have been successful, some have yet to be committed, and some have failed.

- Paradox has successfully stolen The Ghent Altarpiece, the Tome of Anubis, some form of blackmail on Fairfax,[10] a hellenistic Bust of Homer,[11] one of Johann Geist's paintings,[12][9] Booth's Deringer,[13] and the location of Seven's safehouse.[14]
- The Paradox Organisation has shown interest in robbing Kelvin's home during the ritual. Paradox, the playable hero, has shown personal interest in Abrams' tome,[15] Holliday's revolver,[16] McGinnis' research and secrets she holds for Fairfax,[17][18] Nashala,[19] rare books Paige may have,[20] Pocket's suitcase,[21] and Yamato's sword.[22]
- The Paradox Organisation has tried, and failed, to break into the Baxter Society's Manor House, although they haven't given up trying.[23] They have also been unsuccessful at breaking into the Baroness Hotel.[24] The Paradox Organisation keep trying to steal Celeste's horn.[25]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The Paradox Organisation is wary of Abrams.[26]
- Paradox holds Kelvin in high regard.[27]

“

If someone's by themselves, I'll drag 'em to where I want them to be.

**Paradox** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. She wields time manipulation with potent disruption and slowing abilities. With a charged Kinetic Carbine, she can threaten her enemies at any range while damaging and slowing them with thrown Pulse Grenades and well-placed Time Walls. At just the right moment, Paradox can activate her Paradoxical Swap to change places with her target, dropping them into a dangerous situation amongst her team.

Paradox is both the name of this Hero and the name of their Thieves' Guild, specializing in stealing the untouchable and breaking into ultra-secure facilities. Their motives are unclear, except for a certain level of delight that its members seem to take in snubbing the world's biggest corporations and governments.

### Kinetic Carbine

KINETIC CARBINE

**28**s

Charge up a powerful shot of time energy, dealing   spirit damage and applying a Time-Stop to enemies hit. The damage dealt increases with   weapon damage. Move speed is increased while charging.  

While in the air and charging, ** Zoom / alt-fire** to timeslow your movement.

Notes

- Carbine's damage scaling is based on Weapon Damage of a full burst shot (5 * bullet damage).

- Despite scaling with Weapon Damage, it deals Spirit Damage, and thus can trigger spirit items like  Mystic Reverb,  Tankbuster or  Spirit Burn.
- Carbine is immune to Bullet Evasion.
- Conditional Weapon Damage items apply their bonuses to Carbine. For example, having  Point Blank will make Carbine use it's damage bonus if the shot target is in close range.
- Carbine has inconsistent interactions with items that affect shooting:

- Items that apply their effects with Kinetic Carbine:

- Restorative Shot.
- Mystic Shot.
- Weakening Headshot and  Crippling Headshot.
- Hollow Point's bullet resist debuff.
- Items that do not apply their effects with Kinetic Carbine:

- Headshot Booster and  Headhunter.
- Spirit Shredder Bullets and  Spirit Rend.
- Point Blank slow.
- Tesla Bullets and  Capacitor.
- Armor Piercing Rounds' pierce.
- Lucky Shot's extra damage.
- Ricochet.
- Siphon Bullets.
- Buildup items like  Toxic Bullets.
- Split Shot allows Paradox to fire 5 Carbine shots at once. However, it will only affect the first enemy hit.
- Express Shot gives the smaller "Secondary Fire Weapon Damage" bonus to Carbine shot and immediately shoots a regular bullet with the bigger "Weapon Damage" bonus.
- Despite saying "Move Speed is increased while charging", the bonus is only given after the Carbine is fully charged.
- Move Speed bonus is a unique buff that applies a multiplicative modifier to all of Paradox's animations. This has several consequences:

- Move speed bonus works as a flat multiplicative modifier on top of all other move speed buffs and debuffs and is not part of usual stacking algorithm.
- Jump height also gets boost, both for ground and air jumps
- Dash distance seems to be unaffected.
- Reload animation gets completed quicker, but it is only a visual/audial indicator and the actual reload time is unaffected.
- Several items get affected by quicker animations:

- Majestic Leap performs the leap quicker.
- Magic Carpet gets increase to its flying speed.
- Ethereal Shift gets increase to its "floating" speed.

Notes

- On T3, holding alt cast (middle mouse click) before swapping lets the player swap a single target.
- Paradoxical Swap will trigger  Reactive Barrier,  Indomitable and  Cloak of Opportunity, cleansing the effect, so neither you or the target will move.

- On T3, if you hit a target that cleanses Paradoxical Swap, but another target is within the swap area of effect, the following happens:

- The original target of Paradoxical Swap doesn't move.
- Any other nearby targets affected by the swap area of effect will be swapped.
- Paradox will move to the original target's position.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Paradox/Lore** for more story content.*

“

Paradox.  An artifact of time, and the name of a notorious thieves' guild... one that prides themselves on constructing elaborate heists that target the most untouchable of individuals and institutions.  What does Paradox do with the countless artifacts, state secrets, and celebrity paternity tests that they have stolen?  Put it on display at pop-up museums, so that they can show the world that no one is out of Paradox’s reach.

Shrouded in mystery, each member of Paradox dons a mask and takes on the organization's name.  They are everywhere.  They are nowhere.  And if they want something, they are inevitable.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Paradox was named **Chrono** in *Neon Prime*.
- Paradox is voiced by Elle Newlands, who also voiced Horizon in *Apex Legends*. Both characters are Scottish and use technology of spacetime manipulation.
- Paradox wears a blue rose in her lapel, which do not exist in nature, and are only possible through genetic modification. In art, blue roses are a symbol for mystery and the unattainable.
- "Scheming in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Paradox in the Hideout.

# Paradox/Lore

“Alright buddy, give 'em hell!”

This page is under construction. To avoid edit conflicts, please consult the edit history and the talk page.

Paradox.  An artifact of time, and the name of a notorious thieves' guild... one that prides themselves on constructing elaborate heists that target the most untouchable of individuals and institutions.  What does Paradox do with the countless artifacts, state secrets, and celebrity paternity tests that they have stolen?  Put it on display at pop-up museums, so that they can show the world that no one is out of Paradox’s reach.

Shrouded in mystery, each member of Paradox dons a mask and takes on the organization's name.  They are everywhere.  They are nowhere.  And if they want something, they are inevitable.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Paradox has a few motivations in the ritual, the main one being to prove herself to the Paradox Organisation, partially for bragging rights.[1][2][3][4] It's implied that one of Paradox's goals in the ritual is to steal something from the opposing Patron (such as the Hidden King's crown) and display it at the Paradox Museum.[5][6][3] It's also implied that Paradox wants to show that she's fit to lead the Paradox Organisation by completing the ritual.[7] Her exact wish is unknown, but there are dozens of possibilities according to the Patrons.[8]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Not much is known about Paradox herself. She's Scottish and a "bored rich person",[9][10] who gladly gave up her identity to join the Paradox Organisation.[11] The helmet Paradox wears can be taken off (as it's just a mask),[12] but what Paradox does in her free time is unknown.

Paradox is nicknamed as "The Time Thief".[13]

Paradox is currently trying to find a way to break into the Baxter Society's manor house,[14] the Baroness Hotel,[15] and  McGinnis' lab.[16] Paradox was expecting  Venator to come after her at some point, implying the Paradox Organisation has robbed the Vatican before.[17]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Paradox is playful and jokey, but takes the name of the Paradox Organisation very seriously. She drops the humor if Paradox gets threatened or disrespected.[18][19][20]

Other characters often call Paradox "clever".[21]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

How the time manipulation Paradox uses works is a tightly held secret.[22] Paradox says time travel "isn't a thing yet".[23]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Abrams

[edit | edit source]

Abrams has been investigating the Paradox Organisation outside of his case with the Tome.[24]

Paradox threatens Abrams to stop asking questions about them.[25]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Paradox is amazed by the craftsmanship used to create  Bebop.[26]
- Paradox is interested in doing business with  Wraith.[27]
- Paradox knows exactly who  Pocket is.[28][29]
- Paradox loves messing with  Lady Geist and  Kelvin.[30][31]
- Paradox likes  Calico,  Mo & Krill and  Viscous.[32][33][34]
- Paradox loves  Warden's conviction.[35]
- Kelvin is one of Paradox's targets.[36]
- Seven wants to commission Paradox for a job.[37]
- Lady Geist has an old grudge against Paradox.[38]  The Paradox Organisation has stolen one of her husband's paintings.[39][40]
- Holliday,[41]  Kelvin,[42]  Seven[43] and  Warden[44] call out Paradox for wasting their power on petty crimes.
- Drifter,[45] Ivy,[46] Paige,[47] Rem[48] and Vyper[49] like Paradox's trench coat.
- Both  Raven and Paradox claim to be in possession of the Tome of Anubis.  Wraith says she thought the Tome was at the Met.[50][51]

- At some point, the Tome of Anubis was reportedly seen in New York's black market.[52]

### Thefts

[edit | edit source]

Paradox has shown interest in stealing a wide variety of objects belonging to the other characters. Some of these objects include:

- Abrams' Tome.[53]
- Celeste's horn.[54]
- Holliday's revolver.[55]
- McGinnis' research and secrets she holds for Fairfax.[56][57]
- Nashala.[58]
- Paige's rare books.[59]
- Pocket's suitcase.[60]
- Yamato's sword.[61]

There are also some things Paradox has successfully stolen prior to the ritual, such as:

- Seven's safehouse location.[62]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

### Neon Prime - Chrono

[edit | edit source]

Paradox was named **Chrono** in *Neon Prime*.

“

Who wants to summon an elder god?

— Dynamo

A **Patron** is a deity which takes the form of a large extraplanar entity. Each team’s base houses a Patron, **The Hidden King** and **The Archmother**, and victory is secured by defeating the opposing team's Patron, completing the ritual.

The Hidden King appears as a shadowy figure with antlers and glowing yellow eyes, bound to a burning wicker man effigy. Long, claw-like yellow hands extend from the shadows. His base is a factory filled with large speakers and microphones, and his side of the map features working-class red brick buildings labeled "Downtown". The Archmother wears a broken mask resembling the head of the Statue of Liberty, her form bound to a crystalline effigy burning with blue flames. Her base is a museum with a Neoclassic aesthetic, and her side of the map features upper-class white brick buildings labeled "Uptown".

During gameplay, a herald speaks on behalf of the Patrons to their teams, commenting on player performance, announcing major events, and offering boons that allow players to level up.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

The Patron is a formidable unit found at the back of each team's base. In its first phase, the Patron is completely unkillable until both Shrines are destroyed.

The Patron has two methods of attack in Phase 1:

- **Laser Beam**: Fires a slow-moving beam dealing **440 + 5% HP** Spirit Damage per second, targeting enemy players and Troopers and reducing their bullet and spirit resistance by **10%**. The beam leaves behind burning ground that deals damage over time to those who remain in it.
- **Shrine Defense**: Creates a large explosion at a Shrine platform after a 3.5s delay, dealing **300 + 20% HP** Spirit Damage and cursing any enemies caught in the blast, forcing them to retreat or be damaged.

After the first half of its health bar is depleted, the Patron enters its second phase. It becomes invulnerable again for a short period as its shadowy form collapses into its structure. The structure then explodes and reforms into an orb that hovers in the pit. Once the transformation completes, it becomes vulnerable again as a Weakened Patron.

Defeating the Patron's first phase shortens the remaining respawn time of any dead players on the defending team by up to 20s (see Last Stand Buff).

The Patron is the only structure that regenerates health out of combat, restoring **120 health/s**. It is also protected by Backdoor Protection, which increases this regeneration by **75 health/s** when no enemy Troopers are nearby.

## Weakened Patron

[edit | edit source]

In its second phase, the Patron enters its Weakened form, compressing into a spherical orb that hovers inside the pit of its team's base. The Hidden King's orb appears as a cracked sphere of charred wood and burning debris, with a glowing ember core visible through the fissures, surrounded by jagged wooden spikes. The Archmother's orb appears as a crystalline blue sphere surrounded by jagged rock shards arranged to form a face-like structure, with glowing cyan energy emanating from within.

In this state, it has two attacks:

- **Damage Pulse**: Constantly emits **75** damage every second to up to **3** nearby enemies within a **19m** radius.
- **Pit Explosion**: Unleashes a large expanding wave inside the pit after a 3.5s delay, dealing **300 + 20% HP** damage and cursing enemies, similar to the Shrine Defense attack.

Similar to Mid Boss, the Patron is immune to all incoming damage from outside the pit, forcing players to get in close if they want to damage it. The Weakened Patron has the same starting HP as the first phase but gains more HP per minute than phase one.

The Weakened Patron has 50% damage resistance when an ally has been in the pit for more than 2s, and 100% damage resistance when two or more allies are in the pit.

### Health Scaling

[edit | edit source]

The Patron's maximum health is not static and increases as the match progresses, starting at specific times during each phase.

| Phase | Scaling Starts At | Max Health Gained per Minute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Phase 1 | 20 minutes | 250 |
| Phase 2 | 1 minute | 450 |

## Lore

[edit | edit source]

The Patrons are extraplanar[2] elder gods[3][4] whose followers petition heroes to participate in a ritual, in the hopes of summoning them. In order for the ritual to be completed, the enemy Patron must be destroyed.

The two Patrons in-game are the Hidden King and the Archmother. There are more Patrons, but they haven't yet made contact with humanity.[5] The motivations of the Hidden King and Archmother are unclear, although  The Doorman mentions that they've been waiting to be summoned "for centuries".[6]  Warden and his family believe the Patrons will "herald the end of humanity" if they are not stopped.[7]

Once the ritual is completed, the Patrons can grant one wish to each hero who helped summon them.[8] The specifics of the Patron's powers and their limitations are unclear. What the winning Patron intends to do after the ritual is also unclear, although the Patron's herald believes they will usher in a new era.[9][10][11][12]

The Patrons have heralds who speak on their behalf.[13][14][15][16] The heralds have knowledge on the thoughts and desires of the heroes, and can communicate with them telepathically during the ritual. If a hero openly dislikes the Patrons, the herald tells them to direct their anger towards the enemy Patron, as is the case with Warden and  Venator.[17][18] While the heralds can read Warden's emotions, they cannot see his desires.[19]

This is the first time in known history that humanity has been able to make contact with the Patrons.[20] Such rituals used to be impossible, as well as forbidden, before the Second Maelstrom.[21] The orders of the Amber Hand and the Sapphire Flame were supposed to safeguard humanity from the Patrons, but recently are suspected to have changed their objectives.[2]

A Patron looming over humans

The Patrons are familiar with The Doorman, another extraplanar being. They are happy to see Doorman fighting on their behalf.[22][23] The Doorman calls the Patrons "old friends"[24] and refers to them as City Mother and Amber King.[25]

*The Binding of Oathkeeper's* multiple endings shows potential wishes granted by the Patrons:

- An answer to one of  Abrams' questions regarding the Tome;
- Binding Oathkeeper back to the Tome and allowing  Lady Geist to stay young;
- The sacrifice of Johann Jr. in exchange for 200 years of Oathkeeper's complete obedience to Lady Geist;
- The self-sacrifice of Lady Geist in exchange for banishing Oathkeeper from Earth;
- Safely removing Oathkeeper from Geist, but making her return to the natural age she had before their pact.

In addition to the ritual, the Patrons lead skirmishes between their teams in the form of Street Brawl matches.[26]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The Patrons were originally named **The** **Amber Hand** and **The** **Sapphire Flame** before the Old Gods, New Blood update released. The Patrons also used to be the announcers of the game before being replaced by heralds speaking on their behalf.

- These names are referenced in the new design of the Patrons, as the Hidden King has "amber hands" and the Archmother's effigy is surrounded by a "sapphire flame".
- Based on game files and voice lines, another proposed rename for the Patrons was the **Broken Crown** and the **Guided Hand**. Those names are still used in a few voice lines.
- The Hidden King's voice actor was recast in the Old Gods, New Blood update.
- In *Neon Prime*, the Patron was called **Titan**, and the Weakened Patron was the **Core**. The Patrons are still called "Titans" in the game files.
- The Patron damage to the player is listed as "Condemned by the Patron" in the damage report.
- The text across the old Patron model's reads The Patron's crest

KILOZS BOTAREX UNDT VOXT DIOKOTOS DEOS TOPAX DE OS HOLINAS UXFAXT TOV LIMOT OBERXO

GOL EN TAX FOXIST HARFT DEOS MAX OPUS DEONI SUX TOS DUO POLINUAX DREOX SIDWEG

REBTIS AST MECTONUS MAX DERIKT POLTERMUSON DEFONAL WEKMOXAN GETOX D

- As a pseudo-language, many words appear to be phonetic wordplays or portmanteaus based on Latin, Greek, and Germanic roots that seem to reference elements of the Ritual and the Patrons' nature:

- **BOTAREX:** Possibly a blend of *Votum* (vow/wish) and *Rex* (king)
- **HARFT:** Phonetically resembles *Harvest*
- **MAX OPUS:** Similar to *Magnum Opus* (The Great Work in alchemy and occultism)
- **TOS DUO:** Contains the root *duo* (two)
- **MECTONUS:** A possible blend of *Mech* (machine) and *Chthonic* (underworld deity)
- **GETOX:** Phonetically resembles *Gates*

**Plated Armor** is a Tier 4  Vitality Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **6,400**.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Interactions

- 2.1 Weapons
- 2.2 Abilities
- 2.3 Items
- 3 Update history
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- The chance for **Deflection** and *On-hit Prevention* is rolled individually, although **Deflection** will prevent most effects that *On-hit prevention* does. They can both trigger at the same time. This is most evident when testing  Headhunter against Plated Armor.
- If a bullet is deflected, it will fly off in a different direction, maintaining its damaging capability.

## Interactions

[edit | edit source]

Note: Anything missing from this list has not been tested, and, therefore, may, or may not, be affected by Plated Armor.

### Weapons

[edit | edit source]

Blocked by both Deflection and On-Hit Prevention:

- **Spreadshot** weapons (      ): Triggers at once for all pellets. All pellets are deflected as though they are a single shot.
- **Burst** weapons (   ): Applied per bullet.
- Celeste: When deflected, an extra projectile is created. The original projectile can ricochet, as normal, and a new projectile is shot out in a random direction. The new projectile also ricochets.
- Graves: When deflected, it does not ricochet, although a visual bug might appear where a bullet projectile is created. This bullet cannot hit enemies.
- Paige: When deflected, an extra projectile is created. The original projectile pierces, as normal, and a new projectile is shot out in a random direction.

### Abilities

[edit | edit source]

Effects blocked by both Deflection and On-Hit Prevention:

- Billy -  Blasted bonus bullet damage amp
- Celeste -  Light Eater on-hit spirit damage
- Graves -  Essence Theft
- Grey Talon -  Rain of Arrows: Triggers at once for all arrows. All arrows are deflected as though they are a single shot.
- Haze -  Fixation: Stack buildup
- Holliday  Crackshot: Cooldown is not applied when blocked.
- Infernus -  Afterburn: Buildup
- Mina -  Love Bites: Buildup and spirit damage on bullet hits
- Seven -  Power Surge: The chaining damage is blocked per bullet and the opportunity to apply is not consumed when blocked.

Effects partially blocked:

- Venator -  Ira Domini's Weapon damage can be deflected, but not the pure damage.
- Wraith -  Card Trick: Buildup blocked by Deflection.

Effects that are not blocked:

- Mirage -  Djinn's Mark
- Paradox -  Kinetic Carbine
- Silver -  Slam Fire bonus current health damage.
- Sinclair -  Spectral Assistant
- Venator -  Consecrating Grenade and  Gutshot deal weapon damage but cannot be deflected.
- Vindicta -  Flight on-hit spirit damage.
- Wraith -  Full Auto on-hit spirit damage.

### Items

[edit | edit source]

Effects blocked by both Deflection and On-Hit Prevention:

- Point Blank: Slowing debuff
- Ricochet: When blocked, the bullet will never chain, or will be prevented from chaining to any more targets.
- Siphon Bullets: Even when blocked, Siphon Bullets will still go on cooldown.
- Spirit Shredder Bullets /  Spirit Rend
- Stalker: Will not go on cooldown when blocked.
- Slowing Bullets /  Toxic Bullets /  Silencer /  Inhibitor /  Spiritual Overflow: Buildup

Effects partially blocked:

- Headshot Booster /  Headhunter: Blocked by On-Hit Prevention. Always go on cooldown, even when blocked.
- Lucky Shot: Blocked by Deflection.
- Split Shot: Blocked by Deflection.

Effects that are not blocked:

- Armor Piercing Rounds counters Plated Armor, causing bullets to hit and apply their effects. Since both items are chance based, Plated Armor may still block bullets when Armor Piercing Rounds does not trigger.
- Burst Fire
- Crippling Headshot /  Weakening Headshot
- Escalating Resilience
- Hollow Point
- Mercurial Magnum
- Mystic Shot
- Restorative Shot
- Tesla Bullets /  Capacitor

“

I know how to get out of a sticky situation.

**Pocket** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. With a powerful shotgun and highly mobile abilities, they thrive in close encounters. Channelling their magic briefcase to Barrage groups of enemies with spiritual bursts, Pocket may use their sentient cloak to teleport beside their targets and unload their shotgun; disappearing inside their Enchanter's Satchel to avoid return fire. In larger groups, they can unleash an Affliction to slowly eat away at their health, setting their enemies up for a devastating attack.

The eldest heir to Fairfax Industries, Arin "Pocket" Fairfax has been in hiding for over 5 years after a failed assassination attempt. Fearing for their life and wishing to chart their own path, the newly nicknamed Pocket has been keeping their original identity secret while investigating who had tried to kill them.

“

Arin Fairfax, the eldest heir to Fairfax Industries, has been living in hiding for the past 5 years after being shot and left for dead on their 18th birthday.  Arin doesn't know who is trying to keep them from taking control of their parent's company... but in the avarice fueled viper's nest that is Fairfax Industries it could be anyone.

Taking on the name "Pocket", Arin desperately wants to keep their true identity a secret… not only for their own protection; but because they want to forge their own identity separate from their parents.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Pocket was named **Synth** in *Neon Prime*. They were later renamed to **Fairfax**.
- Pocket is voiced by **Greg Chun**, who also voices  Shiv.[1]
- A possible inspiration for Pocket's kit is the hero Puck from *Dota 2*. Besides having similar names, both Pocket and Puck have the abilities to send a slow moving projectile that damages enemies and that they can teleport to, deal AOE burst damage, and become invulnerable for a short time by going into hiding.
- "Sulking in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Pocket in the Hideout.
- Pocket's backstory and abilities have some similarities to the Biblical Plagues of Egypt: the death of the firstborn, the plague of frogs, and the pestilence (Affliction).
- In Pocket's original model, their left hand had an eye tattoo on its back and a decayed skin tissue that glowed with the suitcase.

“

I'll use my family's name when I'm no longer ashamed of it.

Arin Fairfax, the eldest heir to Fairfax Industries, has been living in hiding for the past 5 years after being shot and left for dead on their 18th birthday.  Arin doesn't know who is trying to keep them from taking control of their parent's company... but in the avarice fueled viper's nest that is Fairfax Industries it could be anyone.

Taking on the name "Pocket", Arin desperately wants to keep their true identity a secret… not only for their own protection; but because they want to forge their own identity separate from their parents.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Walter Fairfax statue

Pocket's motivation in the ritual is to stop their father, Maximilian Fairfax,[1][2] and to take control of Fairfax Industries.[3][4]

Pocket believes their father was behind their attempted assasination.[5] Pocket wants to stop their father rather than kill him.[2] Maximilian seems to know that Pocket survived, as in *The Binding of Oathkeeper*, he asks Lady Geist if she knows where Pocket is.[6] Pocket also does not trust their mother.[7]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

A statue of Walter Fairfax, presumably an ancestor of Pocket, can be found in the garden behind the Baroness Hotel. Walter is depicted as an old man with frogs crawling over his legs. The statue also appears in Pocket's background in the hero select screen.

Pocket likely has at least one younger sibling, as their background calls them the "eldest heir" to Fairfax Industries.

Pocket went to Blackmore Academy.[8]

Pocket was betrothed to Mina, implied to be due to an arranged marriage.[9][10][11]

Calico was the assassin hired to kill Pocket, who survived because the bullet missed their heart.[12] It's implied that Enchanter's Satchel also helped Pocket survive.[13][14] Some time after the assassination, Pocket left New York before returning to participate in the ritual.[15][16]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Pocket expresses regret for killing most of their enemies and say they only chose violence as a last resort.[17][18]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Pocket's magical suitcase, while powerful, was never meant to be used as a weapon.[19] Pocket is trying to keep their suitcase away from Maximilian.[20]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Calico

[edit | edit source]

As the assassin hired to kill Pocket, Calico enjoys "tying up loose ends" when she kills Pocket in-game.[21] She also mentions that Maximilian Fairfax will "have questions".[22] Pocket, naturally, dislikes Calico for almost killing them.[23][24]

### Dynamo

[edit | edit source]

Dynamo is Pocket's godfather. He recognizes Pocket and says he would have helped them if he knew they were alive. Pocket didn't tell Dynamo that they survived because they weren't sure if they could trust him.[25][26]

### Mina

[edit | edit source]

Mina hates Pocket for "ruining her life", as their assassination meant Mina couldn't become a Fairfax.[9][10][27]

### Mo & Krill

[edit | edit source]

Mo & Krill protected Pocket after their assassination, and they regard each other as family.[28][29][30] They love each other.[31]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Despite Pocket's desire to hide their true identity, the other characters seem to be aware of their background and refer to them as an "upstart",[32] a "trust fund baby"[33] and a "spoiled brat".[34]
- Pocket loathes McGinnis due to her work for Fairfax Industries.[35][36][37]
- Pocket thinks  Yamato would get along with their mother.[38]
- Pocket says Vyper is more unstable than their parents[39] and is relieved when she is killed, even when both are on the same team.[40]
- Lady Geist recognises Pocket, but mistakes them for a street urchin. She thinks Pocket's jacket is stolen.[41]
- Bebop offers Pocket a place to stay after the ritual.[42]
- Graves, Paradox and Yamato want Pocket's case.[43][44][45]

- Warden warns Pocket that their case will be their undoing.[46]
- According to  Rem, Pocket's clothes smell like the sewer.[47]

### Removed character interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Pocket dislikes Wrecker and wants to dismantle Eldritch Tactical Solutions.[48][49]

[edit | edit source]

In *Neon Prime*, Pocket was named **Synth**. Synth's model was a modified version of *Team Fortress 2'*s Scout with  Holliday's head.

# Powerups

Two Powerup stones in Sandbox mode
Powerup duration icons (all 4 active at once)

**Powerups**, also known as **Bridge Buffs** or **Runes**, are temporary buffs that spawn as a glowing stone on the bridges connecting two buildings near the Urn spawn and dropoff points, starting at 5 minutes and then every 5 minutes thereafter. They require a Heavy Melee Attack to claim.

Powerups are displayed on the Minimap with unique icons indicating their type.

Powerups start weaker and grow stronger (from 5 minutes to 40 minutes). Exact values are the following:

- Casting:

- Starts at +15 Spirit Power and +12% Cooldown Reduction for 160s
- Ends at +65 Spirit Power and +20% Cooldown Reduction for 160s
- Gun:

- Starts at +12% Fire Rate and +35% Ammo for 160s
- Ends at +35% Fire Rate and +70% Ammo for 160s
- Movement:

- Starts at +2 Stamina, +1.5m/s Sprint Speed, +20% Stamina Regeneration Rate, and +40% Zipline Speed for 160s
- Ends at +4 Stamina, +4m/s Sprint Speed, +50% Stamina Regeneration Rate and +80% Zipline Speed for 160s
- Survival:

- Starts at +200 Bonus Health and +4 (fixed) Health Regen for 160s
- Ends at +700 Bonus Health and +40 (fixed) Health Regen for 160s

These temporary stat increases do not appear in the in-game stats, but they are listed as active effects on the left side of the player's HUD. The duration of powerup effects appears in the lower left of the HUD, above the soul count. When another player has the powerup, the icon is shown below their healthbar.

# Pure Damage

Pure Damage from Venator's Ira Domini (grey bar only)

**Pure Damage** is a damage type from Abilities and Items that isn't considered Spirit or Weapon Damage, and thus cannot be mitigated by Damage Resistance or Barriers.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 List of Pure Damage Abilities
- 3 List of Pure Damage Items
- 4 Notes

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Pure Damage appears as white numbers, and a grey bar in the damage report tab.

Some items can function similarly to Pure Damage by bypassing mitigation of their damage type.

Some abilities or items show as Pure Damage (white numbers), however they are a post damage mitigation damage amp, therefore the damage is already reduced once.

Only effects that make the player Invincible can block Pure Damage. Backdoor Protection can also make Structures block Pure Damage.

## List of Pure Damage Abilities

[edit | edit source]

| Hero | Ability | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Billy | Blasted | Post-mitigation damage amp |
| Grey Talon | Guided Owl | T3 execute only (below health threshold) |
| Lady Geist | Soul Exchange |  |
| Shiv | Killing Blow | Execute only (below health threshold) |
| Venator | Consecrating Grenade | Burn damage only |
| Venator | Gutshot | T3 upgrade |
| Venator | Ira Domini | While Blessed only |
| Victor | Jumpstart |  |
| Victor | Aura of Suffering | Self Damage only |

## List of Pure Damage Items

[edit | edit source]

| Name | Cost | Category | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Blood Tribute | **3,200** | Weapon | Self Damage part |
| Siphon Bullets | **6,400** | Vitality |  |
| Focus Lens | **6,400** | Spirit | Post-mitigation damage amp |

- Armor Piercing Rounds and  Tankbuster don't deal Pure Damage (white numbers), but their damage bypasses Weapon and Spirit Resistances, respectively.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Pure Damage does not trigger  Mystic Reverb. If an ability has bonus Pure Damage like the blessed stakes of  Venator's  Ira Domini, it will not be used to calculate the damage of the reverb.
- Pure Damage was added in the Six New Heroes update. Before this, the abilities and items listed dealt Spirit Damage instead.

- Their behavior was similar, bypassing resistances, however some interactions were different, for example Lady Geist's  Soul Exchange worked with  Mystic Reverb.

**Quicksilver Reload** is a Tier 2  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **1,600**.

It is a component of  Mercurial Magnum.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Notable Interactions
- 3 Update history
- 4 Gallery
- 5 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Quicksilver Reload uses Charge-Up.
- Quicksilver Reload's bonus Spirit Damage will only trigger when the imbued ability first deals Weapon Damage or Spirit Damage to the target. If the initial damage is reduced to 0 (rounded down) or only deals Pure Damage (i.e.  Lady Geist's  Soul Exchange), Quicksilver Reload's bonus Spirit Damage is not applied.
- Abilities that do not deal damage still trigger the instant reload and bonus Fire Rate effects.
- The passive buff has a fixed duration of 12 seconds and is **not** affected by cooldown reduction.

## Notable Interactions

[edit | edit source]

Heroes with long reload times and quick-charging or multi-charge abilities can make good usage of Quicksilver:

- McGinnis with multiple turret charges
- Infernus with multiple Napalm charges
- Haze who benefits from maintaining Fixation stacks on targeted enemies
- Vindicta  Crow Familiar has a short cooldown after second upgrade
- Mo & Krill  Scorn has a short cooldown and heals a percent of damage dealt

# Ranked mode

“Farewell, my friends.”

This page contains game content that has been removed from the game.

In-game description of Ranked mode

*For the current rank system, see Skill Rating.*

“

Ranked is a challenge mode that provides a more competitive Deadlock experience where you'll be matchmade with players of similar skill to determine your Skill Rank among the global population.

**Ranked mode** was a game mode in Deadlock for competitive players to compete with other players of similar skill levels. By winning matches and performing well, players could earn badges for their profile depending on the highest rank they achieve.

Medals were updated once per week, requiring at least 7 games played within that week to receive a rank. [1]

Ranked mode was added to the game on October 10, 2024, but was not publicly available until October 15th. Medals were granted the following Tuesday, on October 22nd. The gamemode was removed on November 21st. Ranks still appears in a player's profile as Skill Ratings.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Ranks

- 2.1 Initiate, Rank 1
- 2.2 Seeker, Rank 2
- 2.3 Alchemist, Rank 3
- 2.4 Arcanist, Rank 4
- 2.5 Ritualist, Rank 5

- 2.7 Archon, Rank 7
- 2.8 Oracle, Rank 8
- 2.9 Phantom, Rank 9
- 2.10 Ascendant, Rank 10
- 2.11 Eternus, Rank 11
- 3 Update history
- 4 References

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

The rank badge can be found by viewing the profile. In ranked mode, an additional small icon was displayed when hovering other player's profiles and on the hero's icon in the end game stats.

In order to play, players:

- Had to have 50 games played
- Had to have zero behavior-related restrictions (Voice/text bans, report misuse, etc.)

## Ranks

[edit | edit source]

Players were grouped into the below ranks, with Eternus as the highest and most skilled rank available.

Within each rank, players were further assigned a subrank from I to VI, with VI the highest subrank. The ranks, from lowest to highest were:

## Update history

[edit | edit source]

| Update | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| November 21, 2024 | [ Matchmaking Rework ]    - This update includes a new version of the matchmaker. The matchmaking pools are no longer split between normal and ranked, there is only one primary matchmaking mode and there are no limited hours. |
| October 18, 2024 | - We have adjusted the matchmaking schedule to not be split across many different hours throughout the day, primarily to help address queue times. There will now be a wider continuous, but more concentrated, set of hours that it is enabled in. The schedule is now more simplified as well, as there is no more user selection component. - Ranked now has weekend specific hours (starts 5 hours earlier) - Fixed some regions (South America, Oceania, Asia) that were off by 1-2 hours from their intended times |
| October 10, 2024 | [ Ranked Mode ]    - Added Ranked mode |

“

The Raven flies no more.

— Mirage

**Raven** is an unreleased Hero in *Deadlock*, a Russian operative seeking to re-corporealize Catherine the Great by using cunning and tactics to outwit his opponents. Raven Blindsides his enemies with concussion grenades, launching into the air with an Umbrella maneuver to continue blasting and shooting his target with a bonus for shooting them in the back. Against multiple foes, Raven activates his Revelation relic to punish them for looking in his direction, Cursing those who look too long in the process.

As the Spymaster of the Soviet Empire, "The Raven" has sought every scrap of ancient writing, artifacts, and history in an effort to give the specter of Catherine the Great a body once more. In the Cursed Apple, the Patrons offer him the best chance to achieve his goal.

Raven was added to Hero Labs on December 6, 2024, and removed from the game when the mode was discontinued on August 18, 2025.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

“

Led by the specter of Catherine the Great, the Soviet Empire has flourished in a brave new world of mysticism.  But while her deeper motivations are often obfuscated from the world stage, one thing is for certain: she hates being a ghost.  To this end she has tasked The Empire’s spymaster with one goal: find a way to make her corporeal once more.

Relentless in pursuit of his task; the operative known only as "The Raven" has scoured the Earth looking for strange artifacts, apocryphal writings, and wisdom of the life beyond. Now in New York, Raven looks to find a way to tether Catherine’s spirit to the mortal coil.

### Lore

[edit | edit source]

Raven carries a canopic jar, used by ancient Egyptians to store the soul of the dead in the mummification process.[1] It is used in his ultimate.

Raven mentions Rasputin[2] and the Romanovs.[3]

Raven hopes the OSIC will be cooperative to his plans.[4]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Both Raven and  Paradox claim to be in possession of the Tome of Anubis.  Wraith says she thought the Tome was at the Met.[1][5]

- At some point, the Tome of Anubis was reportedly seen in New York's black market.[6]
- Calico knows Raven and likes him.[7][8]
- Mirage has met Raven before[9] and mentions a conflict between the Soviet Empire and the Djinn.[10]
- Holliday finds Raven handsome.[11]

It is a component of  Indomitable.

## Contents

- 1 Notable interactions
- 2 Sources of Melee Damage

- 2.1 Melee damage abilities
- 3 Update history
- 4 Navigation

## Notable interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Rebuttal procs when parrying  Viscous'  Puddle Punch.
- Rebuttal does not proc when parrying abilities with  Counterspell.

## Sources of Melee Damage

[edit | edit source]

Apart from light and heavy melee attacks, some hero abilities are also considered to deal melee damage. Generally if an ability scales with melee damage, its damage is reduced by Melee Resist.

# Rejuvenator

The Rejuvenator.

The **Rejuvenator** is a single rune that spawns above the Mid-Boss pit after it is slain. It appears as a large, green crystal. After the Mid-Boss is killed, the Rejuvenator descends over 6 seconds and cannot be claimed until it fully touches the ground. Once it lands, any player in the match can hit it with a heavy melee attack, granting the **Rejuvenation Credit** buff to their entire team. Each heavy melee hit grants one Rejuvenator Credit to the team, up to 3. Hitting the Rejuvenator also heals the first player who punched it to full health.

## Contents

- 1 Rejuvenation Credit
- 2 Update history
- 3 Gallery
- 4 Trivia
- 5 References

## Rejuvenation Credit

[edit | edit source]

The Rejuvenation Credit is a team-wide buff granted to all allies when a Rejuvenator crystal is claimed. The buff lasts 4 minutes or until all credits are consumed, whichever comes first.

When there are 30 seconds left on the buff duration, Heroes are warned that it will expire soon.

The buff allows each player to revive with **100%** of their health in the place of their death after **3** seconds. Upon death, the player respawns in place, loses the buff, and their team's Rejuvenator Credits are reduced by 1 (each player can only consume one credit). The top UI bar displays the remaining Rejuvenator Credits, and players who haven't consumed a credit have a highlight below their net worth. When all credits are used, the buff is removed from all team members.

Killing a player with a Rejuvenator credit does not appear as a kill in the HUD and does not grant any souls, but it does trigger "on hero kill" effects such as the cooldown reset of  Shiv's  Killing Blow or the stack buildup of  Grey Talon's,  Mo & Krill's and  Vindicta's ultimates.

# Reload Time

**Reload Time** is the time it takes for a hero to reload their weapon's ammo count.

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Full Reload and Single Reload
- 1.2 Base Reload Time
- 2 Items

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Each weapon has either a **full** or **single** reload type. Using a Melee Attack or Dashing will interrupt the reload until the melee or dash animation is finished.

A notable exception is  Billy, whose reload is not interrupted when performing a light melee attack.

### Full Reload and Single Reload

[edit | edit source]

Most heroes will reload their weapon's entire magazine at once, with a consistent reload time regardless of ammo left.

Abrams' and  Silver's weapons are reloaded one shell at a time, and the reload can be interrupted before it's finished. For these weapons, the time to reload a full magazine depends on how much ammo was left before reloading. These heroes also have a short delay to start reloading after firing their weapon.

There are several items that bypass reloading completely, and will instantly reload the player's weapon.

- Active Reload allows the player to skip 50% of the reload by adding a quick-time event in the reload bar. Active Reload's activation window lasts 0.3s.
- Crushing Fists will restore 15% ammo on a light melee and 30% ammo on a heavy melee.
- Quicksilver Reload and  Mercurial Magnum will reload the player's weapon when using the ability imbued by this item.
- Vampiric Burst will cancel reloading and add 75% base ammo to the player's clip, adding bonus ammo to any amount over the clip capacity.

“

I'm useful, I promise!

**Rem** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. An accidental stowaway from the world of dreams, Rem has found himself stranded in the city that never sleeps. Pillow fights are Rem's preferred form of conflict, tossing his favorite pillow at enemies to knock them back when they're getting too close. His friends, however, he likes to keep nearby - leaping to their aid when things get dicey and taking a quick nap on their shoulder. His Lil Helpers are curious creatures, taking interest in everything the streets of New York have to offer, and cheering on his allies as they go. Ultimately when Naptime hits, no one will be able to keep their eyes open.

A sleepy child from a world of dreams, Rem and his little helpers found themselves stranded in New York. Searching the five boroughs for a way home, Rem seeks to summon the Patrons so he can finally return to his family.

Rem was released on January 26, 2026 as the first winner of the Old Gods, New Blood update contest.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Rem has a secret room in the Hideout that can be accessed by entering the vents behind the news computer or the large statue in the Atrium, then climbing over the boiler machine in the backroom.
- Rem was originally leaked in November 2025 with a screenshot of the character's select screen.[1] On 20th January 2026, Rem was teased in the Hideout with a pillow in a chair.
- Rem's name references Rapid Eye Movement, a unique and active phase of sleep where most dreaming occurs, characterized by fast brain waves, increased heart rate, and rapid, darting eye movements behind closed lids.
- Rem's design trivia

- Base body-design resembles of anthropomorphic wingless / Minoan gryphon / demigryph / keythong.
- Thematically, Rem's clothing gives an impression of a folklore sandman.

- Rem's facial shape resembles a mask of plague doctors.
- Drifting star patterns can be observed on Rem's plumage and inner ears.
- While it hasn't been disclosed what exactly Rem is, there are many possible inspiration sources:

- Rem's ability to "smell" and "taste" dreams could be reference to baku, a nightmare devouring benevolent chimera. There is also a dream-destroying variant of baku.
- Finnish mythology has menninkäinen, a nocturnal daylight-avoiding but otherwise mostly philanthropic spirit combining elements of fairies / sprites, trolls, and nisse / tomte / brownies / leprechauns (not to be confused to "maahinen" which is more human-like / humanoid akin to gnomes or imps).

- The Lil Helpers highlight the curiosity and preference of shiny items.
- Rem has a line where he dreams about mangos,[2] which are the favorite fruit of developer Icefrog and an item in *Dota 2*.[3]
- "Having Sweet Dreams in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Rem in the Hideout.

“

No more sleeping, need to help, then sleep more.

An accidental stowaway from the world of dreams, Rem has found himself stranded in the city that never sleeps.  Driven by his curious nature, Rem and his helpful friends have been seen wandering across the five boroughs in search of a way back home.

So if you ever find yourself dozing off while taking the Blue line home from work, maybe you’ve just had an encounter with one of the Cursed Apple’s newest denizens.

## Contents

- 1.1 Biography

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Rem's motivation in the ritual is to find a way back to his home.[1][2]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Rem's exact species is unknown,[3][4] although he is called a familiar.[5]

Rem can see people's dreams when they're asleep. This allows him to learn information he wouldn't normally know, such as how to speak Ixian,[6] that  Mo wants to audit a pottery class,[7][8] or  Yamato's true name.[9]

Rem has a family who misses him.[10]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

While his age is unknown, Rem is heavily implied to be a child,[11] exhibiting childlike characteristics.[12][13]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Rem molts.[14]

Rem can't read.[15]

Rem brought his lucky pillow to the ritual.[16]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Haze

[edit | edit source]

Haze and Rem are friends.[17][18][19] Haze promised to help Rem get home and dislikes him fighting in the ritual due to the dangers.[20][21]

Rem calls Haze his "mom".[22]

Rem sees Haze when he sleeps and claims that "she's him".[23][24]

Rem seems to have caused Haze some trouble prior to the ritual,[25] but how the two met and how they know each other is currently unknown.

### Billy

[edit | edit source]

Rem thinks Billy could "teach him all kinds of fun words",[26] but also thinks that he should wait until he's older to hang out with Billy.[27]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Rem refers to Grey Talon as "grandpa."[28][29]
- Rem likes Vyper and hopes she could be his "cool aunt."[30][31]
- Rem wants to trade hats with  Infernus.[32]
- Rem calls  Holliday a "sad sheriff with dead sister".[33]

- Seven warns Rem to stay away from anyone who mentions the OSIC, claiming that they won't help Rem get home.[34] Rem finds Seven scary.[35]
- Venator promises to protect Rem and help him get home while they're on the same team.[36][37] If they're on opposing teams, however, Venator believes Rem's putting on a façade and calls him a "furry bastard".[38][39]
- Graves wishes she could make Rem a pet.[40]

# Rescue Beam Slingshot

| Rescue Beam Slingshot |  |
| --- | --- |
| https://deadlock.wiki/File:Rescuebeamslingshot.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Item Tech |
| Difficulty: | Advanced Easy |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Inputs: | Rescue Beam → (Pull) → (Cancel) |

Rescue Beam’s pull is fastest at the start of the pull, after which it decelerates. The further away you are from the puller, the faster you go. At any time during Rescue Beam, you are able to cancel and return to normal.

You can take advantage of the large amounts of speed to slingshot allies across the map by cancelling Rescue Beam just as you start pulling them towards yourself.

The best conditions are for the puller to be as far away as possible, for the puller to immediately cancel once the target starts getting pulled, and for the puller to have some sort of leverage over the target (typically though standing on a higher platform).

To execute, cast Rescue Beam onto an ally. Start pulling, then immediately cancel. They should be slingshotted behind you.

**Rescue Beam** is a Tier 3  Vitality Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**. Its component,  Healing Rite, makes up  **800** of the cost.

## Contents

- 1 Movement
- 2 Notes
- 3 Update history
- 4 Trivia
- 5 Gallery
- 6 Navigation

## Movement

[edit | edit source]

At any range, Rescue Beam will fully pull your target towards you in one second.

The speed that Rescue Beam pulls targets is typically fastest at the start. The peak speed is also dependent on distance between the target and the caster. At the max range of 34 meters, the peak speed is ~1700 u/s. The target will decelerate in speed until next to the caster.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- If self-cast, the item holder cannot pull themselves, and only one of two heals will be received.
- Rescue Beam is a channel, and can be cancelled by Stun and Interrupt if used on the caster, ending the heal and preventing the use of the pull. Targets already being pulled will continue to be pulled.

- Silence does not interrupt Rescue Beam, as it has no effect on items or channels.
- Allies will be moved to the current location of the item holder over the duration of the pull, not where the pull was activated.

# Response Rules

“Let's get started, shall we?”

This article is a stub. You can help the Deadlock Wiki by expanding it.

This page lists triggers for various **voice lines**, also known as **responses**. These triggers are controlled by the game files called **response_rules** and **generated_response_rules**.

## Contents

- 1 Menu

- 1.1 Select
- 1.2 Unselect
- 2 Conversations
- 3 Ability Lines

- 3.1 Upgrade
- 3.2 Use
- 3.3 Use (Low Health)
- 4 Pings

- 4.1 Context Pings
- 4.2 Headed to Lane/Base
- 4.3 See Enemy
- 4.4 Missing Enemy
- 4.5 Warn Ally
- 5 Patrons

- 5.1 Match Start
- 5.2 Big Healing
- 6 Unused Lines

- 6.1 Win and Lose
- 6.2 Pass on zipline
- 6.3 Killed By
- 7 External Links

## Menu

[edit | edit source]

### Select

[edit | edit source]

Select lines are played when selecting a Hero to search for a match, or increasing a Hero's matchmaking priority.

### Unselect

[edit | edit source]

Unselect lines are played when unselecting a Hero before searching for a match, or reducing a Hero's matchmaking priority.

## Conversations

[edit | edit source]

Conversations are played in the zipline at the start of the match. If a conversation is incomplete, only the first line is played. If the Hero has no conversations with their lane partner, a Patron Match Start line is played instead.

## Ability Lines

[edit | edit source]

### Upgrade

[edit | edit source]

Upgrade lines are played when unlocking and upgrading abilities.

### Use

[edit | edit source]

Usage lines are played when using an ability.

### Use (Low Health)

[edit | edit source]

Variation of Usage lines, played when the Hero has less than 20% health. Labeled as "desperation".

## Pings

[edit | edit source]

**Pings** or **voice commands** are lines played when the player marks a location, another player, or wants to send a message to their team. Pings also appear as text messages.

Pings are triggered by pressing Mouse 3, holding Mouse 3 to open the Chat Wheel menu, or holding Tab and clicking on the map with Mouse 1 or clicking on another player's portrait or items with Mouse 3.

The Chat Wheel menu can be customized in settings.

### Context Pings

[edit | edit source]

Context Pings are a unique option in the Chat Wheel that shows a ping based on the player's current state in the game, or as a response to another player's ping or actions. Various pings can appear as context pings.

### Headed to Lane/Base

[edit | edit source]

The player can ping where they are going by aiming at the location and clicking Mouse 3, selecting the option in the Chat Wheel, or holding Tab and clicking in the map close to the location they want to go. It appears as a context ping when riding a zipline to the lane or to the base. Using line of sight or clicking on the map shows a green arrow at the marked location.

### See Enemy

[edit | edit source]

An enemy's location can be pinged by aiming at the enemy and clicking Mouse 3, or clicking at the enemy's icon in the Minimap. This will also highlight the enemy in red for the player and allies.

### Missing Enemy

[edit | edit source]

A missing enemy can be pinged by holding Tab and clicking Mouse 3 at the enemy's portrait.

### Warn Ally

[edit | edit source]

An ally can be warned of danger by aiming at them and clicking Mouse 3, or holding Tab and clicking at their portrait or Minimap icon with Mouse 3.

## Patrons

[edit | edit source]

### Match Start

[edit | edit source]

Patrons' Match Start lines are played in the zipline at the beginning of the match. They are hero-specific.

### Big Healing

[edit | edit source]

Big Healing lines are played when a Hero has healed its allies for a total of 5000 HP.

## Unused Lines

[edit | edit source]

### Win and Lose

[edit | edit source]

Win and Lose are lines in which the Heroes react to either winning or losing the match. There are specific lines for winning or losing short games (less than 30 minutes) and long games (more than 50 minutes).

### Pass on zipline

[edit | edit source]

"Pass on zipline" lines are intended to be played when two ally Heroes cross paths on a zipline. Based on the context, the Hero who says it is going back to the base.

### Killed By

[edit | edit source]

"Killed By" lines were responses to being killed by specific enemy Heroes. These lines were only present in *Neon Prime*.

**Return Fire** is a Tier 2  Vitality Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **1,600**.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- **Damage Reflection Mechanics**

- Returns the attacker's **pre-mitigation** damage (original damage before your resistances apply)

- Example: If an enemy deals 100 Bullet Damage while you have 30% Bullet Resist, you reflect 65 damage, and you take 70.
- Works even with 100% damage immunity (e.g.,  Metal Skin reflects full damage while preventing damage to the user).
- Does not apply build-up or stacking effects against the attacker.

# Ropes

A rope on Greenwich

Ropes are climbable entities in the game that can be grabbed onto by pressing the jump key. If a player is hit by a melee attack while on a rope, they are slowed by 80%, which ramps down to 20% over 2s.

If a Hero has taken damage from another Hero in the last 4s, they will climb ropes 40% slower, which tapers off to 0% in the last second.

Ropes are often located next to buildings that have Jungle camps on their rooftops.

# Scaling

**Scaling** refers to Stats or properties of Abilities and Items that increase incrementally based on another stat.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Scaling is represented by a number next to the scaling icon, which indicates how much the stat is multiplied by. The scaling value is added to the stat's base value. The player can see how much value is added by the scaling by holding Tab or Alt.

Most scaling properties have effects based on the stat they scale from. However, there may be exceptions such as  Paradox's  Kinetic Carbine, which scales off Weapon Damage but deals Spirit Damage.

## List of scaling types

[edit | edit source]

- Boon scaling
- Spirit Power scaling
- Weapon Damage scaling
- Melee Damage scaling

**Seasonal events** are temporary events in *Deadlock* to celebrate holidays.

## Halloween

[edit | edit source]

The 2024 Halloween event ran from October 31 to November 7. The 2025 Halloween event ran from October 24 to November 12.

It added 4 Halloween masks for heroes and pumpkin models for boxes, statues and Denizens. The Halloween masks were randomized.

### Gallery

[edit | edit source]

- Halloween masks
- Heroes wearing Halloween masks
- Heroes wearing Halloween masks
- Halloween Jungle Denizens

## Winter

[edit | edit source]

### 2025

[edit | edit source]

Winter 2025 souvenir

The 2025 Winter event ran from December 15 to January 20.

During the event, all players received a unique Snowball item that could be leveled up by winning matches with different Heroes, which also unlocked ornaments for the Christmas tree in the Hideout. Players who participated in the Winter challenge also unlocked a souvenir above their fireplace in the Hideout.

The Shopkeeper also received new holiday-themed lines for all heroes, and Drifter has holiday-themed songs when using Eternal Night.

### 2024

[edit | edit source]

2024 Winter main menu

The 2024 Winter event ran from December 17 to January 17.

It added a new main menu animation, remixed music for the menu and shops, and Winter-themed decorations in the streets, buildings, and Curiosity Shop. The Shopkeeper featured a Santa mask and unique lines. In addition, the Denizens were modelled after snowmen. Dynamo and the Newscaster had unique holiday voice lines.

All the mainline Heroes received unique Winter skins, which could be unlocked by completing their respective challenge. A list of which skins were unlocked during the event can be seen in the "Showcase" tab in the player's profile, next to the "Match History" button. Players who participated in the Winter challenge also unlocked a snow globe above their fireplace in the Hideout.

#### Skin challenges

[edit | edit source]

As the winter skin challenges weren't listed in-game or in patch notes, the challenges were discovered and shared by the player community over the duration of the event.

These challenges could be achieved only in a normal match or a labs match, not in a custom game or against bots. The conditions for each challenge must be completed in **one match.**

Winter skins were tracked in-game by a Santa hat icon in the main menu that showed how many skins had already been unlocked. Heroes with Winter skins had the Santa hat icon and a red background in the Heroes page.

The skins can be tested in sandbox mode or custom games (with cheats enabled) with the console commands ent_fire player setbodygroup hat,1 and ent_fire player setbodygroup xmas,1.

| Bebop | Reach 100 bomb stacks |

“

The masses will fall.

**Seven** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. A visionary who aims to continuously grow his power, Seven excels in rapidly taking control of the battlefield by denying areas with Lightning Balls and Surging his gun to punish his foes for staying close together. After showing his enemies their place with Static Charge, Seven is free to discharge himself into a Storm Cloud and fry them like a microwave casserole.

It is unknown what actions led to Seven being imprisoned within Lost Whisper. However, Seven managed to turn what was meant to be his execution into the bloody murder of his captors. Finally free and waiting within the underbelly of the Cursed Apple, he wishes to reach "apotheosis" by completing the ritual.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Seven/Lore** for more story content.*

“

When mystic energy awoke on Earth, the world changed... anything was possible.  But just because anything WAS possible, didn’t mean that anything SHOULD be possible.  And so the government made rules.   Laws.  A means for US citizens to enjoy the benefits of the supernatural world in safety.  But rules and laws are for lesser men.  Men with limitations.  Men who were not Seven.  

There are many rumors about what Seven did to land himself in Lost Whisper, an oubliette for the most dangerous of occultists.  But there is no doubt about what happened on the night of his execution. 

Wards placed by the most powerful ritualists of 7 different nations… wards designed to not just prevent mystical interference with the execution, but to simultaneously obliterate Seven's soul so that it could never be contacted, resurrected, or otherwise be used by someone looking to follow in his footsteps... failed.

Onlookers viewed in horror as the strongest mentalist employed by the US Army’s head popped like a grape.  They screamed as Scotland Yard’s premiere occult investigator, the one who allegedly captured Seven, crumbled to ash.  Seven's body buckled and writhed against his restraints; his skin burning from eldritch electricity... and yet he would not die.  He laughed.

He laughed as he tore himself free from his bondage.

He laughed as his captors cowered in fear.

He laughed as he massacred his tormentors.

He laughed as he tasted the fresh air that was denied to him for years.

And he laughed when he thought about what he was going to do once he reached New York City.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Seven was named **Gigawatt** in *Neon Prime*.
- Seven's chestplate has numbers that form a Gorowase, a form of Japanese wordplay with numbers. 4279 can be read as Shi (4) Ni (2) Na (7) Ku (9) = Shininaku (死になく), or "Become unkillable" (rough translation).
- Seven's name may be a reference to Numerology, in which the number 7 is associated with spirituality and the search for knowledge.[2]
- Seven was the only hero with a limping animation which played when he was low on health. This has since been removed.
- "Plotting in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Seven in the Hideout.
- Seven's character select line *"With these hands I will destroy, and with these hands I will rebuild"* is a quote from the song *The Good Doctor* by The Protomen.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Seven's motive and wish in the ritual is to achieve "apotheosis",[1] which means the glorification of a subject to divine level,[2] meaning that Seven wants to become a god, or gain godlike powers.[3][4]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Seven claims he was imprisoned in Lost Whisper because he "offended small-minded simpletons with fragile egos".[5] Seven implies getting caught and sent to Lost Whisper was part of his plan.[6] How Seven survived the botched execution is unknown, but he was implied to have died in the process, which could mean he's undead.[7]

Seven has done research on the Astral Gates, and he credits  Professor Dynamo as an influence in his work.[8]

Seven mentions that he once loved someone.[9] According to the Archmother, Seven had a "destiny" which his lover tried to steal.[10]

The OSIC wants Seven dead.[11] They seem to know that Seven is in New York, as Seven is hiding from them in New York's subway tunnels.[12]

Seven mentions that he had to "scurry with the rats since he was a child".[13]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Seven says he doesn't like murder, rather, he is "indifferent" to it.[14] He does enjoy letting fear sink into his victims, however.[15]

Seven believes he will become powerful enough for the Patrons to bow to him.[16]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Seven can speak the Ixian language.[17][18]

The New York Oracle reporter Allie Kincaid is writing a story on Seven.[19][20]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Kelvin

[edit | edit source]

Seven has a one-sided hatred towards Kelvin for unknown reasons.[21][22][23]

Kelvin thinks Seven "seems familiar".[24] When being healed by Kelvin, Seven is reminded of "old times".[25]

Both Seven and Kelvin have an interest on researching Astral Gates.[26][27]

Seven believes Kelvin has a bigger ego than  Lash.[28]

A likely possibility is that Seven is Kelvin's old friend Ettrick, who "vanished".  Lady Geist says Ettrick "caused a scene" at one of Kelvin's fundraisers.[29] This is supported by one of Seven's lines to Kelvin that mirrors one of Kelvin's lines about Ettrick.[30][31] Kelvin pushed Ettrick away due to his "ambition", which aligns with Seven's ambition to achieve apotheosis.[32] Seven also believes that mentors "use the young to achieve glories they could not achieve on their own", possibly referring to Kelvin.[33]

-The Doorman(?)

-Rem(?)

-Paradox(?)

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Seven has a strong conviction that exceptional magic users should use their powers, regardless of how others might judge them for it. He criticizes  Dynamo for wanting to "throw away" the "great gift" of his star form,[34] teases  Infernus for "putting on a muzzle" and "wasting" his powers,[35][36] criticizes  Celeste for masking her power at a sideshow,[37] and says  McGinnis is "wasting her brilliance" working for Fairfax Industries.[38]

- Seven respects  Ivy for "seeing the world as it was and deciding it was not acceptable to her".[39]
- Seven wants to commission  Paradox for a job.[40]
- Seven knows that  The Doorman isn't normal and wants to uncover his secrets.[41][42]
- Seven warns  Graves that her mentor is using her to "live glories they could not achieve on their own".[35] He also warns Graves that the path she's on will eventually get her killed. Seven warns Graves because he "hates to see talent wasted".[43]

- Graves would like to be Seven's "intern".[44]
- Seven warns  Rem to stay away from anyone who mentions the OSIC, claiming that they won't help Rem get home.[45] Rem finds Seven scary.[46]
- When on the same team, Seven teases  Haze for working alongside him and asks how soon will they start fighting each other once the ritual is over.[47][48]
- McGinnis offers help to remove Seven's headgear.[49]
- Paradox is aware of Seven's safehouse in the tunnels and threatens to reveal their location.[50]
- Paige swears she won't let her brother turn out like Seven.[51]
- The Doorman thinks Seven is more delusional than  Lash.[52]
- According to  Rem, Seven smells like "evil s'mores".[53] This contrasts  Kelvin's scent of "nice s'mores."[54]

# Seventh Moon

“

I knew a guy who owed the Seventh Moon a C-Note... Yamato murdered the shit out of him.

— Vyper

The Seventh Moon are a Japanese criminal organisation led by Yamato.

To make this page easier to read, Yamato (the playable hero) is referred to by her real name:  Kaori.

## Contents

- 1 Summary
- 2 Members

- 2.1 Yamato: The Brother
- 3 Trivia
- 4 References

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

The Seventh Moon was once a powerful crime family in Japan, led by siblings  Kaori and Yamato. The two siblings were born into power, and took over the organisation once their father died. With Yamato's dreams of expanding the Seventh Moon to the United States, the two siblings made a plan where Kaori would stay in Japan while Yamato would set up an international presence in America. However, several insecure underlings disliked the idea of being led by Kaori in Japan. This resulted in a brutal coup, where Yamato sacrificed himself to ensure Kaori and a small group of loyalists could escape to America. With a fraction of the power she once held, Kaori took up her brother's name and committed herself to rebuilding the Seventh Moon's might in America.[1]

The strength of the Seventh Moon is a fraction of the power it once held in Japan. While the status of the Seventh Moon in Japan is unknown, it's implied to have been dismantled.[2]

Kaori's wish in the ritual is to make the Seventh Moon powerful enough to control New York.[3][4]

Kaori intends to challenge the other criminal organisations in New York in the Seventh Moon's rise to power.[5] She is grateful to  Ivy for dismantling the Mendoza Syndicate[6] and sees  Wraith as her final hurdle to conquering New York.[7]

The Seventh Moon are small enough for the OSIC to not bother allocating resources to dismantle the gang, but they are keeping an eye on things in case the Seventh Moon gets too strong.[8][9]

## Members

[edit | edit source]

- Yamato - Deceased leader
- Kaori (now named Yamato) - Leader

### Yamato: The Brother

[edit | edit source]

Kaori's brother Yamato (not to be confused with the playable Yamato) was one of the co-leaders of the Seventh Moon before he lost his life saving Kaori from a coup. The goal of expanding the Seventh Moon to America was Yamato's dream.[1][10]

Kaori's ultimate ability (Shadow Transformation) is Kaori infusing Yamato's shadow soul with herself.[11][12]

According to Kaori, Yamato had a "useless" body guard.[13]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Seventh Moon in Japanese Katakana is spelt "セブンスムーン".
- Vyper is the only hero who shows any interest in joining the Seventh Moon.[14]
