# Shadowline

“Farewell, my friends.”

This page contains game content that has been removed from the game.

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Guide_the_map_welcome.mp3Shadowline tutorial narration

***Shadowline*** was an early development version of *Deadlock*.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Mentions
- 3 Caldera_trooper
- 4 References

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Not much is known about *Shadowline*. It existed at some point in the transition from *Neon Prime* to *Deadlock*, in 2022-2023. The web domain *playshadowline.com* and twitter account *@PlayShadowline* were registered in November 2023. It is assumed to be the first version to use the 20th Century American occult setting.

In this version, the ziplines were called "shadowlines",[1] and Astral Gates were "shadowline nexus". The shadowlines were based on ley lines.

## Mentions

[edit | edit source]

- The Shopkeeper narrated an old version of the tutorial that refers to the game as *Shadowline.*[2][1]
- Kelvin may reference a shadowline when upgrading his Ice Path.[3]
- In Viscous' background, the Bermuda Triangle Astral Gate is described as a "shadowline nexus".

## Caldera_trooper

[edit | edit source]

**Caldera_trooper** was a map found in early builds of *Deadlock* that presumably started development during the *Shadowline* period. It had a similar layout to *Neon Prime's* map, but with new lighting and assets from what would later become the Cursed Apple. Caldera_trooper was last compiled in July 2023.

# Shelly Fisher

Ms. Shelly in *The Binding of Oathkeeper*

“

If you knew anything about me, you'd know I traffic in creation, not death.

— Ms. Shelly

**Shelly Fisher**, also known as **Ms. Shelly** or **Miss Shelly**, is a widowed junk yard attendant. She created  Bebop to assist her in her work and to be the son she could never have.[1]

## Summary

[edit | edit source]

Shelly Fisher is an elderly black woman with grey hair and glasses.[2]

Ms. Shelly has fallen ill and Bebop has turned to pit fighting in order to pay for her medication. While Ms. Shelly's exact illness is unknown, it's implied that modern medicine can't save her.[3] While not eager to die, Ms. Shelly was content with her life and has accepted her eventual death.[4]

Bebop's motivation and wish in the ritual is to cure Shelly Fisher of her illness.[5][6] He views Ms. Shelly as his "mother".[7] Shelly doesn't know Bebop is a pit fighter, and he believes she wouldn't approve of his activities.[1] Shelly Fisher is resting at home during the in-game ritual.[8]

Ms. Shelly's creation of Bebop is described as "an act of craftsmanship, willpower and sacrifice". Shelly created Bebop without any bindings (rules to keep Bebop under control) because she "doesn't believe in that sort of thing".[9] McGinnis is impressed by the craftsmanship used to create Bebop and shows interest in hiring Ms. Shelly to work at Fairfax Industries.[10]

Ms. Shelly is a fan of Jazz, which was the inspiration for the name Bebop.[11]

Ms. Shelly's doctor is Johann Geist Jr.,  Lady Geist's grandson.[12]

“

There's a whole lotta people that don't got enough knifes stuck in 'em.

**Shiv** is a Hero in *Deadlock*. He is a monster hunter with a cause, conducting hit-and-run attacks and picking off vulnerable targets. Flinging Serrated Knives to bleed his targets from range, Shiv builds his Rage through damage and dashes up to his enemy with a Slice and Dice flurry of blades and a few powerful shotgun blasts. Withstanding grievous damage via Bloodletting, Shiv hunts down any dying targets to finish them off with a devastating Killing Blow.

A former criminal, Shiv seeks to make up for his past mistakes by hunting down monsters on behalf of The Baxter Society.

Shiv was added to the roster on August 15, 2024.

- After activating Killing Blow, the targeted hero is able to heal up to 3% of their max health, and still be instantly killed.

### Rage

[edit | edit source]

After unlocking Shiv's **Killing Blow** ultimate, rage can be built by dealing any damage. The amount of rage built varies depending on the source.

Rage has a **max value of 10** which is required to be filled before becoming **Enraged**, granting you the full rage bonuses.

| Damage type | Rage built per damage dealt |
| --- | --- |
| Weapon Damage | 0.0158766 |
| Spirit Damage | 0.01452864 |
| Light melee | 1.55664 |
| Heavy melee | 2.85384 |

Rage will begin to decay after **12 seconds** of not dealing any damage, at a rate of 0.25 per second (43 seconds total).

Rage only builds up from damage dealt to players (this includes Barriers).

NOTE: These numbers are taken from the code for the game, but rage built per damage does not actually reflect in game values.

As a rule of thumb: Rage built from **Weapon Damage** and **Melee Damage** does not noticeably change with increases to weapon or spirit power, always taking roughly 18 shots at point blank or 4-7 Melee attacks (depending on strength) to build max rage. Rage built from **Spirit Damage** does scale with spirit power granting more rage the more damage your abilities do, however this is offset by the rage you build decreasing with spirit power, 100 Spirit power halving the rage built  (Imbued spirit power from Surge of Power is not counted towards this, causing it to grant a lot more rage (to the imbued ability) than Boundless Spirit.)

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Shiv has an alternate model in the game files titled **"shiv_ult.vmdl_c"** which shows an unfinished giant mole transformation, presumably meant for an old ultimate ability.
- Shiv is voiced by **Greg Chun**, who also voices  Pocket.[1]
- In now removed voice lines, the Patrons said that Shiv "had been" a father[2] and had a "monster inside him" called "The Beast".[3] These lines were removed in the Old Gods, New Blood update.
- Shiv used to collect hairspray cans in Neon Prime, presumably as an old version of his Rage passive ability.
- Shiv's pre-release ultimate ability, **Haunt** was nearly identical to Lifestealer's Infest ability from *Dota 2* and had him become surrounded by bats before leaping inside an enemy hero.
- Shiv's weapon name, the **Busted Flush**, is a hand in Poker of four cards of the same suit (colour and type) and one of a different suit. It's also an expression referring to a promising thing that ends up failing its potential.
- Shiv carries an amulet on his hip with a design similar to the blood key from the movie *Demon Knight*.[4] The amulet glows red when Shiv is at full Rage.
- "Playing With Knives in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Shiv in the Hideout.
- Bloodletting allows Shiv to tank the instant kill damage from  Killing Blow if it is copied by  Sinclair, and the lethal damage of the Street Brawl item   Unstable Concoction.

This page is under construction. To avoid edit conflicts, please consult the edit history and the talk page.

A loyal member of "The Baxter Society", an international order of monster hunters, Shiv travels across North America looking to put down creatures that prey on the living.

While his less polished nature and criminal past make some of the more traditional members of the Society wary, no one can deny his effectiveness.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Shiv is fighting in the ritual on behalf of the Baxter Society.[1][2] His wish is unknown, but Shiv's motivation is to prove his worth to  Grey Talon and the Baxter Society.[3][4][5]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Not much is known about Shiv's criminal past from before he joined the Baxter Society. The Hidden King calls Shiv's past "bloody",[6] Paige calls Shiv a "man with a tortured past",[7] and the Venators of St. Benedict are keeping an eye on Shiv in case he strays from the path of redemption.[8] Shiv's claims that the Baxter Society "saved his life",[9] and his change of heart seems to be genuine.[10]Shiv was chosen by Grey Talon as his replacement in the Baxter Society.[11][12][13] He has been in the Society for "a few years" and says he is not respected by the other members.[14] Shiv worries that the Baxter Society would eventually turn on him,[15][16] as they still doubt that he's changed from his past.[17] It's implied that Shiv feels lonely.[18]

Shiv allegedly "took something that doesn't belong to him".[19]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Shiv likes to go bowling and drink bourbon.[20][21] He is also referred to as a biker.[22]

Shiv hates cats.[23]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Grey Talon

[edit | edit source]

Grey Talon has high hopes for Shiv, despite his criminal past, and holds him in high regard, placing Shiv in the top 8 of people he'd want fighting alongside him.[17][24] While the conversations are unfinished, Grey Talon seems to defend Shiv's change of heart from Silver and Venator's doubts.[25][8]

### Drifter

[edit | edit source]

Drifter knew Shiv before he joined the Baxter Society.[26] If he kills Shiv, he calls him a "disappointment" and mentions that killing him feels "Shakespearean".[27][28][29] He also mentions that, had Shiv not "put himself in a muzzle, maybe he'd be worried".[30] When hunting Shiv, he refers to himself as an "old friend".[31] How Shiv and Drifter met each other is unknown.

### Silver

[edit | edit source]

Silver loathes Shiv with a passion and refuses to believe he could change from his criminal past.[32][33] She believes he deserves a fate worse than death.[34] How Silver and Shiv met each other and why Silver hates Shiv is currently unknown.

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Multiple characters compliment Shiv's appearance, calling him "pretty boy",[35] "handsome bastard",[36] "impossibly handsome asshole",[37] and a "shampoo ad with knives".[38]
- Shiv respects Holliday and offers her a place at the Baxter Society.[39] If they're on opposing teams, Shiv promises to kill the Troubadour on Holliday's behalf.[40] Shiv loves Holliday's hat.[41]
- Shiv respects Lash's moxie.[42]
- Venator doesn't believe in Shiv's change of heart, waiting for him to slip up and ruin his "charade".[43][44]
- Lady Geist calls Shiv attractive and asks to have a drink with him after the ritual.[45]
- Ivy expresses admiration for Shiv.[46]  McGinnis wants to talk to Shiv and "fix him".[47][48]  Yamato will simply remark "nice hair".[49]
- Haze and Vyper respect Shiv's taste in knives.[50][51]
- Celeste "doesn't get the appeal" of Shiv and says he has "ruined a lot of lives".[52][53]
- Paige thinks Shiv pulls off the "bad boy thing" better than Lash does.[54] Paige likes Shiv, although she prefers Mirage.[55]

## Removed Lore

[edit | edit source]

In removed voice lines, the Patrons said that Shiv "had been" a father[56] and had a "monster inside him" called "The Beast".[57] These lines were removed in the Old Gods, New Blood update.

# Shopkeeper

The Shopkeeper in the Curiosity Shop in-game.

“

I don't know what that does, but my kid says all the mystics are buying it!

— The Shopkeeper

The **Shopkeeper** is a character in game who mans The Curiosity Shop stall and sells items to players.

The Shopkeeper has specific voice lines triggered by buying certain items, or for the player's hero when they buy a T4 item.

The Shopkeeper is voiced by Jason Keller,[1] who also voices the Newscaster.

## Lore

[edit | edit source]

The Shopkeeper has a wife and kid, implying that he has a mortal body.[2][3] The Shopkeeper's kid is implied to be old enough to go to Columbia College.[4]

The Shopkeeper is a big fan of the New York Knickerbockers basketball team and dislikes their rivals, the Celtics.[5][6][7] While a fan of the Knickerbockers, it's implied that the Shopkeeper broke the legs of a Knickerbocker player for owing him money.[8][9]

The Shopkeeper plays in Wraith's weekly poker games, although he needs permission from his wife to play.[10][11] He describes himself as a "degenerate gambler".[12] Wraith also has a marker on him.[13]

The Shopkeeper has been robbed by Vyper in the past.[14] Despite this, he still likes Vyper and considers her "his kind of scumbag".[15]

The Shopkeeper dislikes Santa Claus.[16]

# Shrine

| Shrine |  |
| --- | --- |
| Stats |  |
| Health |  |
| Base Health: | 5000 |
| Bullet Resist: | 60% |
| Damage |  |

**Shrines** are defensive Structures located in pairs within each team's base. They are the final objectives that must be destroyed before the Patron can be damaged.

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Durability
- 2 Destruction
- 3 Gallery
- 4 Update history
- 5 Trivia
- 6 References

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

The Hidden King shrine resembles a speaker tower with three large loudspeakers and three smaller ones, all mounted on an inscribed hexagonal platform with a candle placed at each point. A glowing magical symbol sits at the center of the speakers. The shrine is primarily colored orange to match the Hidden King’s theme, and it faces the Hidden King patron, appearing to transmit sound waves toward it.

In contrast, the Archmother shrine takes the form of a blue-lit platform, fitting the Archmother theme, topped by a book stand holding a magical tome. A hexagon is also inscribed on the platform, surrounded by magical sigils and inscriptions. The book periodically flips open and appears to emit magical energy directed toward the Archmother patron.

Shrines are found in pairs within each team's base, located on opposite sides to each other. The Patron will defend any that are under attack with a beam that deals damage and curses players in or near the Shrine platform. Shrines have 5000 Health.

### Durability

[edit | edit source]

Shrines have 10% Bullet Resist.

Additionally, like Base Guardians, Shrines have scaling Bullet Resist. It starts at 60%, losing 20% per enemy hero nearby, up to 0% minimum. They are also immune to damage from any source outside their platform.

| Nearby Enemy Heroes | Bullet Resist |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | 60% |
| 1 | 40% |
| 2 | 20% |
| 3 | 0% |
| 4 | 0% |
| 5 | 0% |
| 6 | 0% |

When Backdoor Protection is active, they have 65% Damage Resist and 65 Health Regen per second.

## Destruction

[edit | edit source]

Once both Shrines have been destroyed, the enemy Patron will become vulnerable to damage. Allied Troopers also become **Super Troopers** and gain 60% damage and 40% health for the lane in which the Shrine was destroyed, and for the Blue lane when either Shrine has been destroyed, for the rest of the match. They also yield 15% less souls when killed.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Latin inscription on the throneThe backrest of the throne in the old shrine, as well as the sign worn by the Guardian, featured the following Latin text

EN SACRIFICIUM CUSTOS LAPIDIS CORDE DIVINO OBLATUM TESTAMENTUM IN  CHORO VIRTUTIS ET OBSEQUIL IN UMBRIS HUIUS THRONI RESONAT LEGATUM  EORUM QUI AUSI SUNT CAELOS LACES SERE SOLUM INVENIRE FORTUNAM IN  SACRIFICIO DESINATAM. HIC THRONUS MEMORIALE STET OPORTET ET POTEN  TISSIMUM ORDINEM COELESTE ADORARE

In English this approximately translates to

Behold the sacrifice, the guardian of the stone offered with a divine heart—a testament.  In the chorus of virtue and obedience, in the shadows of this throne, resounds the legacy of those who dared to challenge the heavens, only to find fortune destined in sacrifice.   This throne must stand as a memorial, and it is fitting to worship the most powerful celestial order.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Silencer's Damage Reduction Debuff effect on Spirit Damage will apply to enemy players with Unstoppable activated; But only the *Damage Debuff* portion is applied, the Silenced aspect will not take effect.

## Buildup Per Shot

[edit | edit source]

The item has a different buildup per shot depending on which hero purchased the item. The status only triggers once a buildup reaches 100% on an enemy player, and the buildup decays back to 0 if an enemy hasn't been shot for some time. Melee attacks count as 1 shot.

Once Silenced, subsequent shots have no effect until the victim's immunity expires.

**Warning:** Display title "Silver (Transformed)" overrides earlier display title "Silver".

**Silver** is a Hero in *Deadlock*, making her living tracking down lowlifes, but today New York’s misanthrope lycanthrope plans on summoning a god. Fortunately, her career as a bounty hunter has prepared her well for all that the ritual requires. She makes quick work of adversaries by catching them with her Entangling Bola, Boot Kicking them in the face, and finishing them off with a Slam Fire from her rifle. But inevitably, the Lycan Curse comes calling whether she likes it or not, and her foes will regret being too close when it does.

Lilah Silver has been a werewolf for as long as she can remember, insisting that she has her Lycanthropy under control. Despite her successes as a bounty hunter, Silver struggles with alcohol, smoking, financial, and personal troubles on a daily basis, driving her to seek the Patron's help to "thrive".

Silver was released on February 2, 2026 as the third winner of the Old Gods, New Blood update contest.

42 Damage Per Second

Hair of the Dog reloads single shots and the reload can be interrupted.

**Loose Muzzle**

Spreadshot

Medium Range

50 Damage Per Second

Falloff Range

N/A

Loose Muzzle only hits enemies in melee range, in a cone-shaped attack that can hit multiple enemies. The range cannot be increased by items such as  Sharpshooter. It has no ammo count and no reload, and does not deal headshot damage. It does proc Weapon item effects such as  Ricochet.

Split Shot has no effect on Loose Muzzle.

## Abilities

[edit | edit source]

Silver is unique among heroes in having two distinct sets of abilities — one for her default (human) form and one for her transformed (werewolf) form — which swap automatically when Lycan Curse transforms her. Her ultimate, Lycan Curse, is shared between both forms and triggers the transformation.

### Lycan Curse

LYCAN CURSE

Active: Instantly transform, gaining increased   max health, and stacking   fire rate on enemy heroes, and replacing your abilities and weapon with their ferocious versions.

On Hero Kill: Refresh abilities, duration, and transformation heal

Notes

- The passive feature has a short delay before automatically casting Lycan Curse once bloodlust is full. The player can press the ability button to transform instantly during that delay.
- Damage dealt to NPCs does not count towards Lycan Curse. However, it does generate the 1% passive buildup in combat.
- After Lycan Curse ends, Silver's weapon is automatically reloaded.
- Lycan Curse's cooldown does not begin until the transformation ends.
- Buildup notes:

- Lycan Curse bloodlust builds 0.255% per damage dealt.
- Whenever Silver is below 30% health, the bloodlust buildup is increased by +40%. This additional buildup grows by +1.8% per Boon (additively), making it +103% at max level. This bonus is applied retroactively to the existing buildup when Silver reaches the health threshold.
- The base required amount of hero-damage inflicted (not counting low health bonus) to charge Lycan Curse is 392. The damage required increases by +9.4% per Boon (additively), making it 613 at level 6 when the ultimate is unlocked, and 1682 at max level.
- Lycan Curse bloodlust also passively builds up 1% per second in combat, effectively lowering the damage required.

- Buildup is lost at the rate of -3% per second when out of combat.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- During development, Silver was originally codenamed **Shapeshifter**, whose name was leaked in November 2025.[3]
- Silver had a scrapped ability where she tracked bounties during the match, as indicated by unused voicelines still in the files.
- The name of Silver's weapon, **Hair of the Dog**, is a shortening of the expression *Hair of the Dog that Bit You*, referring to alcohol consumed to lessen the effect of a hangover.
- Silver is the first hero to possess a weapon without a traditional projectile or ranged option, as her primary fire in Werewolf form swings her claws to maim enemies in melee range. She's also the first hero to have two sets of abilities.
- "Figuring What Happened Last Night in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Silver in the Hideout.
- Silver's name could be an ironic reference to the fact that silver is a common weakness to werewolves.

- The word "silver" is a common component-word primarily to describe appearance of non-human specimen (E.G. silver back, silver fang, etc.).
- Silver's release date, February 2, 2026, was under a full moon, a common association with werewolves.
- Silver's hairstyle is known as a Wolf Cut, originally known as a  *Shag*.

“

I'm gonna be washing a whole lotta blood out of my fur tonight.

Lilah Silver is a mess.  She drinks too much, she smokes too much, and the less is said about her personal life the better.   But despite Silver's flaws she has managed to carve out a career as a successful bounty hunter, and while she would like to think that her successes are solely because she has incredible intuition, the fact that she’s a werewolf doesn’t hurt.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Silver's goal in the ritual is to get money and sort her life out.[1][2][3][4]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Silver has been a werewolf for as long as she can remember.[5]

Silver claims to have her Lycanthropy under control.[6] However, Silver seems unable to control her transformation due to it triggering automatically in-game without her compliance.[7]

Silver tries to take bounties in alive, although her methods usually end up killing them.[8] She's brought  Vyper into custody on several occasions and is after a bounty on The Troubadour.[9][10]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Silver hates her life and is aware of her self-destructive tendencies.[11][12] While she doesn't love being a bounty hunter, she believes she isn't good at anything else and would end up homeless if she didn't do a job that paid well.[13][14]

Silver has a habit of spending all of her money on rent or alcohol.[15]

Silver is paranoid that her teammates will steal her bounties.[16][17]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Silver has an unnamed ex-partner who accused her of pushing people away.[18]

Silver once got kicked out of the Baroness Hotel during brunch.[19][20]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Shiv

[edit | edit source]

Silver loathes Shiv with a passion and refuses to believe he could change from his criminal past.[21][22] She believes he deserves a fate worse than death.[23]

How Silver and Shiv met each other and why Silver hates Shiv is currently unknown.

An unfinished conversation with  Grey Talon hints at Silver in disbelief that Grey Talon would support Shiv.[24]

### Abrams

[edit | edit source]

Silver is old friends with Abrams, referring to him as "Abe".[25]

According to Silver, they used to make "bad decisions" before Abrams became "boring".[26]

### Infernus and Hank

[edit | edit source]

As a heavy drinker, Silver frequents Jezebel's and is friends with Hank and Infernus.[27][28]

Silver refers to Infernus as "Fern".[29]

### Vyper

[edit | edit source]

Silver has hunted and caught Vyper so many times that Vyper's use of  Petrifying Bola comes from Silver's  Entangling Bola.[30][31]

### Mo & Krill

[edit | edit source]

Mo and Krill have worked with Silver in the past and have a good working relationship with her.[32]

While on the other team, they express concern over "how desperate" Silver has gotten and wish they could've helped her.[33]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Silver plays in Wraith's weekly poker games.[34]
- Silver is implied to have been hunting Drifter for a while and hates him.[35][36] Silver is also after a bounty on Calico.[37]
- Silver and Venator get along with each other, planning to go drink whiskey together after the ritual.[38][39]
- Celeste offers to have a drink with Silver after the ritual.[40]
- According to Rem, Silver's hair smells like Bourbon.[41]

“

Time for some misdirection.

**Sinclair** are Heroes in *Deadlock*. With their trusty magic wand, they can shoot unpredictable Bolts to surprise enemies and use magic to turn them into Rabbits. The Spectral Assistant amplifies their damage and can serve as a fast escape route. Sinclair can even turn their enemies' abilities against themselves with their surprising final trick, Audience Participation.

Henry and Savannah were two young stage magicians in love, who bound their souls to each other for eternity. However, their relationship was strained after a tragic on-stage accident claimed both of their lives. Now, under the shared title of Sinclair, they seek a way to be separated and find peace in the afterlife.

Sinclair was added to Hero Labs (as **Magician**) on October 24, 2024, and officially released on January 17, 2025 (as **THE MAGNIFICENT SINCLAIR**).

### Audience Participation

AUDIENCE PARTICIPATION

**20**m

**85**s

Copy the Ultimate of an enemy hero for a limited time. Reactivating the ability will use the Copied Ultimate instead.

Copies will inherit this ability's upgrade points.
Audience Participation will also copy the cooldown.

**1**

Notes

- The "**Upgrade**" effect determines what Tier level the copied ultimate will be. (The ultimate that is copied will be restricted to however many upgrade Tiers Sinclair has unlocked.)
- Sinclair has a 1s delay to use the target ultimate after copying.
- Sinclair can use Audience Participation even if the target enemy hasn't unlocked their ultimate yet.
- If  Spectral Assistant is active, Sinclair can use the teleport ability while copying an ultimate, besides the following exceptions:

- Dynamo's  Singularity
- Haze's  Bullet Dance
- McGinnis'  Heavy Barrage
- Mo & Krill's  Combo
- Rem's  Naptime
- Seven's  Storm Cloud
- Warden's  Last Stand (while channeling)
- If Sinclair copies an ultimate but does not use it, Audience Participation uses its default cooldown of 85s (with the exception of  Vindicta's  Assassinate).
- Imbuing  Compress Cooldown on Audience Participation does not reduce the copied cooldown, only the default cooldown. However, other sources of cooldown reduction do reduce the copied cooldown.
- Sinclair only copies the properties of the ultimate, which can make it weaker compared to the original hero. For example, when copying  Haze's  Bullet Dance, they will deal less damage due to their lower fire rate and lack of the Fixation passive ability.
- Sinclair gets permanent bonus health from kills or assists with  Mo & Krill's  Combo, permanent bonus spirit power from kills with  Grey Talon's  Guided Owl, and Bonus Weapon Damage from kills with  Vindicta's  Assassinate.
- Audience Participation has instant cooldown if Sinclair kills an enemy with  Shiv's  Killing Blow T3.
- If Sinclair copies  Vindicta's  Assassinate, they start with one less charge.
- Sinclair gets  Shiv's Rage passive if they copy  Killing Blow, dealing bonus damage when at full Rage. The Rage lasts until Sinclair either loses Killing Blow or Rage goes down to zero. However, if Sinclair copies Killing Blow again, they will still have the remaining built-up Rage from the last copy, allowing them to reach full Rage faster.
- If Sinclair copies  Silver's  Lycan Curse, they can transform instantly with no build-up. However, likely due to a bug, Sinclair will not gain the upgrades for two specific  Silver (Transformed) abilities if their base counterparts are currently deployed: a deployed  Vexing Bolt results in an un-upgraded  Go For The Throat, and a deployed  Spectral Assistant results in an un-upgraded  Mauling Leap.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Sinclair/Lore** for more story content.*

“

Henry's parents told him he was too young and impulsive to mess with real magic, and so they gave him a deck of cards to play with.  He took to sleight of hand naturally and soon was dazzling his classmates with fantastic feats of illusions that were done without mystic artifacts or incantation.

When he was in high school he met Savannah, and their mutual love of stage magic sparked a whirlwind romance.  Soon they fell in love and created an act together.  Obviously they were meant to be; and so at prom, Henry proposed to Savannah and they married soon after graduation.

Unsurprisingly both sets of parents were not thrilled at this prospect, but Henry and Savannah knew they were soulmates.  And so they cemented their love for one another by having a blood mystic bind their souls for eternity.

When an on-stage accident claimed both their lives, no one was sure who to blame.  Henry claims Savannah was out of position.  Savannah says Henry didn't wait for his cue.  But one thing's for sure, since their souls are tied to each other neither one of them have been able to move on.  Now a bickering pair of ghosts, Henry and Savannah need to work together if they want to have any chance of undoing their eternal union.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Sinclair changes voices on death, depending on which ghost is controlling the body. It starts as Henry's voice, then changes to Savannah's when Henry dies and vice-versa.
- Sinclair's weapon name **The Prestige** is a possible reference to the Christopher Priest's novel of the same name (which was adapted to movie by Christopher and Jonathan Nolan in 2006).

- The weapon was previously named **Legerdemain** and **Magic Wand**.
- Sinclair's current design is based on one of the scrapped designs for  Wraith. It is also used in a Metal Skin advert.
- Sinclair's lead developer is Hopoo,[3] best known as the co-creator of the *Risk of Rain* series.
- The Spectral Assistant currently uses a modified version of  Lady Geist's original model prior to the Six Heroes update.
- Sinclair's bunny uses the same model as Arnabus the Fairy Rabbit from *Dota 2*.
- Savannah's voice actor, Andia Winslow, also plays the role of Allie Kinkaid in Holliday's visual novel.
- "Working Magic in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Sinclair in the Hideout.
- When copying  Yamato's  Shadow Transformation, the description shows "Become infused with Sinclair's shadow soul." instead of 'Become infused with Yamato's shadow soul."
- If a hero has a voice line warning against a specific enemy ultimate, that voice line is triggered if the enemy Sinclair copies and uses that ultimate.

Henry's parents told him he was too young and impulsive to mess with real magic, and so they gave him a deck of cards to play with.  He took to sleight of hand naturally and soon was dazzling his classmates with fantastic feats of illusions that were done without mystic artifacts or incantation.

When he was in high school he met Savannah, and their mutual love of stage magic sparked a whirlwind romance.  Soon they fell in love and created an act together.  Obviously they were meant to be; and so at prom, Henry proposed to Savannah and they married soon after graduation.

Unsurprisingly both sets of parents were not thrilled at this prospect, but Henry and Savannah knew they were soulmates.  And so they cemented their love for one another by having a blood mystic bind their souls for eternity.

When an on-stage accident claimed both their lives, no one was sure who to blame.  Henry claims Savannah was out of position.  Savannah says Henry didn't wait for his cue.  But one thing's for sure, since their souls are tied to each other neither one of them have been able to move on.  Now a bickering pair of ghosts, Henry and Savannah need to work together if they want to have any chance of undoing their eternal union.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

"Sinclair" is implied to be Henry and Savannah's surname.[1] Their stage names are *Henry the Magnificent* and *The Spectacular Savannah.*[2][3]

Henry and Savannah both inhabit the same body. During the Ritual, the body is initially controlled by Henry, then changes to Savannah once Henry dies, and vice-versa. This body is implied to be a wooden mannequin or automaton, rather than an actual organic body that Sinclair is possessing, since their footsteps sound like clanging wood and mechanical whirring while walking or using certain abilities. The character who isn't controlling the body plays the  Spectral Assistant (though the Assistant currently only has a female model).

Both Henry and Savannah have to agree on who's controlling the body before the ritual.[4]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Henry and Savannah hate each other.[5] When calling upon their partner as a Spectral Assistant, they say it's "just like old times".[6]

Both Henry and Savannah believe they are "the responsible one".[7][8]

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Various heroes complain about being turned into a rabbit by Sinclair.[9]
- Although their conversation is incomplete, it's implied in  Holliday's interaction with Sinclair that she relates to them due to having had a divorce before.[10][11]
- Krill says Sinclair's stage show was "incredible".[12]
- Seven says he prefers his fate to Sinclair's.[13]
- Celeste thinks both Sinclairs deserve each other.[14]
- The Shopkeeper tells the Sinclairs that they need counseling, and a gun.[15]

# Sinner's Sacrifice

Sinner's Sacrifice in-game

**Sinner's Sacrifice** machines are  breakable objects in the map that may be broken using a  melee attack to earn  **** Souls and other rewards.

## Contents

- 1 Locations
- 2 Behavior

- 2.1 Interacting with the machine
- 2.2 Jackpot
- 3 Rewards

- 3.1 Souls
- 3.2 Buffs
- 4 Update history
- 5 Trivia

## Locations

[edit | edit source]

There are a total of 10 Sinner's Sacrifice locations and 3 types of sites on the map.

- 6 sites of the machine by itself
- 2 "hybrid" camps of 1 machine and 2 Medium Denizens
- 2 "hybrid" camps of 2 machines and 1 Medium Denizen

They spawn **8** minutes after game starts and respawn **5** minutes after being broken (solo) or fully cleared ("hybrid").

Sites are shown on the map with a  icon (a rectangle with a circle within it). It should be noted that the icon represents the site and not the Sinner's Sacrifice machine. The icon of a "hybrid" camp will not disappear from the map after breaking the machine but instead when fully cleared.

## Behavior

[edit | edit source]

### Interacting with the machine

[edit | edit source]

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Vault_music.mp3Music that plays on loop from the Sinner's Sacrifice

Each machine has 500 health and can only be damaged by melee attacks. A light melee deals 50 damage, and a heavy melee deals 100 damage.

The machine retaliates against attackers by dealing 80 damage back per a melee hit with the total retaliation damage to a hero being 320-640 depending on the mixture weights of melee strikes: Primarily eight light melee strikes 8 x 80 = 640 retaliation damage vs. four heavy melee strikes 4 x 80 = 320 retaliation damage. There is virtually no time difference between light or heavy melee exclusivity, with the exception of  Billy, who has faster light melee recovery and thus can hit jackpot faster than with heavy melees.

Abilities that deal melee damage, such as  Viscous'  Puddle Punch or  Calico's  Leaping Slash, will not affect the machine.

The machine's health is indicated by the lightbulbs at the top of the machine: The first melee attack will cause all the lights to turn on and further hits will cause them to turn off from right to left. A light melee will turn off one bulb per hit and a heavy melee turns off two bulbs.

Note:  Pocket with  Barrage stacks can deal more damage per hit to the Sinner's. This is likely a bug.

### Jackpot

[edit | edit source]

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Vault_music_hit_05.mp3Jackpot fanfare music
Ideal jackpot timing for a heavy melee last hit

After being reduced to one or zero bulbs (400 damage taken), the Sinner's Sacrifice will enter a looping **3**-second timing minigame. The lights will begin turning on from left to right accompanied by a count of 8 sound effects.

Hitting the machine within the final **1.3**-second window when all the bulbs are on will cause a "Jackpot," represented by the last hit dealing 100 damage regardless of melee type, fanfare playing, and the slot rolls landing on three red eyes. If the Jackpot timing is missed, the player receives the same soul reward as a regular final hit.

Retaliation damage is deactivated during this state.

## Rewards

[edit | edit source]

### Souls

[edit | edit source]

Each Sinner's Sacrifice internally holds a total bounty value that increases over the course of a match. This value starts at  **310** and grows by  **3.35** per minute from the beginning of the match.

The table below shows its approximate total worth at key intervals.

| Time in Match (min) | Total Souls Worth |
| --- | --- |
| 8 (Initial Spawn) | **336** |
| 10 | **343** |
| 15 | **360** |
| 20 | **376** |
| 25 | **393** |
| 30 | **410** |
| 35 | **427** |
| 40 | **443** |
| 45 | **460** |
| 50 | **477** |

This total value is distributed in Unsecured Souls with each hit:

- A **light melee** grants the total value divided by 20, rounded.
- A **heavy melee** grants the total value divided by 10, rounded.
- The **final hit** grants the total value divided by 2 (rounded), plus one heavy melee payout.
- A **Jackpot** adds 1 bonus soul to the final hit payout.

The payout is intended to grant half of its souls from melee attacks and the other half when destroyed. However, due to rounding on each hit, the total souls granted may be slightly more or less than the internal value shown above.

If multiple people hit the machine, subsequent melee attacks will attempt to evenly distribute the payout to everyone that has hit it. If there is a remainder after the division, the most recent attacker receives the extra soul.

### Buffs

[edit | edit source]

Successfully hitting the Jackpot provides the player with stacks of the Golden Statue buff.

- Hitting the jackpot with a **light melee** gives the player 1 buff.
- Hitting with a **heavy melee** gives 4 buffs.

To get the jackpot with a heavy melee last hit, the heavy melee needs to be charged before the 2nd-to-last lightbulb lights up.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- In *Neon Prime* and early *Deadlock,* Sinner's Sacrifices were originally designed as **Vaults**, and didn't have the jackpot mechanic.
- Their current minimap icon is still based on the **Vaults**, being depicted as a rectangle with a circle in the middle.

**Siphon Bullets** is a Tier 4  Vitality Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **6,400**.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Update history
- 3 Trivia
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

Shooting an enemy hero deals 2.5% max HP damage and applies the *Siphon Bullets* debuff, which reduces the target's max HP by the amount of damage dealt, and increases the user's max HP while healing them by the same amount.

The max HP steal lasts for 17 seconds (affected by Debuff Resist), refreshes on subsequent applications, and stacks infinitely. Stealing max HP from an enemy places the effect on a  1.2s cooldown (affected by Item Cooldown Reduction).

Each application will steal up to 2.5% max HP from afflicted targets, but the amount siphoned is reduced with falloff and the flat damage dealt may interact with certain passives.

- The damage dealt by Siphon Bullets cannot be increased or decreased by Bullet Resist, Spirit Resist, or damage amplification ( Pocket's  Barrage or  Escalating Exposure).
- Shiv's  Bloodletting passive will reduce the flat damage dealt by Siphon Bullets, but Shiv will still lose 2.5% max HP per application.
- The damage dealt by Siphon Bullets will still trigger  Abrams'  Infernal Resilience regeneration passive.
- The damage dealt by Siphon Bullets does not proc item effects.
- Siphon Bullets does not trigger if the initial bullet deals 0 damage.
- Siphon Bullets can not be applied on multiple targets by  Ricochet due to its 1.2s cooldown, only the initial target will receive the debuff.
- Due to the max HP steal being based on the *current* max HP, which decreases after each proc, the damage dealt decays exponentially, meaning subsequent applications deal less damage.
- Siphon Bullets' current and max HP increase for its user can proc Healing Tempo, but is not affected by healing reduction.

For each instance of max HP steal on an enemy, the user gains the same amount of max HP, equal to the stolen health. When an enemy has their max HP steal duration refreshed, the whole amount of max HP that was gained from that enemy also has its duration refreshed. If max HP has been gained from multiple enemies, refreshing the steal duration on one enemy will only refresh the duration of all max HP gained from that specific target, and the buff indicator will show the duration of the instance with the least time left.

- If an enemies steal duration expires, the enemy is healed by the same amount of the regained max HP.
- Stolen max HP can be regained by debuff removal, but this does not remove the gained max HP from the owner of Siphon Bullets.
- Selling Siphon Bullets does not remove the max HP steal from affected enemies.

Health gained from Siphon Bullets is visible on the user's healthbar to allies and enemies.

- Ally Siphon Bullets' gained health
- Enemy Siphon Bullets' gained health

# Skill Rating

In-game description of Skill Rating.

**Skill Rating** or **Skill Ranks** is a system in *Deadlock* that determines a player's matchmaking rating and hero-based rating.

It was added in the November 21, 2024 Update and replaced Ranked mode.

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Hero-Based Rating
- 1.2 Leaderboards
- 2 Skill Ratings

- 2.1 Initiate, Rating 1
- 2.2 Seeker, Rating 2
- 2.3 Alchemist, Rating 3
- 2.4 Arcanist, Rating 4
- 2.5 Ritualist, Rating 5
- 2.6 Emissary, Rating 6
- 2.7 Archon, Rating 7
- 2.8 Oracle, Rating 8
- 2.9 Phantom, Rating 9
- 2.10 Ascendant, Rating 10
- 2.11 Eternus, Rating 11
- 3 Update history

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Every player starts with the provisional rating of Obscurus. Once a player has played enough Normal mode matches, they will be assigned a new rating. Only Normal mode matches counts for skill rating. The rating is automatically updated based on the player's performance after every Normal match.

Matches in which a player has disconnected within the first 5 minutes do not count for skill rating.

A player's rating is less affected by "bad quality" matches with large skill disparity, and more affected by evenly balanced matches.

The player can enable an option in settings to see the average rating of each Team in a match in the post-game screen, as well as an option to be notified when their rating increases.

### Hero-Based Rating

[edit | edit source]

The Skill Rating tab also shows the player's hero-based rating, which represents their skill performance with each hero relative to their core rating. It is represented by one or two green upward arrows and one or two gray downward arrows. Green arrows and gray arrows indicate if the player's matchmaking rating with that hero is high or low relative to their core skill rating, respectively. Unplayed heroes start with two gray arrows.

### Leaderboards

[edit | edit source]

The Global leaderboard showcases the top 1,000 *Deadlock* players per region, as well as up to 3 of their highest-rated heroes. Hero leaderboards showcase the top 1.000 players of each hero available in Normal mode, per region.

A player needs to have played a minimum of 50 matches in the past 30 days to appear in the global leaderboard, and a minimum of 20 matches with a specific hero in the past 30 days to appear in that hero's leaderboard.

The leaderboard regions are North America, South America, Europe, Asia and Oceania.

# Sliding

| Sliding |  |
| --- | --- |
| https://deadlock.wiki/File:Sliding.mp4 |  |
| Tech Type: | Universal Tech |
| Difficulty: | Basic Mechanics |
| Character Dependent: | No |
| Stamina: | 0 |
| Inputs: | Crouch walk above 350 u/s or when on a ramp |

**Sliding** is a fundamental part of movement in **Deadlock**. Sliding allows you to gain momentum down slopes and to conserve already gained momentum to gain further distance. Sliding is only available while on the ground. While sliding, a blue trail (green if playing as  Vyper) will be emitted behind you, with small dust particles on your sides. One unique property of sliding is that *while sliding, you have infinite ammunition*; this is incredibly useful for combat and maximising DPSDamage per second[1].

Sliding takes no stamina to execute; you only have to be moving at a speed higher than 350 u/s (or 8.9 m/s) to initiate the slide. After executing the slide, you will eventually decelerate to a complete stop[2]. Cancelling the slide before you reach speeds slower than walking by releasing the duck button is advised.

Sliding for more than 0.75 seconds (or 1.00 second when Dash Jumping) applies increased friction[3]. This impacts your ability to maintain momentum. Items with the *+Slide Distance* statistic increase the time until the increased friction is applied by increments of +0.25 seconds.

To execute a slide, move above the required speed threshold (350 u/s or 8.9 m/s) or be moving at any speed on a ramp, and crouch. You should automatically slide.

## Contents

- 1 Items that Increase Slide Distance
- 2 Timings for Late Slide Friction Penalty
- 3 Slide Storage
- 4 Crouch Storage

#### Items that Increase Slide Distance

[edit | edit source]

Items with the *+Slide Distance* statistic increase the distance covered when sliding by delaying the friction penalty. Slide Distance does not increase speed.

#### Slide Storage

[edit | edit source]

**Slide Storage**Also known as Slide Conservation is the act of infinitely buffering a slide input for later use. This allows you to slide on objects and ramps instantly without minimal speed. Incredibly small parts of map geometry (e.g., curbs, lips of edges) that would be impossible to slide on normally can be slid on using Slide Storage.

Slide Storage allows you to buffer a slide input while in the air; this allows you to slide after any airborne action (e.g., dash jumping, jumping).

To execute, be airborne (through jumping, dash jumping, etc.) and then hold the crouch button. While the crouch button is held, your slide is being buffered. If you then move down a ramp, fall off a slope, or have enough speed, you will begin sliding.

#### Crouch Storage

[edit | edit source]

By applying the inverse principles of Slide Storage, one can instead trigger **Crouch Storage**Also known as Crouch Conservation. This allows you to stop on objects and ramps nearly instantly without sliding.

Crouch Storage allows you to hold a crouch while in the air; this allows you to stay crouching after any airborne action (with the exception of down dashing).

To execute, hold the crouch button before dashing or going airborne. While the crouch button is held, your crouch is stored. Now, no matter what surface you're on or what speed you're moving, you will never slide.

1. ↑ Very useful for conserving ammo during laning and necessary for bullet carry heroes for the whole game, such as  Haze,  Wraith and  Vyper
1. ↑ Sliding has a friction coefficient of 0.1875
1. ↑ The late slide friction penalty sets friction coefficient to around 3.1875 when sliding from a grounded dash, and 0.6875 when from a Dash Jump. Contibution by Altimor.

**Slowing Hex** is a Tier 2  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **1,600**.

It is a component of  Vortex Web.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Hero abilities silenced by Slowing Hex
- 3 Items silenced by Slowing Hex
- 4 Update history
- 5 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Slowing Hex sets a player's gravity to 120%, regardless of their base gravity. This especially affects  Celeste and  Ivy, who have innate gravity reduction.
- Slowing Hex does not disable passive effects such as  Vyper's  Slither.
- The Doorman's  Doorway and  Mo & Krill's  Burrow are *not* affected by Slowing Hex.

# Snowball

| Snowball |  |
| --- | --- |
| Cost | **0** |
| Tier | 0 |
| **Active** | 18 to 8s |
| Throw snowballs at your friends and enemies. Distance and other properties improve as you make progress in the 2025 Holiday Challenge.  Throwing a Snowball at an ally won't inflict damage and will reset its cooldown. |  |
| Codename: cosmetic_item_snowball |  |

**Snowball** was a seasonal Item in *Deadlock*.

Snowball was unlocked for all players during the 2025 Winter holiday event. It was a free colorless item that did not take an item slot and used a "Cosmetic" slot added during the event, appearing to the right of your active items.

Players could throw a Snowball that dealt Spirit Damage. It leveled up and increased in damage, velocity, radius, charges, projectile count and reduced cooldown as the player unlocked Christmas tree ornaments by winning matches with different heroes. Throwing a Snowball at an ally would reset its cooldown.

The Snowball level could be tested in the Hideout and Sandbox with the console command citadel_snowball_level_override + the level number.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

Despite dealing Spirit damage and being affected by Spirit Resistance, the Snowball did not proc effects based on Spirit damage.

When rebinding the Snowball in settings it is labeled under "Cosmetic 1", possibly hinting at the possibilities of other cosmetics or multiple cosmetics being enabled in the future.

Purchased items such as  Rapid Recharge and  Superior Cooldown did not have any effect on the Snowball.

# Soul Rebirth

“Farewell, my friends.”

This page contains game content that has been removed from the game.

| Soul Rebirth |  |
| --- | --- |
| Cost | **6,200** |
| Tier | 4 |
| +15s Increased Respawn Time |  |
| +12 Spirit Power |  |
| *Passive* | 240s |
| If you die, after 4s you will **respawn at your death location** with partial health. |  |
| Codename: upgrade_rebirth |  |

**Soul Rebirth** was a Tier 4 Vitality Item that provided Spirit Power to the purchasing hero and increased basic respawn time.

**Soul Rebirth** had a Passive component which would respawn the hero with 50% health at the location they died after 4 seconds; this effect had a cooldown of 180 seconds, which could be reduced with additional Cooldown Reduction.

On November 7, 2024, this item was removed from the game.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Update history
- 3 Gallery
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- When **Soul Rebirth**'s passive effect triggers, an animation is shown of the hero rising from their body before finally respawning.
- Killing a hero that has **Soul Rebirth** ready will still give kill credit and reward the instant souls, but the hero's corpse will not release additional soul orbs.
- Killing a hero that has **Soul Rebirth** ready will trigger on-kill effects, such as  Healbane's passive.

# Soul Urn

“

You'd think people would be more excited about a jar of souls!

— Soul Urn

The **Soul Urn**, also known as **Spirit Urn, Soul Jar** or **Spirit Jar**, is an objective that spawns at the 10-minute mark and respawns in 5-minute intervals.

Players can pick up the urn and deliver it to its destination on the opposite side of the map. Doing so grants the delivering team Soul Orbs, a Golden statue buff, and additional souls for the courier.

Soul Urn icon

## Carrying the soul urn

[edit | edit source]

After 10 minutes, the Soul Urn spawns in one of two locations in the outermost lanes: beside the overhanging bridge at York Street (Yellow Lane) or beside the bridge at Park Avenue (Green Lane). The urn always spawns first on Yellow Lane at 10 minutes and alternates lanes every 5 minutes. However, if the urn is picked up *before* the next spawn time and delivered *after* (i.e. picked up before 15 minutes and delivered after), it does not spawn again until the next scheduled spawn time. It descends from the sky for 12 seconds before it can be picked up. A player can grab the landed urn by standing near its pickup range for 2 seconds. Being melee'd or stunned while picking up the urn resets its pickup time, and the player cannot parry while picking it up.

While carrying the urn, the courier is affected in several ways:

- They get a Move Speed bonus of +3.5 m/s (capped at 15 m/s max), get their Sprint Speed disabled and have 100% Slow Resistance and 30% Bullet and Spirit Resist.
- They are disarmed, silenced, and cannot use active items.

- Channeled abilities and items started before picking up the urn, like  Ivy's  Air Drop and  Magic Carpet, are not interrupted. Abilities can still be activated for about half a second while picking up urn.  Viscous cannot carry as  Goo Ball.
- While Ivy can no longer pick up the urn while activating her ult, she can still fly allies who are carrying it, or pick the urn up during ult if she stays over it while flying. The latter can be achieved by dropping the urn inside a room with a low roof to fly inside.
- They are revealed to the enemy team at all times on the Minimap.
- They cannot use Ziplines or Teleporters.
- Going through  the Doorman's  Doors drops the urn at the entrance door.
- Rem and  Calico (during  Ava) cannot enter vents.

The courier can drop the urn at any time by pressing their parry key. A melee attack (light or heavy) or any stun from an enemy (including Troopers) will also force the courier to drop it. If the urn is left on the ground for too long, it will walk back to its spawn point.

**Note:** The Soul Urn's soul value is determined at the moment it spawns (e.g., 10:00, 15:00). Holding onto the urn for longer durations does not increase its value.

### Drop-off location

[edit | edit source]

The drop-off point is on the opposite side of the map, marked by a Soul Urn outline icon on the Minimap and colored red if an enemy player is currently carrying the urn. The urn is instantly turned in when the courier steps onto the drop-off (being in the air doesn't count).

If a team is behind by a certain soul threshold, the drop-off point moves closer to their side. This "favored" status is indicated by four floating green candles around the urn, and a green arrow over the urn pointing to the favored side in the minimap. For the leading team (drop-off on the enemy's side), the candles and minimap arrow are red.

The drop-off location is determined when an urn is first picked up by any player. Once determined, the drop-off point is fixed until the next urn spawn, even if the urn walks back to its spawn or the team soul difference changes.

### Anti-stalling mechanics

[edit | edit source]

To prevent one team from holding the urn for too long without delivering it, the urn begins to deal Pure Damage to its courier for 1.5% of their max health per second and disables their Health Regen after carrying it for 45 seconds. Furthermore, if the urn is dropped after that point the courier's entire team is prevented from picking up the urn again for 12 seconds. The 45-second timer pauses if the urn is dropped and resets if the enemy team picks it up.

## Soul urn reward

[edit | edit source]

The Soul Urn's base soul bounty is **1300 Souls** and increases by **230 Souls per minute** of game time. This value is "locked in" at the minute the Urn spawns.

- **10-minute Urn:** 3,600 Souls
- **20-minute Urn:** 5,900 Souls
- **30-minute Urn:** 8,200 Souls

When a team successfully turns in the Soul Urn:

- A random **Golden Statue buff** is granted to each member of the capturing team.
- 50% of the base value is distributed **instantly and equally** to all team members.
- 50% of the base value is spawned as contestable **Soul Orbs**.

### Courier's bonus

[edit | edit source]

The courier receives a personal bonus equal to **35% of their total share** (Base Share + Comeback Bonus). This bonus is awarded **instantly** upon delivery and cannot be denied by the enemy team. They also get 4 random Golden Statue buffs.

### The "Comeback" mechanic

[edit | edit source]

“If we are to complete the ritual, we must think clearly.”

This page may contain **factual inaccuracies**. The information presented requires verification against reliable sources.

Issue: *The math for comeback bounty may be inaccurate and needs more testing*

Green candles indicating favored drop-off on the player's side

If the capturing team is behind by **10% or more** (15% for the first urn), the Urn becomes a "Comeback," "Preferred," or "Favored" Urn. If this is the case, candles will appear around the urn after it has landed. In the case of one's own team being in a soul deficit, **green candles** will rotate around the urn. In the case that the enemy team is in a soul deficit, **red candles** will rotate around the urn.

This adds a **Comeback Bonus** to the reward:

- **Bonus Calculation:** The bonus scales based on game time and the team's soul deficit. It uses a growth rate of **130 Souls per minute**.
- **Approximate Formula:** Individual Bonus = 130 × Minutes × Deficit %
- **Safe Payout:** The entire Comeback Bonus is added to the **Instant Soul** pool.
- **Orbs:** The contestable Soul Orbs **do not increase** during a comeback; they remain fixed at 50% of the original base share.

**Note:** The first 3,000 souls of net worth difference are generally ignored when calculating the deficit, which may slightly dampen the bonus for smaller leads.

## Reward scenarios

[edit | edit source]

The following examples use the **10-minute Soul Urn** (Base Value: 3,600 Souls).

### Scenario 1: Standard delivery (Team is winning or even)

[edit | edit source]

- **Individual Base Share:** 600 Souls (3,600 ÷ 6)
- **Orbs per player:** 300 Souls (50% of share, deniable)
- **Instant per player:** 300 Souls (50% of share, guaranteed)

1. **Each Teammate receives:** 600 Souls total (300 instant + 300 from orbs)
1. **The Courier receives:** 810 Souls total (300 instant + 300 orbs + 210 courier bonus)

- The courier's 35% bonus is: 600 × 0.35 = 210 souls.

### Scenario 2: Comeback delivery (30% deficit)

[edit | edit source]

- **Individual Base Share:** 600 Souls
- **Comeback Bonus per player:** 130 × 10 × 0.30 = 390 Souls
- **Total Individual Share:** 990 Souls (600 base + 390 bonus)

1. **Each Teammate receives:** 990 Souls total (690 instant + 300 from orbs)

- Instant souls include 300 (base) + 390 (comeback).
1. **The Courier receives:** 1,337 Souls total (1,037 instant + 300 orbs)

- Courier bonus is: 990 × 0.35 = 346.5 souls.
- Instant souls include 300 (base) + 390 (comeback) + 346.5 (bonus).

## Lore

[edit | edit source]

Trapper builds Soul Urns for the New York Municipal Coven.[1]

The Urn is sentient and says its job is to keep New York clean by capturing rogue spirits, which should then be released in another location.

The Urn nags heroes to be delivered quickly and believes its work is underappreciated.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- In *Neon Prime*, the Urn was called the **Idol** and dropped off at the Center Temple, a location above the Mid-Boss.

# Souls

Soul released by the trooper.
Dark and light soul orb. Only light orbs can be claimed or denied

“

The more they die, the stronger I become!

— Graves

**Souls** are a crucial element in *Deadlock*, serving both as currency and experience points (XP) for heroes. Players collect souls by various means, including shooting **Soul Orbs** released when certain entities die, taking Guardians/Walkers, killing enemy players, and finding **Unsecured Souls** in boxes or crates. The amount of souls earned from a kill is a **Bounty**. Unsecured souls are added to your total immediately but can drop upon death for other players to collect.

Every player starts the game with  **600**.

## Contents

- 1 Soul Orbs

- 1.1 Local Soul Sharing
- 1.2 Soul Well
- 2 Gathering Souls

## Soul Orbs

[edit | edit source]

Troopers and the Soul Urn release souls in **Soul Orbs**. These orbs may be shot or hit with melee to confirm (or deny) the souls and grant them to the attacker. If they are not attacked, then the souls will be granted to the killer automatically after around 1 second. Certain abilities like  Serrated Knives or  Malice can also confirm or deny orbs.

Troopers drop two orbs on death, one that floats and one that falls on the ground. The floating orb has 40% of the kill bounty and the ground orb has 60%. The ground orb cannot be denied (they appear as white to enemies) and remains for a few seconds before disappearing (their duration increases over time).

The floating soul orbs spawn dark-colored, and can only be shot and confirmed once they light up. Ally orbs are green and enemy orbs are orange. Hitting an enemy orb will deny the souls to the killer and grant them to the player who hit it. If the orb "pops" without being claimed, it's automatically rewarded to nearby allies, and if there are no allies nearby the souls are lost. Orbs can be claimed by a single bullet or pellet, regardless of damage. The bullet that hit the orb is refunded to the player's magazine.

Soul confirmation accounts for latency, which in some situations can cause the player to lose the orb even if they visually seem to have hit it first. The ally team has confirm advantage.

Soul orbs can be divided into "local" and "global" types:

Local
Orbs spawned by killing Troopers grant souls to the player who confirmed them and any nearby allies.
Global
Orbs spawned by delivering theSoul Urn grant souls to the entire team of the player who claims them.

### Local Soul Sharing

[edit | edit source]

When souls are to be shared, the game checks two distances to add allied heroes to the "pool" of heroes to split the received souls:

- 45m from the soul orb itself when it is broken
- 30m from the hero that killed the Trooper

If an allied hero is within **either** of these distances, souls are shared between the killer and those allied heroes.

### Soul Well

[edit | edit source]

Inside each team's base, there is a soul well that releases orbs worth 10 souls each. Unlike regular orbs, these orbs only grant souls if they are confirmed, and they can be either green or orange-colored.

## Gathering Souls

[edit | edit source]

- Teams with fewer souls will gain more souls from all sources (see ***Comeback Mechanics*** below).

### Soul Distribution

[edit | edit source]

- Hero kill souls are distributed between nearby players with the following rate:

- 125%/57%/28%/17%/11%/8% (for 1/2/3/4/5/6 players)

- EX: 1000 souls between 4 players would grant each player 170 souls (1000 * 17%)
- Additionally, for kills with two or more players, the player who got the kill receives bonus souls.
- Trooper souls are distributed between nearby players with the following rate:

- 100%/54%/36%/25%/20%/16% (for 1/2/3/4/5/6 players)

- EX: 120 souls between 4 players would grant each player 30 souls (120 * 25%)

- When a Trooper is killed, 60% of the Trooper's souls drop as a ground orb that flies to allies within 18m and remains on the ground for 18 seconds (scaling to 40 seconds after 10 minutes), while the remaining 40% fly out as a deniable soul orb that enemies can shoot. Both orbs use Soul distribution among nearby allies; enemy ground orbs are visible but cannot be claimed. Killing the Trooper with a melee attack grants 100% of the souls instantly, distributed among nearby allies.

### Denizens (Jungle Creeps)

[edit | edit source]

- Jungle camps contain Denizens that give souls to players on kill. They do not release soul orbs.

- In order for Denizens to give souls to both players, both players must deal damage to the Denizen.
- Souls from Denizens are split between all allied players who dealt damage to said Denizens.
- Souls from Denizens are **unsecured** souls.

### Sinner's Sacrifices

[edit | edit source]

- Some jungle camps contain one or two Sinner's Sacrifice machines, which grants souls to the player by hitting them with melee attacks. Those souls are unsecured.

### Breakables

[edit | edit source]

- Breaking the wooden crates scattered throughout the map will have a chance to spawn some souls.

- Chance for any given crate to drop souls when broken is approximately 60%
- Amount of souls dropped is a function of in-game time:

- *[Souls Dropped] = 23 + 2.0*[Game Time in Minutes]*
- For example: At 30:00 game time, a broken crate will drop 83 souls.

### Other

[edit | edit source]

- Trophy Collector is an item that gives the player passive souls per minute.

- Killing cockroaches in underground tunnels grants the player 1 soul each.

## Unsecured Souls

[edit | edit source]

Unsecured souls icon

Souls earned from killing Denizens and destroying Sinner's Sacrifice machines are **unsecured** and are lost on death. If a player dies with at least 150 unsecured souls they will be dropped in a **Soul Container**, which can be claimed by any player by hitting it with a Heavy Melee. Soul Containers will despawn after 3 minutes. These containers are marked with a circle icon on the Minimap and have a green glow effect. If a player dies with fewer than 150 unsecured souls, no Soul Container will drop—they are permanently lost.

Unsecured souls are converted into secured souls over time, meaning they will no longer be dropped on death. This conversion rate is dynamic:

- **Percentage Drain:** Each second, **0.5%** of the player's *current* unsecured souls are converted. This means larger amounts of unsecured souls secure faster initially.
- **Base Drain:** In addition to the percentage, a flat amount is secured every second. This starts at **1.6 souls/second** and increases as the match progresses (scaling with the global bounty growth of ~8% per minute).

- **Example at 10 Minutes:** A player carrying **1,000 unsecured souls** will secure them at a rate of roughly **7.9 souls/second** (5 from percentage + ~2.9 base).
- **Example at 20 Minutes:** That same player carrying **1,000 unsecured souls** will secure them faster, at a rate of roughly **9.2 souls/second** (5 from percentage + ~4.2 base), due to the base rate scaling over time.

Souls UI for Heroes

Unsecured souls may be spent in the shop, but are spent *after* secured souls. They are indicated by the silver-green ball on the Hero's hip known internally as a Soul Container, as well as in the number on the HUD with a red icon.

Unsecured souls count towards leveling up. However, if the player dies and loses those souls, they will remain at the last unlocked level but lose progress to the next level equivalent to their dropped souls.

On the character UI, the large souls number is the **total** number of secured and unsecured souls added together.

## Leveling Up

[edit | edit source]

Gathering souls will gradually "level up" your hero, granting a variety of benefits. See boons for detailed information.

## Soul Values

[edit | edit source]

- **Soul Value:** Value of the target at the time = 0m
- **Soul Gain:** How the value changes over the time of the match, measured in minutes

* Soul gain from Urns is divided among the team. The Courier gets slightly more souls.

** Soul gain from structures is split with 40% given to nearby allied heroes, while 60% is divided amongst the entire team.

### First Blood bonus

[edit | edit source]

- A player gets 150 bonus souls on their first kill.

### Comeback Mechanics

[edit | edit source]

When a team is behind on souls, there are some "comeback mechanics" that come into play to allow the losing team to quickly catch up.

- Killing an enemy hero will award more souls if that hero is stronger than the killer team's average networth, regardless of which team is leading in souls.
- The Soul Urn will give additional souls to the team that is behind based on game duration and total soul deficit. (see Soul Urn for details)
- The losing team gains up to 30% more souls from Troopers, Denizens, Sinner's Sacrifices and Objectives, based on how behind they are (peaks at 20% max net worth difference). The first 3k in net worth difference is ignored. (This means that the first 3k souls should be subtracted when calculating comeback values, e.g. 100k to 105k is calculated as a 2k difference)
- After 10 minutes in a match, killing a player whose net worth is above 15% higher than the killer team's average net worth increases that player's respawn time. The increase varies based on the net worth difference and match duration, from +6s for 15% net worth at 10 minutes to +22s for 30% net worth at 25 minutes.

### Catch up Mechanics

[edit | edit source]

Catch up mechanics allow for players with low net worth to catch up to the other players on their team.

- The two players per team with the lowest net worth have a passive gain of souls per second based on the total souls per second gathered by the team (2.5% and 1.5% for the lowest and second-lowest player, respectively). This occurs after laning phase (8 min).

- For example, if a team gathered 200 souls in the last second, the lowest player earns 5 extra souls.

# Spirit Armor

“Farewell, my friends.”

This page contains game content that has been removed from the game.

| Spirit Armor |  |
| --- | --- |

| Tier | 2 |
| +22% Spirit Resist |  |
| +5 Spirit Power |  |

**Spirit Armor** was a Tier 2 Vitality Item that provided Spirit Resist and Spirit Power to the purchasing hero.

Spirit Armor was a component of Improved Spirit Armor before it was removed. Improved Spirit Armor was renamed to Spirit Resilience.

It was able to be bought for  **1,250** from the Shop.

# Spirit Damage

“Let's get started, shall we?”

This article is a stub. You can help the Deadlock Wiki by expanding it.

**Spirit Damage** is a form of damage dealt by some abilities and items. It is modifiable by obtaining Spirit Power, and scales with the respective ability or item's Spirit Scaling. Certain items will deal additional Spirit Damage if a condition is met.

Load video

YouTube

YouTube might collect personal data. Privacy Policy

Dismiss

Video explaining Spirit Damage

## NPCs

[edit | edit source]

Attacks from Walkers, Shrines and Patrons deal Spirit Damage.

## Sources

[edit | edit source]

There are several items that deal Spirit Damage, but called in a different name or applied in a specific manner. (Not a comprehensive list)

- Alchemical Fire deals increasing Spirit Damage per second in an area.
- Mystic Shot makes the player's bullet deal 40 *x*1 Spirit Damage every 8 seconds.
- Tesla Bullets deals 33 *x*0.19 Shock Damage on hit and on jump.
- Torment Pulse deals 25 *x*0.23 Pulse Damage every 1.4s (scaling with Spirit Power).
- Toxic Bullets deals 1.7% *x*0.005 Bleed Damage based on current health per second.

See also Spirit Power for a list of items that grant Spirit Power and abilities that scale Spirit Damage.

# Spirit Power

**Spirit Power** is a stat that increases the effectiveness of abilities and items. In addition to increasing Spirit Damage, Spirit Power can also increase miscellaneous ability attributes that are not otherwise broadly covered by spirit stats. Spirit Power is generally useful on all heroes, but some will benefit much more than others due to better scaling coefficients.

## Contents

- 1 Spirit Power Scaling
- 2 Spirit Scaling by Hero
- 3 Sources

- 3.1 Map spawns

## Spirit Power Scaling

[edit | edit source]

The upward trending purple arrow and spirit star indicate this damage is increased by spirit power.

When an ability or item can be scaled by spirit power it will be indicated with a purple upward trending arrow and the spirit star icon. The effectiveness of spirit power on a given ability is based on its spirit power coefficient shown after the spirit scaling icon e.g. *x*0.5. Using that spirit power coefficient, spirit damage can be represented with the formula:

𝑆𝑝𝑖𝑟𝑖𝑡𝐷𝑎𝑚𝑎𝑔𝑒=𝐵𝑎𝑠𝑒𝐷𝑎𝑚𝑎𝑔𝑒+(𝑆𝑝𝑖𝑟𝑖𝑡𝑃𝑜𝑤𝑒𝑟*𝑆𝑝𝑖𝑟𝑖𝑡𝑃𝑜𝑤𝑒𝑟𝐶𝑜𝑒𝑓𝑓𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑛𝑡)

For example,  Lash's  Flog ability deals 65 base damage and has a spirit power coefficient of *x*0.8. In a case where it was being buffed by 20 **spirit power**, the calculation would be as follows:

𝑆𝑝𝑖𝑟𝑖𝑡𝐷𝑎𝑚𝑎𝑔𝑒=65+(20*0.8)=81

The same principle applies to items. For instance, Tesla Bullets deals 33 base damage with a coefficient of *x*0.19. If you have 76 spirit power, its damage becomes:

𝑆𝑝𝑖𝑟𝑖𝑡𝐷𝑎𝑚𝑎𝑔𝑒=33+(76*0.19)=47.44

In general this represents linear scaling, with the rate of increase being determined by the spirit power coefficient. In most cases, the spirit power coefficient can be obtained by hovering over the skill while pressing the Extra Info hotkey.

**WARNING**: Obtaining exact calculations can be difficult because the spirit scaling values are *rounded to the nearest tenth*. This can lead to inaccurate calculations when trying to apply the above formula. In general, it is possible to obtain good approximations of spirit power's affect on damage but exact calculations often require sandbox testing to obtain the un-rounded scaling values.

[edit | edit source]

**Spirit Rend** is a Tier 3  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**. Its component,  Spirit Shredder Bullets, makes up  **1,600** of the cost.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Update history
- 3 Trivia
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- All stacks are refreshed with each new stack.
- Spirit Rend's second passive's resist reduction stacks additively with each stack, however, the final sum stacks multiplicatively with the base resist reduction from the first passive.
- Getting a headshot with  Ricochet will not apply stacks to the secondary targets, but will still apply the non-stacking debuff.
- As with  Spirit Shredder Bullets, the primary passive debuffs can be applied by melee attacks and abilities that deal melee damage.

## Update history

[edit | edit source]

*View the full update history: **Spirit Rend/Update history***

| Update | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| April 30, 2026 | - Lifesteal reduced from 12% to 10%. |
| March 6, 2026 | - Cooldown reduced from 2.2s to 2s - Spirit Lifesteal increased from 8% to 12% |
| October 2, 2025 | - Debuff duration increased from 7s to 8s. - Cooldown reduced from 2.5s to 2.25s. |

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- This item was previously named **Spellslinger Headshots**.

- This item can't be bought on  Graves, as she is incapable of targeting heads.

**Spirit Shredder Bullets** is a Tier 2  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **1,600**.

It is a component of  Spirit Rend.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Update history
- 3 Trivia
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- The Spirit Lifesteal from the debuff is independent of the diminishing returns from other sources of spirit lifesteal. It will always grant the player a flat +10% spirit lifesteal.
- The debuff can be applied with melee attacks, as well as abilities that are considered melee attacks.

**Spiritual Overflow** is a Tier 4  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **6,400**.

## Buildup Per Shot

[edit | edit source]

The item has a different buildup per shot depending on which hero purchased the item. The Overflow status only triggers once a buildup reaches 100% on an enemy player, and the buildup decays back to 0 if an enemy hasn't been shot for some time. Melee attacks count as 1 shot.

Once Overflowing, subsequent shots do not buildup or trigger another Overflow until the current Overflow expires.

**Split Shot** is a Tier 2  Weapon Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **1,600**.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Notable interactions
- 3 Update history
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Multishots can hit units as well, but they do not grant stacks.
- Each shot is separated by approximately 5°, leading to a total of approximately 20° spread between the furthest two shots.

## Notable interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Like  Armor Piercing Rounds, Split Shot's bullets can penetrate  Kelvin's  Frozen Shelter and  McGinnis'  Spectral Wall. This effect is probably unintended.
- For  Celeste, it splits into 3 shots at 70° spread.
- Split Shot affects  Grey Talon's  Rain of Arrows, allowing him to fire 25 arrows at once.
- Split Shot affects  Paradox's  Kinetic Carbine, allowing her to fire 5 Kinetic Carbine shots at once. However, it will only affect the first enemy hit.
- Paige and  The Doorman can gain stacks by hitting multiple players with the same shot.
- Split Shot has no effect on  Silver (Transformed).

# Stack

A **Stack** is a scaling effect or buff that can be increased through specific means or actions. Stacks are most often applied through dealing damage, where one instance applies one stack. Most stacking effects are built up quickly and are only temporary, disappearing all at once after their duration runs out. Additionally, there are stacking bonuses that apply directly to heroes, making them stronger, with a few of these bonuses sometimes being permanent. Only a handful of heroes can infinitely stack, allowing them to constantly scale as a game goes on.

While most stacking items effects are temporary,  Glass Cannon and  Restorative Locket are the only items to semi-permanently keep their stacks, and require certain conditions to lose them.

See Build-Up for abilities and items that trigger an effect after reaching 100% of a damage metric.
