# Stamina

Stamina is a stat that heroes start with and can obtain more through items. Stamina dictates the amount of dashes a hero can use. Stamina regenerates back over time, taking 5 seconds for most heroes without items to regenerate 1 bar.

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Stamina Bars

- 2.1 Cooldown
- 3 Dash Speed
- 4 Sources

- 4.1 Stamina
- 4.2 Stamina Recovery
- 4.3 Stamina Disable
- 4.4 Dash Distance Reduction
- 4.5 Map spawns

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Movement

A bar of stamina allows the player to perform several different maneuvers. In the following list, the Dash key by default refers to Shift, and Crouch key to Control:

- By pressing Dash and walking in a direction on the ground, the player can perform a basic Dash.
- By pressing Dash with a direction input in the air, the player will perform an Air Dash. The momentum during an Air Dash is affected by previous momentum, such as a left or right Air Dash with forward momentum would result in a diagonal trajectory. Only one Air Dash can be performed before touching the ground again.
- By pressing Jump while in a basic Dash, the player can perform a Dash Jump at the cost of a second bar of stamina in addition to the first bar for the dash. This will maintain the speed of the dash for longer while also providing significant height. This does have a specific timing that is allowed, close to about 2/3 of the way through the initial dash, and if performed incorrectly, the player will be locked out of it for the remainder of the Dash and not allowed to attempt it again.
- By pressing Jump while in midair, the player can perform an Air Jump/Double Jump. This can be combined with the Dash Jump to cover large amounts of ground very quickly, at the total cost of three stamina for the combination.
- By double tapping Crouch in midair, the player can perform an Down dash, descending quickly.
- By pressing Crouch in the middle of a basic Dash, you can perform a Dash Slide, which will start slowing momentum, but will grant unlimited ammo for the duration, and notably allow the player to cancel out of a Dash if you needed to act quicker than the Dash animation would normally allow. This is useful for things such as repositioning for last hits with melee in lane. The slide will continue as long as the player has momentum, so slopes will extend it or shorten it depending on orientation.
- Doing a Wall Jump does not cost Stamina while successive Wall Jumps cost 0.5 Stamina.

## Stamina Bars

[edit | edit source]

Heroes start with 2 to 4 stamina bars, and can increase it with items or abilities.

## Dash Speed

[edit | edit source]

**Dash Speed** is a stat that determines how fast a hero performs a dash. These are also commonly referred to as **Dash Buckets**, in which the fastest Dash heroes are in "bucket 1" and the slowest ones are in "bucket 3".

All dashes cover the same distance  (10m for ground dashes, 8m for air dashes), but take different durations. Ground dashes are slower than air dashes, but cover more distance. The "Dash Speed" stat uses the ground dash speed.

# Status Effects

*See also Crowd Control for a list of all Crowd Control effects.*

**Status Effects** are modifiers or effects applied to units or players after certain conditions have been met. Buffs are positive status effects, while debuffs are negative. They will last for a set duration unless cleared through certain items or abilities. Status effects can be displayed over an entity's health bar, as a transparent overlay on the entity's body, or not displayed at all.

[edit | edit source]

## Hero Specific Effects

[edit | edit source]

The following Status Effects are either exclusively relevant to or only applied by a specific Hero.

Affliction

### Affliction

[edit | edit source]

A negative status effect applied by  Pocket's  Affliction ability. It deals constant damage over time for a long duration, however it is non-lethal and cannot reduce a target's health below 1. It also does not apply item procs.

Eternal Night

### Eternal Night

[edit | edit source]

A negative status effect applied by  Drifter's ability of the same name. Inflicted heroes have their vision severely limited.

Fixation

### Fixation

[edit | edit source]

A negative status effect that increases the target's damage received from  Haze. It is unique to her, applied through her ability of the same name.

Hotel Guest

### Hotel Guest

[edit | edit source]

A negative status effect applied by  The Doorman's ability of the same name. The target is sent to the Baroness Hotel and has to make their way to the elevator to escape.

Lethal Venom

### Lethal Venom

[edit | edit source]

A negative status effect applied exclusively by  Vyper's ability of the same name. After a short delay, it deals Spirit Damage to the target. The max damage depends on the target's missing health.

Malice

### Malice

[edit | edit source]

A negative status effect applied exclusively by  Lady Geist's ability of the same name. It inflicts a decaying Movement Slow on the target and increases the amount of damage Lady Geist deals to them. It can be stacked up to 5 times and refreshed.

Petrified

### Petrified

[edit | edit source]

A negative status effect applied by  Vyper's  Petrifying Bola. Inflicted heroes are interrupted, unable to move and perform actions, but block all incoming damage, with the exception of  Vyper's  Lethal Venom (both the buildup and damage).

Rabbit Hex

### Rabbit Hex

[edit | edit source]

A negative status effect applied by  Sinclair's ability of the same name. Inflicted heroes change shape into a rabbit, with its corresponding hitbox, and move faster but have amplified received damage. The hero cannot perform any actions and abilities in rabbit form besides walking and jumping, but any actions and abilities initiated before the transformation are not interrupted.

Tether

### Tether

[edit | edit source]

A negative status effect applied by  Vindicta's  Stake ability. It binds all nearby targets to a central point, forcing them to stay within a short radius of the center.

Wrecked

### Wrecked

[edit | edit source]

A negative status effect applied by the passive of  Billy's  Blasted ability. Melee hits will inflict wrecked on enemies. When  Blasted is activated,  Billy will gain additional bullet damage against Wrecked enemies.

## Countering Debuffs

[edit | edit source]

Certain abilities and items can be used to mitigate or remove negative status effects.

### Temporary Buffs

[edit | edit source]

These effects grant a short-term immunity to certain debuffs. For a full list of sources, see the main entry for each buff.

- **Invincibility**: Grants temporary immunity to all damage and hostile effects.
- **Unstoppable**: Grants temporary immunity to crowd control effects.
- ** Indomitable**: Grants immunity to a single crowd control effect.

# Steve Jaros

**Steve Jaros** is a *Deadlock* developer. He is best known for his work as a writer on the *Saints Row* series, as well as on *Dota 2* and *Artifact*.[1][2]

Steve is *Deadlock's* lead writer.[3][4]

## Timeline

[edit | edit source]

The Deadlock timeline and time period are kept purposefully ambiguous, as the game is still in development and story aspects are subject to change. However, based on context clues such as references to the 1949 musical South Pacific[1][2][3][4] by various characters, it can be inferred that the game takes place circa the 1930s-1940s (see *Historical References* below). The buildings in the Cursed Apple use architectural references from New York City up to 1932.[5] Even so, there are visual references from later in the 20th century: Shiv's design is reminiscent of a 1950s Greaser, while Billy is inspired by 1970s Punks. The computer in the Hideout is similar to the 1973 Xerox Alto, one of the first personal computers, albeit with a typewriter keyboard.

The timeline below is based on mentioned in-game events and the Lady Geist visual novel. Events without a specific year use the date of the ritual as a reference point.

| Date | Events |
| --- | --- |

| 1692 | The Salem Witch Trials take place, leading to the killing of  Vindicta[8] |

| 1815 | Jeanne (Lady Geist) is born[9] |
| 1850 | Walter Geist is born[9] |
| 1880 | Johann Geist dies[9] |

The existence of the supernatural is revealed to humanity.[10]  Vindicta is brought back to Earth as a ghost,  Dynamo loses his body and becomes a dying star, and  Lady Geist makes a deal with Oathkeeper in exchange for eternal youth. |
| 42-45 years B.R. | The Baxter Society is founded[11] |
| 31 years B.R. | Dynamo marries Marla[12] |
| 23 years B.R. | Pocket is born[13] |

| 6 months B.R. | The Troubadour murders multiple people in Illinois and disappears[20] |
| Year of the ritual | Celestial Alignment, the second Maelstrom and the ritual take place |

# Strategy

“

What's the plan?

**Strategy** in *Deadlock* refers to the game knowledge and techniques employed by players to achieve the ultimate goal of destroying the enemy team's Patron.

## Contents

- 1 Team Composition
- 2 Laning
- 3 Objectives

- 3.1 Secondary Objectives
- 3.2 Pushing Lanes
- 4 Micro Strategies

- 4.1 Uptime
- 4.2 Positioning
- 4.3 Cover Usage
- 4.4 Map Knowledge
- 4.5 Rotations
- 4.6 Movement
- 4.7 Troop Management
- 4.8 Freezing a Lane
- 4.9 Counters
- 4.10 Soul Lead

- 4.10.1 Box Running
- 4.10.2 Jungling
- 4.10.3 Funneling

## Team Composition

[edit | edit source]

A **Team Composition** is the 6 heroes a team employs in battle.

Since Deadlock's matchmaking uses a semi-random roster selection, players are encouraged to learn different heroes and adapt to the needs of their teams instead of fitting into rigid roles. Some heroes like  Ivy,  Rem and  Paige fit a support role since their abilities have strong synergies with teammates. Others like  Haze and  Infernus fit the carry role, and can have strong individual impact in a game by securing kills. However, most heroes have some flexibility to fit different playstyles as needed.

## Laning

[edit | edit source]

The mini-map in the bottom-right corner of *Deadlock's* HUD.

Laning is the process of managing the troopers on a lane and destroying objectives along it. At the start of each round, players are assigned to three lanes according to a 2-2-2 setup, with two players in each lane.

Support-centric characters like  Paige or  Dynamo typically perform best when paired with a high-DPS counterpart with sustain or poke abilities, like  Shiv.

**Laning** is strategically divided into three phases:

- **Laning Phase (Early game)**: Players focus on winning their lane by managing troops, clearing Denizen camps, looking for easy kills, and gaining a Soul advantage.
- **Midgame**: Players who have secured an advantage in their lane begin roaming to assist teammates, while all players continue farming objectives to strengthen their team’s position.
- **Endgame**: Teams work to solidify their Soul advantage, engage in most of the teamfights, and push to attack the enemy Patron.

## Objectives

[edit | edit source]

Taking down Objectives is crucial to unlocking Extra Slots, gaining more Souls for the entire team and earning control of the map, thus gaining a tactical advantage over the enemy.

It's important to find the opportunity to unlock Extra Slots as soon as possible. For example, if one Guardian is down at the end of Laning Phase, it's usually more advantageous to help that lane's Troopers reach the Walkers, as taking down a Walker awards an Extra Slot.

### Secondary Objectives

[edit | edit source]

The Soul Urn and the Mid-Boss are secondary objectives that aren't necessary to win the game, but can give a strong boost to the team who secures them, either to hold an advantage or to turn the tide in their favor. They can also be used to bait the enemy team into a fight and leave their main Objectives unprotected for a short time.

### Pushing Lanes

[edit | edit source]

Lanes are pushed by killing enemy troopers and objectives. The length of the lane (seen in the zipline and minimap) is based on the progress of the last trooper wave. A lane can only be pushed as far as the closest enemy objective. At the start of the game, the enemy and allied lanes are frozen at the midpoint until one of the Lane Guardians are destroyed. Attacking a Walker or a Base Guardian without pushing their lane first gives them backdoor protection, in which they take much less damage and can regenerate damage taken.

## Micro Strategies

[edit | edit source]

### Uptime

[edit | edit source]

**Uptime** is the amount of time you spend actively contributing to something in a match, usually by creating pressure against the enemy team or collecting Souls for your team. Time spent farming Denizens, harassing enemies, and pushing troopers towards enemy Guardians and Walkers contributes to **uptime**, as opposed to "downtime" which can include time spent respawning, idly waiting for objectives to spawn, and rotating aimlessly around the map.

### Positioning

[edit | edit source]

Managing your **positioning** will allow you to control more space on the map, be effective in teamfights, deny enemy pushes, and utilize your Hero's abilities most effectively. Controlling more area of the map increases the viable farming area for both Denizens and enemy Troopers for your team. **Positioning** in teamfights or in smaller skirmishes is critical; staying safe but active in the fight will allow you to apply pressure to the enemy while removing the opportunity for them to gain an advantage by killing you.

### Cover Usage

[edit | edit source]

Like any shooter, using corners and walls allows you to be covered against almost all skills and items, since most of them require Line of Sight to be activated or cause damage. Heroes will lean around cover when close to the cover's vertical edge, exposing their head hitbox.

At present, the third person camera is locked to each Hero's right shoulder, which means that peeking on the right side of cover will always expose you less than the left side. Using this to your advantage in the laning phase will give you a significant advantage when trading weapon damage.

### Map Knowledge

[edit | edit source]

Knowledge of the Map's layout helps with maximizing uptime, positioning, rotations, and other crucial aspects in greater strategies throughout the game. This includes, but is not limited to, knowing Cosmic Veil locations, Powerup locations, and Teleporter locations.

### Rotations

[edit | edit source]

The process of traversing one part of the map to enter another. **Rotation** can be related to concepts such as ganking or roaming. Ganking refere to the art of appearing from the jungle to surprise - and potentially kill - enemies, while **rotations** are more broad and are related to creating space in different lanes and related concepts.

### Movement

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Movement

The process of moving and positioning your Hero. Involves Ziplines and Stamina usage in addition to sliding.

### Troop Management

[edit | edit source]

The process of killing enemy Troopers and **denying** the enemy from getting Souls from their Trooper kills. Can also be referred to as Creep Management.

**Creep/Troop denial** is a crucial part of the game's laning phase and involves shooting the Souls of one's own trooper when they are killed. This prevents enemy laners from obtaining Soul Orbs by killing Troopers. Denying Souls is still effective after the laning phase, as Souls increase in value as the game continues. Denying Souls after the lane phase grants all Souls to the denier, which can be an effective way to individually gain more Souls if you are farming for an important item.

Pushing up lanes by killing enemy Troopers spreads your team's area of control and removes farmable space from the enemy. If your team is able to control more of the map by pushing up Troopers, friendly Ziplines will extend and allow Trooper reinforcements to help push Guardians and Walkers, further pressing your advantage.

### Freezing a Lane

[edit | edit source]

By carefully damaging enemy troopers to equalize the number of troopers on each team within a lane, it is possible to "freeze" a lane in place so that the troops neither advance nor fall back. By limiting your damage to the wave, it is possible to effectively keep it "frozen" indefinitely.

This tactic is useful to keep troops close to your Guardian or Walker for your own safety. By preventing your troops from pushing forward, you can stay within the safe zones of your defenses.

It is also useful for denying your opponent's access to farm due to the distance from their defenses. Since your guardian or walker is the point furthest from their guardian or walker, freezing a lane on your side of the map can make retreat difficult for your opponent.

The healing from the medic pack dropped by a medic trooper can heal your minions and change the balance of the wave state, inadvertently causing your wave to push and breaking the freeze. You can prevent this from happening by keeping your distance from your own wave as it dies and collecting the medic pack only after a few of the minions in your wave have died.

### Counters

[edit | edit source]

Using counter items is an important strategy to deal with strong enemies. Picking counters requires knowing the enemy's strengths and weaknesses and which items are the most effective against them. Active items are often a good choice. Here are some examples of counter items:

- Debuff Reducer,  Debuff Remover and  Divine Barrier are effective against heroes who rely on passive damage over time, such as Bebop, Infernus, Mirage, and others.

- These items are also useful against heroes who depend on stuns, sleep, and similar crowd-control effects, such as Haze, Mo & Krill, Seven, and others.

- Metal Skin,  Return Fire,  Battle Vest,  Weapon Shielding, and  Bullet Resilience are effective against heroes who deal high burst weapon damage, such as Haze and Vyper.

- Healbane,  Decay and  Toxic Bullets are effective against heroes with strong healing abilities, such as Abrams, Lady Geist, and Shiv.

- Slowing Hex is effective against heroes who rely on movement-based abilities, such as Vindicta, Grey Talon, Holliday, and others.

- Silence Wave and  Silencer are effective against heroes who rely on constant ability usage, as they apply a  **silence** effect to the target and reduce outgoing spirit damage respectively. This makes them strong counters to heroes such as Yamato, Pocket, and Lady Geist.

### Soul Lead

[edit | edit source]

Earning more souls than your opponent makes you and your team stronger and more likely to win. During the laning phase generating a soul lead over your opponent causes you to get your ultimate before your enemies which can then be used to snowball your advantage.

#### Box Running

[edit | edit source]

Box running refers to moving around the map in certain routes to collect souls and buffs from Crates and Golden Statues. Pushing the wave into the enemies' tower can give you time to box run and get back to lane without missing out on collecting souls from troopers.

#### Jungling

[edit | edit source]

"Jungling" or "farming" refers to clearing Denizen camps to earn more souls. Unlike some MOBAs, *Deadlock* doesn't have a dedicated Jungler role, but some heroes can clear camps faster than others. Some items such as  Cultist Sacrifice and  Ricochet also help players clear camps more efficiently.

Clearing a trooper wave is generally faster and rewards more souls than a Denizen camp, so it's recommended to clear camps in between trooper waves. The camp respawn timer only starts once all of its Denizens are dead, so players should clear the entire camp when possible to avoid stalling respawns (Sinner's Sacrifices must be cleared as well). Or alternatively, players can leave one or more Denizens alive in camps in enemy territory to stall its respawn.

When jungling, players need to be careful to avoid roaming assassin heroes who might steal their unsecured souls.

#### Funneling

[edit | edit source]

Funneling refers to when the collection of souls on a team is purposefully imbalanced so that a hero can earn more souls than the rest of their team. This is most relevant on carries who become strong with a soul lead. The simplest method of funneling is to have only one person collect the souls from a lane so that the souls aren't split between two players.

# Street Brawl

“

Only those who keep their wits about them will survive.

— Seven

**Street Brawl** is a fast-paced, 4v4, combat-focused game mode in *Deadlock*, offering a short game format designed for quick sessions. Street Brawl removes the standard soul economy entirely, placing players in a best-of-five series of skirmishes with the ability to obtain a fixed amount of items each round.

Before each round, players will be presented with three sets of three items to choose from. Players can choose to reroll one set of items each round. Players who queued for Street Brawl with the random hero option will be given an additional reroll for the first three rounds. Street Brawl has exclusive legendary items not available in standard matches. Additionally, both normal and legendary items can appear as "enhanced" versions, with improved numerical stats. If a player is presented with an item that normally builds into an item they have already chosen, they will be given another item of a lower tier as a bonus.

Having access to the same number of items reduces the likelihood of one particular player snowballing ahead of others, and players do not need to make decisions about what objectives to focus on. Each round, all abilities start ready to use, except for ultimate abilities, which start on a heavily reduced cooldown.

Street Brawl matches do not affect the player's matchmaking rating in standard mode.[1]

Street Brawl was added in the Old Gods, New Blood update.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

- **Team Size:** 4v4
- **Format:** Best-of-Five (First team to win 3 rounds wins the match). The team who takes down the Guardian wins the round. Once a team wins 2 rounds, the enemy Guardian is removed and their final objective is to take down a Walker.
- **Round Duration:** After 3 minutes a round goes in Overtime, during which troopers have increased health and respawn times are increased.
- **Ability Points:** Every player receives 6 ability points to spend in the 1st and 2nd rounds, 5 points in the 3rd and 4th rounds, and 10 points in the 5th round.
- **Boons:** Players start with 9 boons in the first round. The number of boons received increases to 16, 21, 27 and finally 34 in the following rounds.
- **Item Rolls:** While all heroes have a random chance to get any item, some items are weighted to be more likely to drop for specific heroes (see item drop rates per hero). Stronger items are more likely to drop in later rounds. Using a reroll will drop items of similar tier and rarity as the items in the current roll. Choosing the random hero option in character select allows the player to have an extra item reroll in the first 3 rounds. Item drops are mirrored between teams: if a player in one team gets an enhanced or legendary item drop, a player in the enemy team will get an equivalent item drop.

## Game Mode Specific Differences

[edit | edit source]

Street Brawl-specific balance changes are marked in the ability/item description in Street Brawl with a yellow circle icon.

### Heroes

[edit | edit source]

- Bebop:  Hyper Beam -5s duration
- Calico:  Return to Shadows cooldown reduced from 90s to 60s
- Celeste:  Shining Wonder max linger duration reduced by 30%
- Drifter:  Bloodscent Isolation Range reduced from 20m to 10m
- Dynamo:  Rejuvenating Aurora T3 reduced from 2.5% to 2%
- Dynamo:  Singularity max HP damage reduced from 1.5% to 1%
- Graves:  Jar of Dead charge cooldown increased from 13s to 16s
- Graves:  Borrowed Decree duration reduced by 30%
- Graves:  Borrowed Decree ghoul damage reduced by 30%
- Holliday:  Crackshot Spirit Scaling increased from 1.1 to 2.5
- Holliday:  Bounce Pad cooldown reduced by 20s
- Infernus:  Flame Dash range reduced by 15%
- Ivy:  Entangling Thorns range reduced by 15%
- Kelvin:  Frost Grenade range reduced by 15%
- Lady Geist:  Essence Bomb range reduced by 15%
- Lash:  Death Slam throw distance reduced by 30%
- Lash:  Ground Strike damage reduced by 10%
- McGinnis:  Mini Turret cooldown increased from 18s to 26s
- McGinnis:  Medicinal Specter regen reduced by 20%
- McGinnis:  Heavy Barrage duration reduced from 13s to 8s
- Mirage:  Traveler Cooldown reduced from 155s to 60s
- Paige:  Bookwyrm range reduced by 15%
- Paradox:  Pulse Grenade range reduced by 15%
- Seven:  Storm Cloud damage reduced by 25%
- Seven:  Lightning Ball range reduced by 15%
- Victor:  Aura of Suffering aura radius reduced by 2m
- Warden:  Last Stand healing reduced by 25%

### Items

[edit | edit source]

- Alchemical Fire: Damage reduced by 30%
- Cursed Relic: Duration reduced from 3.25s to 2.75s
- Golden Goose Egg: Disabled in this mode
- Mystic Expansion: Radius bonus reduced from +20% to +16%
- Greater Expansion: Radius bonus reduced from +30% to +25%

### NPCs

[edit | edit source]

Denizens do not spawn in Street Brawl.

Troopers spawn faster and have starting Spirit Resist and increased Spirit Resist during overtime, and deal more damage to structures.

Structures have faster and increased resist decay over time.

Guardians have Backdoor Protection.

### Other differences

[edit | edit source]

Players cannot pause in Street Brawl.

Healing in base is twice as fast as standard play.

There is no item limit. If a player gets more than 12 items, the older items are no longer visible in the UI but still equipped.

## Legendary Items

[edit | edit source]

There are **17** Legendary items exclusive to this mode.

### Weapon

[edit | edit source]

- Haunting Shot: Your next bullet deals additional Spirit Damage based on the enemy's current Health. This bullet is larger and pierces through enemies, applying a debuff which reduces the enemy's healing, movement speed, and damage outputs.

- Infinite Rounds: Your bullets have a chance to become unavoidable, piercing through enemies and ignoring their Bullet Resistance. You have infinite Ammo.

- Runed Gauntlets: Your next Melee pierces through parry. Landing a heavy melee reduces your existing Cooldowns.

### Vitality

[edit | edit source]

- Celestial Blessing: On use, applies a cleansing effect to your whole team, replenishing their health and stamina while increasing their movement speed.

- Cloak of Opportunity: Occasionally block the next debuff that would apply movement lock, stunned, immobilized, chained, or slept to you, instead granting a temporary barrier and movement speed, as well as a temporary Unstoppable effect.

- Electric Slippers: While sliding, evade bullets and gain increased fire rate while dealing periodic Spirit Damage to nearby enemies.

- Eternal Gift: Every 2 seconds, provides a random **permanent** stat buff to your hero, while also occasionally dramatically reducing your next respawn timer.

- Nullification Burst: On use, removes any positive buffs on nearby enemies while blocking them from using any stamina or healing for a short duration.

- Seraphim Wings: Massively reduces your gravity, granting you large amounts of damage amplification and damage reduction while airborne. Also passively grants improved air control and allows for an additional air dash or air jump before landing.

- Shadow Strike: Any stamina use causes you to become temporarily invisible. Dealing damage with a melee attack while invisible applies periodic spirit damage while stealing bullet and spirit resistances.

### Spirit

[edit | edit source]

- Frostbite Charm - Imbue an ability to grant it cooldown reduction and spirit power. When the imbued ability damages a target, it freezes them, dealing bonus spirit damage.

- Mystic Conduit - Passively provides a significant increase to ability range and cooldown reduction for self and nearby allies. Dealing high damage to an enemy Hero within a short period of time heals you and nearby allies.

- Mystical Piano - On use, strikes the target area after a short delay with a large piano, stunning and reducing the stamina of any enemies hit. For a short duration after the stun, enemies are dazed.

- Omnicharge Signet - Imbue an active non-ultimate ability to grant it charges. Already charge-based abilities gain even more charges.

- Prism Blast - On use, become untargetable and invincible for a short duration while damaging lasers rotate around you.

- Shrink Ray - On use, significantly reduces self or target ally hero's model size for a duration while granting significantly increased movement speed.

- Unstable Concoction - On use, grants massively increased movement speed, health, spirit power, and weapon damage for a short duration before you explode, instantly dying but also dealing large area damage based on your max health and stunning enemies.

## Strategy

[edit | edit source]

Since Troopers don't drop Souls in Street Brawl, players are less encouraged to hit them. However, pushing waves is still valuable to gain heal from Banner Troopers and pressure the enemy's objectives.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- If a player doesn't pick any item in the starting phase, the item select screen stays open during the match until an item is selected.
- Enhanced items can be acquired for testing with the command citadel_item_purchases_force_enhanced true with cheats enabled.
- Voice lines from the Patron's announcers imply that, unlike the Ritual, Street Brawl matches are played out multiple times.[2]
- Legendary items are labeled "Tier 5" and worth  **9,999**.

# Structures

Structures are the immobile objectives on the map that provide Souls and other benefits to the team that destroys them.

Each team must defend their own structures while attacking the enemy structures to expose and destroy the enemy Patron to win the game.

| Structure | Image | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Guardian |  | The first objective of the lane is the Guardian, who has a laser attack, a melee attack, and a slam attack. The slam attack does AoE damage to enemies near the Guardian. |
| Walker |  | The second objective of the lane is the Walker who has a laser attack, a Fireball Spray, and a slam.   A team will gain an Extra Slot for each opposing Walker they destroy. |
| Base Guardians |  | The third objective of the lane is two Base Guardians outside the enemy base. When both enemy Base Guardians are defeated in a lane, the zipline for allies in that lane becomes significantly faster. |
| Shrine |  | The fourth objective is the Shrines, which have a Curse attack. There are two shrines, one on each side of the base. They both need to be destroyed in order to weaken the Patron, allowing you to kill it and win the game. |

**Superior Cooldown** is a Tier 3  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**. Its component,  Compress Cooldown, makes up  **1,600** of the cost.

It is a component of  Transcendent Cooldown.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- When bought, Cooldown Reduction is applied retroactively to abilities already on cooldown.

- When sold, the cooldowns of abilities are proportionally increased.

- Because the cooldown refund when sold is based on the current cooldown, buying then selling this item in shop allows the player to accelerate their cooldowns proportional to the amount of time before it was refunded.

| +40% Ability Duration |  |
| Upgrades From:  Duration Extender |  |
| Codename: upgrade_imbued_duration_extender |  |

**Superior Duration** is a Tier 3  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**. Its component,  Duration Extender, makes up  **1,600** of the cost.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Ability Duration affects your ability, item, buff, and debuff durations, with some exceptions:

- Healing items such as  Healing Rite,  Healing Nova and  Rescue Beam cannot be increased, as they heal for a fixed value instead of per second.

**Tankbuster** is a Tier 3  Spirit Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **3,200**. Its component,  Mystic Burst, makes up  **800** of the cost.

## Contents

- 1 Notes
- 2 Update history
- 3 Trivia
- 4 Navigation

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Tankbuster is a Charge-Up item, so it's not affected by Cooldown Reduction.
- Tankbuster only goes on cooldown when it affects enemy heroes. It will not go on cooldown when you hit an NPC.
- Some forms of Spirit Amp applied by items count as separate damage instances and thus don't contribute to the single hit such as Escalating Exposure.
- When the target is hit with spirit damage, the damage value which is compared against the triggering threshold is the base damage value prior to any increases or decreases from damage amp, damage reduction, spirit resistance, and spirit resistance reduction.

- Damage amp and spirit resist reduction will not help you in achieving the damage threshold to trigger the passive.
- Damage reduction and the target's spirit resistance will not prevent the passive from triggering when it otherwise would.
- Interaction with spirit shields: The triggering of the additional damage is entirely unaffected by the target's barriers (or lack thereof).
- The additional damage, and the ability which triggered the additional damage, are applied to the target as separate instances of damage. The additional damage from Tankbuster is dealt after the original spell damage.

# Teams

“Let's get started, shall we?”

This article is a stub. You can help the Deadlock Wiki by expanding it.

In *Deadlock*, there are two opposing teams in the game, each consisting of 6 players. Each team serves either the Archmother or the Hidden King who seek to use the players to complete a ritual and fully realize their existence into the physical world.

In Standard, Street Brawl, and Bot matches, players cannot choose the team they fight for, as this is decided at the start of every match by the matchmaking engine. Between the two teams, each player will be playing a unique hero. On the contrary, Custom Matches will allow players to choose their own respective team and hero where they are not restricted to only having one of a specific hero in either team.

## In-game

[edit | edit source]

During a game, a player works with their team to take down objectives and ultimately destroy the enemy Patron, while defending their own. Each team will be accompanied with a Guardian, a Walker, and a pair of Base Guardians for each lane.

Players can identify the team they are in from the voice of their Patron and the surrounding design of their team's side of the map.

The Archmother has a feminine voice, in which its base is topped with multiple Owl Statues and is named 'Grand Central'. Its team covers the 'Uptown' side of the map which is characterized by its mostly white buildings, and featuring an Aggressive Bull Statue beside the base to the right.

Meanwhile, The Hidden King has a masculine voice and its base is named Penn Station.  Its team covers the 'Downtown' side of the map which instead is characterized by its mostly red buildings, and its Defensive Bear and Horned Gargoyle statue beside on the right and on top the base, respectively.

During a game, the player will view their friendly Patron and Troopers to be in light-greenish blue, while the enemy Patron and Troopers are in red.

## Heroes

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Heroes

Before players can join a game, they are required to pick at least three heroes. When new heroes are introduced in a patch, players must include at least two non-new characters in their roster. A Standard and Bot Match will have 12 different unique heroes between the two teams while a Street Brawl will only have 8 unique heroes between the two teams. Custom Matches may involve multiple of the same heroes within or between the teams, or with lesser than 12 players in total.

# Teleporter

An underground Teleporter
Teleporter locations
Teleporter logo as it appears on the Minimap
A side lane Teleporter (removed as of July 29, 2025)

**Teleporters** can be used to quickly traverse the map horizontally. There are currently 2 pairs of teleporters on the Map, next to the underground Secret Shops, which are available to use from the beginning of the match. Teleporters take four seconds to channel after entering the booth, and a Hero will gain a small speed boost after teleporting.

Teleporter locations appear on the Minimap as an icon of a person stepping through a portal, facing in the direction of the corresponding exit.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Soul Urn couriers cannot use teleporters or Ziplines when delivering the urn.

## Update history

[edit | edit source]

| Update | Changes |
| --- | --- |
| July 29, 2025 | - Removed the teleporters behind the Walkers |
| May 8, 2025 | - Teleporters now start available at the beginning of the game, rather than at 8 minutes. |
| April 4, 2025 | - Removed the outer lanes teleporters |
| October 10, 2024 | [General Changes]    - Fixed Debuff Reducer causing Teleporters to be faster - Fixed Shiv's Killing Blow continuing to do damage while being teleported by Quantum Entanglement    [Misc Gameplay]    - Teleporters open time changed from 10 min to 8 min - Teleporters now grant +3 m/s for 5s after arriving at the other side - Updated teleporter locations - Moved teleporters to travel between outer lane Walkers - Added teleporters in the underground tunnels - Changed underground teleporters to go between Subway and Tunnel on the same side of the map |

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The Teleporter's appearance is similar to the TARDIS from *Doctor Who,* which is a time machine disguised as a 1960s British police phone box.
- The Teleporter logo references the logo for Valve's *Portal 2*.

# The Archmother

Overview

Quotes

The Archmother

“

Glass, steel and stone... Order and power where once there was none... The Archmother has always guided the founders' hands, and now it is time for them to welcome her home.

— Old Gods, New Blood Update

**The Archmother** is a Patron, as well as the name of her Team. Her followers are **The Archmother's Disciples**. The Hidden King is her rival.

The Archmother's herald is voiced by Debra Wilson.[1]

## Contents

- 1 Overview
- 2 Gallery
- 3 Trivia
- 4 References

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

The Archmother wears a broken mask that resembles the head of the Statue of Liberty, her form bound to a crystalline effigy burning with blue flames. She's characterized by the color blue. Her base is a museum with a Neoclassic aesthetic. Her side of the map has upper-class white brick buildings and is labeled "Uptown".

The Archmother does not speak to the heroes directly. Instead, a herald speaks on her behalf.[2][3]

Akin to the Hidden King, the Archmother's goals are unknown. According to The Doorman, the Archmother has wanted to be summoned for "centuries".[4] Warden and his family believe the Patrons will "herald the end of humanity" if left unchecked.[5] It's implied that the Archmother wants to "usher in her new era".[6][7]

The Doorman refers to the Archmother as **City Mother**.[8] The bank behind Archmother's Yellow Walker is called "City Mother Bank".

The Hidden King's herald calls the Archmother a "tyrant".[9]

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- The Archmother was originally named **The Sapphire Flame** prior to the Old Gods, New Blood update. She also referred to herself as **Whisper in the Wind** and **Ambition's Spark** in an unused voice line.[10] This is referenced in a Warden unselect line.[11]

- A proposed rename to the Archmother was **The Guided Hand**.[12]
